job.title: Information Technology Manager - WPXI TV
job.description:
Location: PA-Pittsburgh

Job Title:  Information Technology Manager - WPXI TV

 

Position Overview

WPXI TV, a Cox Media Group (CMG) station in Pittsburgh, PA, is seeking an experienced, highly motivated I.T. Manager. Operating in the nation’s 26th largest television market, this hands-on leadership role manages the station's entire computing environment, localized server architecture, high-security network perimeters, and integrated broadcast-I.T. ecosystems.

 

The I.T. Manager ensures 24/7/365 operational continuity for our live news, production, and multi-platform digital channels. The ideal candidate will blend advanced systems administration with deep technical knowledge of specialized, automated broadcast television environments. This role reports directly to the Director of Engineering and works in tandem with the station's local engineering team and CMG corporate technology group.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Broadcast-I.T. Integration & Support: Maintain high-level technical oversight, provisioning, and daily troubleshooting for mission-critical newsroom and automation systems including Avid, iNews, Grass Valley Ignite, Harmonic, Crispin, Chyron, and Wide Orbit.
  • Infrastructure & Storage Management: Administer and optimize local storage and server environments, directly overseeing the station’s virtualized server platforms (VMware/Hyper-V) and high-capacity NetApp network-attached storage (NAS/SAN) infrastructure.
  • Network & Security Enforcement: Serve as the local gatekeeper for network security. Manage, patch, and monitor the station's Fortinet infrastructure (firewalls, switches, and secure access points), ensuring strict adherence to CMG corporate cybersecurity mandates.
  • Systems & Automation Administration: Direct the optimization of Microsoft enterprise environments, Active Directory, endpoint systems, and localized automated script pipelines to minimize operational overhead and drive reliability.
  • User Support Leadership: Manage the local help desk workflow, ensuring high-priority, zero-downtime technical support for live control rooms, field news crews, digital production teams, sales, and administrative staff.
  • Disaster Recovery & Redundancy: Formulate, test, and manage strict local business continuity blueprints, ensuring off-site cloud backups and local hardware redundancies preserve the on-air and digital stream integrity during critical weather or emergency events.

 

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Broadcast Engineering, or equivalent combined professional experience.
  •  5+ years of experience in systems administration, network engineering, or I.T. infrastructure management, with a proven track record working inside a high-pressure, live broadcast television or multi-platform media environment.
  • Technical Proficiencies:
    • Advanced administration of Microsoft Server, Active Directory, Group Policy, and desktop operating systems.
    • Strong knowledge of virtualization technologies (VMware Horizon/vSphere) and enterprise storage management (NetApp solutions).
    • Profound understanding of core networking concepts (TCP/IP, VLAN segmentation, routing protocols, and QoS settings for media over IP).
  • Must be willing to participate in an on-call emergency rotation encompassing nights, weekends, and holiday coverage to support a continuous news cycle.

job.title: Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Arts Criticism Internship
job.description:
Job Description:


Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Arts Criticism Internship 

Job Description:

The Wall Street Journal's Arts in Review section is seeking aspiring journalists—juniors, seniors or recent graduates (within one year of graduation) with a strong editing background at their school newspapers or elsewhere—for a 10-week paid summer internship. The in-person internship is an opportunity to get hands-on experience working alongside some of the best opinion writers and editors in the world.

The internship—formally the Bartley Fellowship—honors the Journal’s former Opinion editor, Robert L. Bartley. Opportunities will be awarded to individuals interested in the arts who intend to pursue a career in journalism or cultural criticism.

The Arts intern is one of several fellows selected each year through an application process that is overseen by senior editors. Bartley Fellows are assigned to a department within the Opinion section—Arts in Review; Books; or Features (Op-Eds and Columns). The fellow will assist in producing Arts in Review’s content for the print and digital editions of the Journal—editing, fact-checking, liaising with writers, writing display copy, proofing, contributing to social media and digital production. Though this is not a writing fellowship, the Bartley fellow will be encouraged to produce a Masterpiece column, of which more below. They may also pitch articles or projects to editors elsewhere in the Opinion section.

Internships are paid, and generally take place during June, July and August, though start dates can be flexible. 

If you are interested in applying for the Opinion, Books or Arts in Review Bartley Fellowships, please submit separate applications for each position.


About Arts in Review 


Arts criticism is recognized at the Journal as an Editorial Page function, and as such operates under the umbrella of the Opinion section. Like the rest of the Opinion section, in our Arts reviews we believe in rendering clear, independent judgments that are as well argued as they are deeply informed.

In its Arts reviews, the Journal covers the full spectrum, from high art to TV, movies, theater and the many forms of popular music. Our approach is strictly art-for-art’s-sake: We review things because they are intrinsically interesting, not to fulfill a quota or make a political statement. We believe in the past and its traditions, but are keenly interested in the new—not in novelty for its own sake but in the ways those traditions are being extended and new ones invented. And we prize above all a lively, lucid prose style free from jargon of all kinds.


Guidelines and Application Deadline

Though a reporting and/or writing background is a plus, the fellowship is primarily an editing internship. Therefore applicants should have experience editing arts or arts-related copy for their college newspaper, literary magazine, or a comparable publication. Students from any discipline may apply, but preference will be granted to those concentrating in literature, history, a foreign language, classics, pre-law, music, theater, art history, studio art, architecture, philosophy, political science or archaeology—via coursework (though not necessarily a major) or sustained leisure-time activity.

An appreciation for both the Western and non-Western canons is desirable, as is an understanding of current issues in the arts. A demonstrated ability to multitask and meet daily deadlines is critical for success, as is attention to detail and a focus on accuracy. Applicants should be familiar with technology as it relates to journalism. Social media experience with a publication or brand would be a plus.

Applicants will be expected to demonstrate familiarity with our section’s content (student applicants without campus-wide access to the WSJ can purchase discounted subscriptions at https://www.wsj.com/studentoffer).

If you’d like to be considered, please submit the following in one single, complete PDF file:

  • A cover letter
  • Your résumé
  • Full text of your two best clips
  • Your response to the following prompt in no more than 800 words: Write a “Masterpiece” column. In these essays that appear every Saturday, a writer discusses a single work of art (painting, book, film, etc.) and explains why, in their view, it is of surpassing cultural significance. (Examples: https://www.wsj.com/news/types/masterpiece)

All materials must be received by Nov. 30, 2026. Only complete applications that include a cover letter, résumé and responses to the prompt will be considered. Please do not include any additional materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, etc. In order to be considered, you must be a U.S. citizen, or a holder of a green card or visa that will allow you to work in the United States. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and we endeavor to make selections by the end of February. Only finalists will be contacted.


About Bob Bartley


Throughout his 30 years as The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Page Editor, Bob Bartley inspired principled and original thinking that changed and shaped the society in which we live. He also devoted attention to teaching and motivating talented young people, many of whom have gone on to careers in journalism at the Journal and elsewhere. The Bartley Fellowships are consistent with that legacy.

Bob Bartley achieved many honors during his long tenure here, including a Pulitzer Prize and, shortly before his death in December 2003, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In awarding that medal, President George W. Bush cited Bob as “one of the most influential journalists in American history.” The Robert L. Bartley Fellowships will help to perpetuate not only Bob’s memory but, above all, the principles and priorities to which he devoted his distinguished career.


About the Opinion Section


Following the American newspaper practice, the heads of News and Editorial report independently to the publisher of the Journal and CEO of Dow Jones, Almar Latour. The Editorial staff is responsible for the Opinion content published on WSJ.com, the editorial and op-ed pages of The Wall Street Journal in print, and criticism of books and the arts, which are recognized at the Journal as an Opinion function.

While The Wall Street Journal’s news pages are committed to informing our readers, our editorials are dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy and positions that emanate from it. That philosophy can be summed up as “free markets, free people.” We have stood for these fundamental principles even in times—and places—when they were not considered fashionable. While specific issues differ in various parts of the world, we view those issues through a consistent lens everywhere; for example, while protectionism is more popular in some parts of the world than others, our publications around the world are committed uncompromisingly to free trade.

We believe in the individual, in his wisdom and his decency. We oppose all infringements on individual rights, whether they stem from attempts at private monopoly, labor union monopoly or from an overgrowing government. Our section is not easily pigeonholed or predictable. We resist the label “conservative,” in the sense of preserving the status quo, because we think it too confining, too devoid of the optimism inherent in trusting individual wisdom and decency.

It is also important to state clearly what our section does not represent. It is not partisan. Unlike many American publishers, we do not endorse political candidates, and from time to time we have important disagreements with all leading political figures. We view issues through the lens of our philosophy and let our readers decide which person or party best serves to protect market capitalism and self-government.

We believe that the ultimate function of opinion journalism is the same as the rest of the newspaper: to inform. But in opinion journalism we have the additional purpose of making an argument for a point of view. We often take sides on the major issues of politics and society, with a goal of moving policies or events in what we think is the best direction for the country and the world. Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.



Equal Opportunity Employer


All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. EEO/Disabled/Vets

Reasonable Accommodation


We are committed to providing reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application and/or interview process. If you need assistance or accommodation in completing your application or participating in an interview due to a disability, email us at talentresourceteam@dowjones.com. Please put "Reasonable Accommodation" in the subject line and provide a brief description of the type of assistance you need. This inbox will not be monitored for application status updates.

job.title: Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Book Review Internship
job.description:
Job Description:


Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Book Review Internship


Job Description

The Wall Street Journal's Books section is seeking beginning journalists—juniors, seniors or recent graduates (within one year of graduation) with reporting and writing experience at their school newspapers or elsewhere—for a 10-week paid summer internship in our New York City office. The in-person internship is an opportunity to get hands-on experience working alongside some of the best opinion writers and editors in the world.  

The internship—formally the Bartley Fellowship—honors the Journal’s former Opinion editor, Robert L. Bartley. Opportunities will be awarded to young thinkers and writers who intend to pursue a career in journalism or cultural criticism.

The Books intern is one of several fellows selected each year through an application process that is overseen by senior editors. Bartley Fellows are assigned to a department within the Opinion section—Arts in Review; Books; or Features (Op-Eds and Columns). The fellow selected to work with the Books team will assist in commissioning reviews, conducting research, fact-checking and editing content for the print and digital editions, as well as contributing to social media and digital production. The fellow will be encouraged to submit ideas for book reviews and may also pitch articles or projects to editors elsewhere in the Opinion section.

Internships are paid and generally take place during June, July and August, though start dates can be flexible.

If you are interested in applying for the Opinion, Books or Arts in Review Bartley Fellowships, please submit separate applications for each position.


Guidelines and Application Deadline

Though a reporting and/or writing background is a plus, the fellowship is primarily an editing internship. Therefore applicants should have experience editing arts or arts-related copy for their college newspaper, literary magazine or a comparable publication. Students from any discipline may apply, but preference will be granted to those concentrating on literature, history, a foreign language, classics, pre-law, music, theater, art history, studio art, architecture, philosophy, political science or archaeology—via coursework (though not necessarily a major) or sustained leisure-time activity.

An appreciation for both the Western and non-Western canons is desirable, as is an understanding of current issues in the arts. A demonstrated ability to multitask and meet daily deadlines is critical for success, as is attention to detail and a focus on accuracy. Applicants should be familiar with technology as it relates to journalism. Social media experience with a publication or brand would be a plus.

Applicants who are able to demonstrate familiarity with our section’s content will be especially attractive (student applicants without campus-wide access to the WSJ can purchase discounted subscriptions at https://www.wsj.com/studentoffer).

If you’d like to be considered, please submit the following in one single, complete PDF file:

  • A cover letter
  • Your résumé
  • Links to or cited full text of your three best clips
  • Your response to the following prompt in no more than 800 words:  Make a case for any book of your choosing on history, fiction or nonfiction. (Examples: https://www.wsj.com/news/types/bookshelf)

All materials must be received by Nov. 30, 2026. Only complete applications that include a cover letter, résumé and responses to the prompt will be considered. Please do not include any additional materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, etc. In order to be considered, you must be a U.S. citizen, or a holder of a green card or visa that will allow you to work in the United States. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and we endeavor to make selections by the end of February. Only finalists will be contacted.

About Book Reviews at The Wall Street Journal

Books criticism is recognized at the Journal as an Editorial Page function, and as such operates under the umbrella of the Opinion section. Like the rest of the Opinion section, in our book reviews we believe in rendering clear, independent judgments that are as well argued as they are deeply informed.

The Journal’s book reviews are among the most timely, most widely read and most influential in American literary journalism. Our daily reviews appear in the Opinion section and focus on nonfiction books of interest to ambitious readers of politics, business, science, religion and the issues of the day. Our weekend reviews, which make up a six-page Books section in print, offer judicious criticism of the best of the week’s new titles in a broad cross section of subject areas, from the fine arts and literary fiction to popular culture, narrative nonfiction, children’s books and more. In all we do, our goal is simple: to cut through the noise to identify true excellence in publishing—and match it with excellence in reviewing.


About Bob Bartley

Throughout his 30 years as The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Page Editor, Bob Bartley inspired principled and original thinking that changed and shaped the society in which we live. He also devoted attention to teaching and motivating talented young people, many of whom have gone on to careers in journalism at the Journal and elsewhere. The Bartley Fellowships are consistent with that legacy.

Bob Bartley achieved many honors during his long tenure here, including a Pulitzer Prize and, shortly before his death in December 2003, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In awarding that medal, President George W. Bush cited Bob as “one of the most influential journalists in American history.” The Robert L. Bartley Fellowships will help to perpetuate not only Bob’s memory but, above all, the principles and priorities to which he devoted his distinguished career.

About the Opinion Section

Following the American newspaper practice, the heads of News and Editorial report independently to the publisher of the Journal and CEO of Dow Jones, Almar Latour. The Editorial staff is responsible for the Opinion content published on WSJ.com, the editorial and op-ed pages of The Wall Street Journal in print, and criticism of books and the arts, which are recognized at the Journal as an Opinion function.

While The Wall Street Journal’s news pages are committed to informing our readers, our editorials are dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy and positions that emanate from it. That philosophy can be summed up as “free markets, free people.” We have stood for these fundamental principles even in times—and places—when they were not considered fashionable. While specific issues differ in various parts of the world, we view those issues through a consistent lens everywhere; for example, while protectionism is more popular in some parts of the world than others, our publications around the world are committed uncompromisingly to free trade.

We believe in the individual, in his wisdom and his decency. We oppose all infringements on individual rights, whether they stem from attempts at private monopoly, labor union monopoly or from an overgrowing government. Our section is not easily pigeonholed or predictable. We resist the label “conservative,” in the sense of preserving the status quo, because we think it too confining, too devoid of the optimism inherent in trusting individual wisdom and decency.

It is also important to state clearly what our section does not represent. It is not partisan. Unlike many American publishers, we do not endorse political candidates, and from time to time we have important disagreements with all leading political figures. We view issues through the lens of our philosophy and let our readers decide which person or party best serves to protect market capitalism and self-government.

We believe that the ultimate function of opinion journalism is the same as the rest of the newspaper: to inform. But in opinion journalism we have the additional purpose of making an argument for a point of view. We often take sides on the major issues of politics and society, with a goal of moving policies or events in what we think is the best direction for the country and the world. Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.

As Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy's global chemicals price reporting business. You will oversee the editorial teams responsible for the assessment and publication of benchmark prices, assessments and market-moving news across global petrochemical and chemical markets from our PCW brand.

You ensure the integrity, quality, transparency, and market relevance of chemical price assessments while maintaining the highest ethical and methodological standards. You will lead a global team of price reporters and editors responsible for market coverage across key chemical value chains - including aromatics, olefins, plastics, polymers, syngas, methanol, feedstocks, and emerging chemical markets.

You will drive editorial excellence, benchmark innovation, and market engagement, while ensuring compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. You will partner closely with Product, Standards & Compliance, Risk, and other Editorial leaders to ensure Dow Jones Energy's chemicals assessments remain trusted, transparent, and indispensable to global commodity markets.

You will report to the SVP - Markets & Price Reporting.

About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.

Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.

You Will:

  • Lead and develop a global team of chemicals price reporters, editors, and market specialists, fostering a culture of editorial excellence, accountability, and collaboration

  • Ensure all chemical market assessments are developed, maintained, and published in accordance with the highest standards of price assessment integrity, market transparency, governance, and ethical conduct consistent with Dow Jones’ and The Wall Street Journal’s values

  • Lead methodology development, periodic methodology reviews, market consultations, and stakeholder engagement processes to ensure pricing methodologies remain robust, representative, and responsive to evolving market dynamics

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with producers, consumers, traders, brokers, exchanges, trade associations, and other market participants to strengthen market engagement, data integrity, and confidence in Dow Jones Energy's petrochemical and chemical markets assessments

  • Partner with Standards & Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable benchmark regulations, internal controls, audit requirements, and governance frameworks

  • Partner with Product to execute the strategic roadmap for global chemicals market coverage, including identifying opportunities for new benchmarks, market expansion, and portfolio optimization

  • Monitor benchmark performance, market adoption, customer feedback, and competitive developments - recommending changes to methodologies, coverage, and editorial priorities as appropriate

  • Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing editorial talent, ensuring appropriate succession planning, capability development, and organizational resilience across the chemicals price reporting organization

  • Act as a senior spokesperson and subject matter expert for chemicals markets, representing Dow Jones Energy at industry conferences, customer engagements, webinars, and regulatory forums

You Have:

  • 15+ years’ experience in commodity price reporting, market intelligence, or related information services organization

  • Deep knowledge of global chemicals and petrochemical markets, including physical market structures, trading practices, supply chains, and pricing mechanisms

  • Significant leadership experience managing geographically dispersed editorial, price reporting, or market analysis teams

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, or launching benchmark price assessments, methodologies, or market intelligence products

  • Strong understanding of IOSCO Principles for Oil Price Reporting Agencies and familiarity with benchmark regulation, governance, assurance, and audit requirements

  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to cultivate relationships with senior leaders and external market participants

  • A university degree -OR- relevant professional experience

job.title: Principal Product Designer - Market Data
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Designer - Market Data, you will own the design strategy for our Market Data platform—the real-time quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, and visualization systems that power how millions of people read and act on financial markets across The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and Investor's Business Daily. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who sets direction across our financial brands and is the go-to design expert for how Dow Jones presents market data.

Market Data connects across every one of our financial brands, and this role sets the design strategy that spans all of them. Your decisions will establish shared patterns—for quotes, charts, tables, portfolios, and alerts—that these brands build on. You will own the direction for how investors of every kind, from first-time savers to sophisticated professionals, interpret dense, fast-moving data and turn it into confident decisions, balancing the distinct needs of each brand against the consistency and quality users expect wherever they encounter our data.

And this reach won't stop at the consumer. Market and pricing data runs across much of Dow Jones—so your influence will extend well beyond the consumer brands into our professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Dow Jones Risk & Compliance to Dow Jones Energy, wherever market data underpins the experience. Where data meets the broader product, you will be the design lead who makes it cohere.

This is a role of real influence and scope. You will shape strategy with senior leadership, resolve tension between individual brand priorities and platform consistency, define the market-data patterns that live in our Index Design System, and mentor senior designers across the financial brands. You will be the design authority for your domain—navigating ambiguity and setting the standard others in your area build on.

You will report to the VP of Product Design within the Design & Research organization.

About the Team:

Our Design & Research org brings together world-class designers and researchers with a unified purpose: to connect people to the news and information that matters most. We're the strategic force that transforms deep user understanding into exceptional product experiences across our entire portfolio—from The Wall Street Journal to Factiva.

Our integrated approach ensures that research insights directly shape design decisions, while design explorations reveal new research opportunities. Together, we're building coherent, accessible experiences that honor our 135-year legacy while pushing us boldly into the future. We're a globally distributed team spearheading a digital transformation at Dow Jones, newly staffed by industry leaders from Google, LinkedIn, The New York Times, and more. Through our combined expertise in design craft and research rigor, we ensure that millions of users can depend on our platforms for truth in a world full of noise.

You Will:

  • Own the design strategy for the Market Data platform across our financial brands—setting a coherent, multi-year direction for quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, portfolios, and data visualization that spans The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and IBD, and connecting it to measurable outcomes like engagement, retention, and revenue

  • Shape strategy with senior leadership. Present your design direction for the Market Data platform to senior design, product, and business leaders—and to executives where the work warrants—building the partnerships that advance it across brands and making the case for how well-designed data experiences create competitive advantage

  • Solve the hard, ambiguous problems in your domain—developing new patterns, methods, and approaches for presenting complex financial information across multiple brands, and building a deep understanding of the problem space that lets you see opportunities ahead

  • Shape the market-data patterns in our Index Design System. Establish the charting, data-table, real-time, and visualization standards that become the norm across the financial brands—knowing when consistency serves the user and when a brand's audience warrants a tailored approach—and help adjacent teams adopt and evolve them

  • Extend your influence beyond our consumer brands into the wider portfolio—the professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Risk & Compliance to Newswires and OPIS, where market and pricing data is just as central—so the experiences built on our data share the same clarity, rigor, and craft. Be the design lead wherever data shapes the product

  • Set a high bar for craft. Define what excellence looks like for dense, real-time financial information—typography, information density, motion, and the accessibility of complex tables and charts—and ensure consistent quality across the brands through design reviews and audits

  • Connect design to outcomes. Partner with Research and analytics to tie your decisions to engagement, retention, and subscription metrics, and help teams across the financial brands understand which measures matter for market-data experiences

  • Mentor and grow senior designers across the financial brands, shape a strong design culture, and strengthen the talent pipeline through the standards you set and the craft you share

You Have:

  • 10+ years of product design experience, including significant time owning complex, systems-level or platform work, with a track record of setting design direction that spans multiple products or brands

  • Deep expertise designing data-rich experiences—financial data, analytics, dashboards, data visualization, or other complex information display—where clarity, density, and trust matter as much as visual polish

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strategic impact across multiple products or brands: platform or design-system contributions, cross-team pattern-setting, and strong end-to-end craft on sophisticated products

  • A proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, translating design strategy into business terms and building alignment across teams whose priorities compete

  • Mastery of data visualization and information design—charting, tables, real-time data, progressive disclosure—and the judgment to know when complexity serves the user and when it gets in the way

  • Strong systems thinking and deep experience with design systems, including establishing patterns that other teams adopt and evolve

  • Excellence in Figma, with the ability to set standards for design communication, specifications, and documentation across teams

  • A deep command of design fundamentals and accessibility standards (WCAG), with particular fluency in making dense, complex data usable for everyone

  • A track record of mentoring designers and helping raise the craft and quality of the teams around you

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity—setting direction in your domain amid shifting priorities and emerging technology, and acting as the go-to expert others turn to

  • Bachelor's degree in Design, HCI, related field -OR- equivalent experience 

Nice to Have

  • Experience designing for financial services, investing, trading, or fintech products

  • Familiarity with real-time or streaming data systems and the constraints they place on design

  • Working knowledge of financial concepts—markets, instruments, portfolio construction—sufficient to partner deeply with domain experts

  • Background in news media, publishing, or other content-heavy products

  • Experience designing across a multi-brand portfolio

  • Experience contributing meaningfully to a design system

  • An external presence through speaking or writing on data visualization, information design, or design at scale

  • International or cross-cultural design experience

job.description:
Job Description:


Summer 2027 Internship – Brand Intern

Application Deadline: November 13, 2026
We encourage you to submit your application as early as possible, as internship applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

AMER Internship Dates: June 7, 2027 – August 13, 2027
(You must be available to work full-time, in-office during this period.)

About Our Internship Program:
Dow Jones Internship Program is a 10-week summer experience designed to give students real exposure to how . Our interns work on meaningful projects alongside our teams, gaining hands-on skills that make an impact on the business.

We believe the best way to learn is by doing — that’s why you’ll be paired with a mentor, connected with senior leaders, and included in professional development sessions. You’ll also join a diverse global intern community, sharing experiences and building networks that last beyond the program.
Our goal is to provide a supportive, engaging, and fun environment where your work feels valued and your growth comes first. Check out our Dow Jones Internship Program page to learn more and hear directly from past interns about their journeys. At Dow Jones, you’ll have the chance to start your career in an environment where collaboration, trust, and impact come first.

About the Role:
We’re seeking a Brand Design Intern to join our Marketing team. In this hands-on role, you’ll help create new brand identities and support cohesive design experiences across digital, print, and spatial touchpoints. You’ll work with senior designers on projects spanning multiple brands—including The Wall Street Journal, WSJ Events, MarketWatch, Barron’s, IBD, and other Dow Jones companies.

This role is ideal for someone resourceful, proactive, and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment. You’ll gain exposure to high-visibility projects while also rolling up your sleeves on the essential day-to-day tasks that keep brand systems running.

As a Brand Design Intern, you will:
Assist in creating new brand identities from the ground up (logos, color palettes, typography, art direction) and brand guides, moodboards, and toolkits to communicate with stakeholders, partners, and brand ambassadors.
Support senior designers on projects that deliver full brand experiences, including:
Visual concepts and mockups
Digital and media assets (emails, ads, landing pages, digital signage, social graphics campaign collateral, podcast art)
Print and spatial applications (event materials, invitations, onsite design recommendations)
Help build and maintain design systems (typography, composition, hierarchy, color theory, etc.) in Figma, including templates, guidelines, and scalable components.
Collaborate across teams to ensure design consistency across multiple channels and formats.
Conduct competitive research to spot trends, best practices, and opportunities for brand differentiation.
Translate research findings into clear insights that guide creative strategy.

You Have:
Currently pursuing a degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or a related field.
Strong knowledge of digital design principles and fundamentals;
Proficiency in Figma (or practical tools such as Sketch, Adobe Creative Suite).
Strong attention to detail and the ability to produce polished, professional work.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with shifting priorities.
Resourceful, self-driven, and proactive—able to ask the right questions and seek solutions independently.
Open to feedback and eager to learn.
Some knowledge of UI/UX, animation, or print is a plus, but not required.

Program Eligibility:  
Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program
Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)  
Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying.

job.title: Digital Content Producer
job.description:
Overview

Job Title: Digital Content Producer

 

Department: Digital 

 

Reporting To: Brand Manager

 

Employment Type: Part Time

 

Work Arrangement: On-site

 

Job Description:

 

1010 WINS is looking for a digital journalist with strong news judgment, sharp social instincts and a passion for visual storytelling. This role will focus on turning breaking news, reporter content and broadcast material into engaging digital content for Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, LinkedIn, Snapchat, Threads and X. The ideal candidate understands how people consume news on social media, can quickly identify the strongest angle in a story, and knows how to make content feel native to each platform while maintaining high journalistic standards.

The anticipated starting salary range for New York-based individuals expressing interest in this position is $20.00/Hr.-$25.00/Hr. 

Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities and location of the applicant, as well as internal and external equity.

Audacy offers full time employees with a comprehensive benefits package to include:  health care coordinator, medical, dental, vision, telemedicine, flexible spending accounts, health savings account, disability, life insurance, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, paid time off (sick, vacation, personal, parental, volunteer), 401(k) retirement plan, discounted employee stock purchase, student loan payment assistance program, legal assistance, life assistance program, identity theft protection, discounted home and auto insurance, and pet insurance.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do:

  • Produce short-form videos, graphics, photos and infographics from broadcast reports, reporter assets and breaking news, primarily using Canva
  • Monitor broadcast rundowns, AP Newsroom, Bloomberg, press releases, social media and other news sources to identify strong local, national, political and trending stories
  • Work closely with digital producers, broadcast editors, anchors and field reporters to gather video, photos, audio and other assets
  • Source additional visual material from Getty, AP Newsroom, Citizen, Bloomberg and other approved third-party sources
  • Verify content and ensure all material meets station editorial standards, copyright requirements and media licensing rules
  • Write sharp, engaging social copy and headlines tailored to each platform
  • Publish and schedule content using Sprinklr across Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Snapchat and Threads
  • Apply accurate photo, video and source credits
  • Respond quickly to breaking news and changing newsroom priorities
  • Identify opportunities to turn reporter coverage into stronger social and digital content
  • Write and publish web stories when appropriate, including content supporting newsletters and other digital initiatives
  • Contribute ideas for recurring social franchises, original video and new ways to grow audience and engagement

Qualifications

 

More About You:

 

Desired Characteristics:

 

  • Experience using Canva for social video and graphics
  • Experience with Sprinklr or similar social publishing tools
  • Familiarity with AP Newsroom, Bloomberg, Getty, Citizen and other newsroom content sources
  • Experience working in a broadcast, digital or breaking-news newsroom
  • Understanding of social media analytics and how performance can help guide editorial decisions
  • Experience publishing stories in a digital content management system
  • Strong instinct for trending, visual and highly shareable stories
  • Willingness to experiment with new formats and platforms
  • Genuine interest in how younger audiences discover and consume news
  • Curiosity, creativity and a desire to help build something that is still evolving

 

 

Required & Preferred:

 

Qualifications:

 

  • Strong news judgment and a commitment to accuracy, verification and journalistic standards
  • Experience creating short-form video and visual content for platforms including TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts
  • Strong writing and copywriting skills, including the ability to quickly identify the strongest hook in a story
  • A strong understanding of major social platforms and what works on each one
  • Ability to work quickly and calmly in a fast-paced breaking-news environment
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills
  • Knowledge of New York City, the Tri-State area, major national news, politics, culture and current events
  • Understanding of copyright, asset licensing and proper attribution
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with a larger newsroom
  • Availability to work evenings, weekends and holidays as required

 

Important Notes:

Please be aware that Audacy will never ask you to send money at any point during the hiring process. Communication from legitimate Audacy representatives will only come from email addresses ending in @audacy.com. If you receive any suspicious requests or communications, please verify their authenticity before responding.

About Us

Audacy is a leading audio content and entertainment company. As champions of audio, we connect with people in the moments that matter — delivering trusted local news, passionate sports and your favorite music across 220+ radio stations, premium podcasts, live events and digital experiences that reach more than 200 million listeners every month.We create compelling content, foster deeply engaged audiences and deliver outcomes that matter for advertisers. Learn more at www.audacyinc.com and join the conversation on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Location: NC-Charlotte

Job Title:  Anchor/Reporter - WSOC TV

 

Position Overview

WSOC-TV Charlotte is looking for an enterprising and energetic Anchor/Reporter. This anchor/reporter will join a newsroom that emphasizes breaking news, daily investigative reporting and severe weather coverage. They must dig for extra information. They must also be adept at using social media to gather and break stories. This position requires a newsroom leader who can confidently anchor weekend newscasts while also producing impactful, original reporting during the week. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Anchor live Saturday and Sunday newscasts with authority, credibility and strong storytelling
  • Lead breaking news and severe weather overage during weekend broadcasts
  • Collaborate with producers, reporters, meteorologists and newsroom leaders to shape editorial content and presentation
  • Write news stories that are clear, accurate and unbiased
  • Ability to narrate, ad-lib and add value to live breaking news and severe weather coverage
  • Ability to cover live events for all platforms, including live breaking news and station initiatives
  • The ability to engage in investigative reporting that adds depth to the newscast
  • Thorough understanding of social media and demonstrated ability to move audience between all platforms
  • Curiosity that drives an understanding of current events
  • Demonstrate consistently high proficiency with the necessary technical, writing, and presentation skills for television broadcasts

Minimum Qualifications

  • Must have a valid driver's license and clean driving record

Preferred Qualifications

  • BA Degree in Journalism, Communications, or other discipline preferred
  • 5 years’ experience as a Reporter required; anchoring experience strongly preferred

About Cox Media Group 

CMG Media Corporation (d/b/a Cox Media Group) is an industry-leading media company with unparalleled brands, award-winning content, and exceptional team members. CMG provides valuable local and national journalism and entertainment content to the people and communities it serves. The company's businesses encompass 17 high-quality, market-leading television brands in 9 markets; 45 top-performing radio stations delivering multiple genres of content in 9 markets; and numerous streaming and digital platforms. CMG's TV portfolio includes multiple primary affiliates of ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, Telemundo and MyNetworkTV, as well as several valuable news and independent stations. For more information about CMG, visit www.coxmediagroup.com

The audio revolution is here – and iHeart is leading it!  iHeartMedia, the number one audio company in America, reaches 90% of Americans every month -- a monthly audience that’s twice the size of any other audio company – almost three times the size of the largest TV network – and almost 4 times the size of the largest ad-supported music streaming service. 

Because we reach almost every community in America, we’re committed to providing a range of programming that reflects the diversity of the many communities we serve – and our company reflects that same kind of diversity.  Our company values stress collaboration, curiosity, welcoming dissent, accepting mistakes in the pursuit of new ideas, and respect for everyone.


Only one company in America has the #1 position in everything audio: iHeartMedia!


If you’re excited about this role but don’t feel your experience aligns perfectly with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.  At iHeartMedia we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace and are looking for teammates passionate about what we do!

                                                                             

What We Need:

Looking for a new challenge? Join us as an Account Executive and leverage your proven goal-driven mindset, fast-paced work ethic, and exceptional client service skills. The ideal candidate is ready to hit the ground running and will successfully take advantage of all iHeart’s platforms to exceed their clients’ expectations.

                                                                             

What You'll Do:

As an Account Executive at iHeart, you'll learn the ins and outs of our Broadcast + Digital Marketing Products, identify and develop new business opportunities through in-person meetings with clients and research, consistent daily cold-calling, and cultivate existing business using our full suite of products. You will collaborate with internal partners to drive revenue, create effective marketing campaigns, and use your storytelling skills to deliver compelling sales presentations fueled by data to best meet your clients’ expectations.   

                                                                             

What You'll Need:

  • You should be self-motivated (a very “go-getter” attitude!), have excellent relationship-building and problem-solving skills, and communicate persuasively. When people describe you, goal-oriented, expert negotiator and proactive should be at the top of the list.  
  • You should be able to plan and multi-task in a fast-paced environment.  
  • Comfortable with cold-calling and initiating outreach to prospective clients as part of lead generation efforts.
  • A valid driver's license, auto insurance, and a High School Diploma (College Degree preferred) are required.  
  • You should also be skilled in Salesforce, Microsoft Office and social networking platforms.  
  • Strong problem-solving skills; by exercising these skills, you help business grow to the fullest potential.
  • Digital/Media Sales experience are a plus but not required. 
  • The natural ability to organize and prioritize day-to-day depending on where the biggest priorities may be
  • Additional nice-to-haves include experience managing complex, multi-platform campaigns, analytics experience, iHeart and/or audio advertising background, and are well-connected in the market.  

What you’ll get  

  • You'll have the opportunity for uncapped commission, and the ability to grow business across all categories on a local, regional, and national level no matter where you live
  • A 7-week onboarding program to immerse you in the suite of tools and products available to you 
  • The potential to be recognized in our annual iHeartMedia CEO’s Club and iHeartMedia President’s Club programs 
  • Access to competitive benefits including paid vacation and sick time, paid company holidays, a Spirit day to encourage the opportunity to more easily volunteer in their communities, company-paid mental health and financial education resources, 401(k) matching, learning and development resources, and career navigation support.
  • Access to additional perks include pet (they’re part of the family!), disaster, and legal insurance, student loan refinancing, and discounts on merchandise, tickets to events, and more.
  • The support of fellow team members invested in your success.

Envision your first 30 days  

  • Week 1: Complete our onboarding journey for a deep understanding of our company, job-specific trainings and spend time with your team. 
  • Week 2: Spend more time with your manager to ensure you are aligned on work and communication styles, priorities, and any other expectations. 
  • Week 3: Start “owning” your role and leaning into the real day-to-day, of course with your manager’s support and advocacy! 
  • Week 4: Prioritize a 30-day check-in to see what else you might need to be most successful in your new role.  


 

Interested in learning more about iHeart and our platforms? Visit us at www.iHeartMedia.com to learn more about our company, www.iHeartRadio.com to access all your favorite music, radio, and podcasts, and download the free iHeartRadio app!

job.title: Senior Video Editor, Shows
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a Senior Video Editor who can help bring our shows portfolio to mobile, social and digital audiences through horizontal video podcasts and vertical video clips.

This is a post-production position to manage the editing of individual shows as well as clips. You have a refined understanding of editing techniques in multi-camera environments, a meticulous attention to detail, and are adept at working on complex edits autonomously and under deadline. You have an in-depth knowledge of Adobe systems.

You will work with producers, editors, journalists and other internal and external collaborators to lead the edit and publication of the Shows department's work. This role is for someone with a deep understanding of social video trends who takes an innovative and adaptive approach to video formats and techniques.

You will report to the the Post Production Supervisor.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Edit and color-correct Newsroom podcasts across our entire show portfolio, delivering content in both short-form vertical and long-form horizontal format
  • Deliver top-notch product under intense deadline pressure, and without the need for direct supervision, continuous editorial guidance, or task management
  • Bring a digital first mindset to editing on-platform and for social media
  • Edit creatively both for full-length videos and video clips, and in coordination with an audio edit
  • Assist in defining style and techniques that give our videos a voice and make them stand out from the pack
  • Collaborate on optimizing a post production and archival workflow
  • Perform related work as assigned
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at at a major video outlet or production company
  • Strong digital video editing background
  • Must have a strong portfolio of digital work
  • Experience creating original videos that incorporate audio, video, still images, graphics and text
  • Expertise in Adobe Premiere and CS

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Must be up to speed on the latest media techniques and technologies
  • Work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize news into a tight, informative and engaging video
  • Experience working in video podcasts
  • Experience producing, scripting, and/or structuring digital news or documentary stories
  • Experience making quick decisions under intense deadlines in a high-pressure newsroom setting
  • A foundational knowledge of legal, ethical, copyright and usage issues for visuals
  • Well-versed in the world of social and digital media, with a keen eye on what competitors are doing and what new tools are being used
  • Willingness to work a flexible schedule

job.title: Publicist
job.description:
Who we are

Semafor is a global news platform for an increasingly complex world in which consumers are overwhelmed by too many news sources and unsure what to trust. We are building Semafor to enable world-class journalists to deliver reporting and insights with rigor in journalistic forms that ensure a new level of transparency. Our editors and reporters distill the most important stories from all over in formats that uncover the forces shaping the stories, explain the interests behind polarizing narratives, and replenish the stock of shared facts. As a global platform, Semafor recognizes that smart people can disagree and that informed readers need to understand alternative points of view from competing centers of power and culture in a multi-polar world. Want to join us? Read on. 

About this role

Reporting to the Global Head of Communications, this role will be responsible for helping to manage the day-to-day operations of Semafor’s communications efforts. Embedded deep within the fabric of the newsroom, you’ll be working with our journalists and editors each day on amplifying our journalism across outlets that align with our brand and goals, as well as supporting and promoting other core areas of our business.

As Publicist, you will:

  • Work closely with the Global Head of Communications to develop and execute a robust day-to-day communications strategy that supports the newsroom.
  • Develop and implement communications / PR strategies that amplify Semafor’s high-impact reporting, editorial projects, and newsroom initiatives.
  • Proactively identify editorial moments, trends, or news cycles where our reporting and talent should be part of the media conversation 
  • Maintain an always-on awareness of the competitive media landscape to spot gaps and opportunities for coverage.
  • Cultivate strong relationships with national TV and radio/podcast bookers, and maintain segmented, up-to-date media lists.
  • Pitch booking producers across major broadcast networks and platforms (including TV, radio, and podcasts/YouTube) daily, working closely with newsroom leaders and journalists to promote scoops and impactful journalism 
  • Draft talking points, briefings, and internal messaging for internal and external communications, including writing and editing media alerts on deadline.
  • Secure daily press coverage across television, radio, print, and digital outlets for a wide range of coverage areas.
  • Support development and implementation of a creative and consistent internal communications strategy.
  • Lead and manage a global calendar of awards submissions, media lists, and speaking opportunities.
  • Oversee media monitoring, including compiling timely press recaps and reports using a range of PR tools.
  • Proactively recommend and implement new workflows and processes to improve the effectiveness and speed of the communications function.

Requirements:

  • Experience in communications, preferably at a news organization, in media/entertainment/politics or other similar work environments. 
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent is preferred.
  • Deep passion for news and current affairs with broad understanding of the current global / U.S. news/media environment is a must. 
  • Proven ability to garner media attention, craft stories, and drive daily results. 
  • Previous experience booking network appearances for individuals/brands, and interacting with reporters on daily inquiries and media requests.
  • A team player with the ability to work with others in a fast-paced news environment on deadline.
  • A strong sense of what makes a good feature or news angle, and a varied contact list across the media landscape, including broadcast, print and online, with contacts in news in the US and globally
  • Impeccable writing skills with the ability to write and produce clear and concise communications materials under time constraints. 
  • Previous experience with using PR & social media tools (e.g., Critical Mention, Muck Rack, Mailchimp, Twitter) is a plus
  • Experience with handling set-up and logistics for speaking engagements and events.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams.
  • Proactivity and resourceful problem-solving skills.

Additional Job Details

This position is based in New York, NY. Candidates must be willing to work flexible hours and travel domestically and internationally on an as-needed basis.

Salary Range: $90k-$110K base annual salary.  Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to education, work experience, certifications, etc.

Additional job details

Semafor offers a Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) policy to our full-time, salaried employees who may take paid time off as-needed without a prescribed limit or defined balance.

Semafor, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and enthusiastically encourages people from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. Semafor, Inc. will consider all applicants without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical and/or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do:

  • Process multi state payroll for over 500 employees, including union employees across multiple unions in Workday. 
  • Perform calculations in overtime, PTO, and union contributions.
  • Prepare weekly, monthly, and quarterly financial reports that include summaries of earnings, tax deductions and union dues for team audits, finance team and managers requests.
  • Resolve payroll discrepancies and respond timely to employee queries.
  • Provide initial resolution support and ensure prompt, accurate, and consistent handling of inquiries via Zendesk ticketing system, virtual meetings, and face-to-face engagement.
  • Process employee data changes related to payroll, benefits, PTO, employment verifications, job changes, salary, terminations, org-level changes, and HR transactions.
  • Provide aid and guidance to employees seeking to update personal information in the HRIS system, currently Workday.
  • Adhere to ATS Service Level Agreement (SLA) to ensure optimal customer service is consistently achieved.
  • Own market documents that support all changes (Contracts, CBAs, Offer Letters, Notification Forms, etc.) to employee data and payroll.
  • Partner with Subject Matter Experts (SME) to resolve specific inquiries that require further research and knowledge.
  • Participates in team projects and identifies process improvement opportunities.

Qualifications

More About You:

 

A well-rounded team player that can work independently and in group settings on a day to day basis. Someone who is great at multitasking, meeting deadlines, and open to gaining more payroll experience.

 

Required:

  • 2+ years of Payroll or data processing work experience.
  • 2+ year of Workday experience.
  • 1+ year of customer service related work experience.
  • 1+ year of previous experience working with multiple unions, preferably in the media industry (specifically AFTRA, WGA, IBEW).
  • Previous experience with multi state payroll.
  • Previous experience with employee data or HRIS functions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to meet strict deadlines.
  • Shows integrity, discretion, and sensitivity to confidential data.
  • Solution-oriented, organized, and highly attentive.
  • Ability to work in a fast paced and constantly changing environment.
  • Ability to research, interpret, and reconcile data.
  • Ability to keep stakeholders informed.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance or related field.

 

Preferred:

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

We’re looking for a senior editor to lead our visual journalism across Asia, driving the execution of new forms of storytelling and overseeing a team of graphics and multimedia journalists. This role is based in the Times’ Seoul newsroom. 

Visual journalists at The Times have investigated how China built a great wall of villages along its frontier and strong-armed its way into dominating the South China Sea, documented the Myanmar military’s campaign of terror against its own people and Taliban rule in Afghanistan, and reconstructed South Korean president’s botched martial law bid. They have revealed how drones have transformed the war in Ukraine. They have also devised ambitious multimedia approaches to explain the far-reaching impact of the Iran war, air pollution in India and American households’ reliance on Chinese goods.

We want to do more of these kinds of stories. And we want to continue to transform how we work to bring visual reporting and editing into the core of how we show readers the world and hold power accountable. We will do this through compelling graphical explanations; urgent, immersive field reporting in photography and video; sharp visual news coverage; and investigations driven by deep reporting on imagery and data.

This role reports to the assistant international editor for visuals in New York and collaborates with the Asia editor to help drive coverage of Asia. You will work closely with the lead video producer and photo editor in Seoul, the senior editor for visuals in London, and counterparts in photo, video, graphics and news design.

This is an in-office position based in Seoul,  and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Main responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with international editors to drive visual coverage of Asia. 
  • Coordinate, lead and edit the work of correspondents and visual journalists on visual stories.
  • Serve as the leader of a small group of graphics/multimedia reporters focused on Asia, helping to create, design and edit multimedia coverage. 
  • In collaboration with the deputy International editor for visuals, plan and execute stories that use data analysis and visualization, photography, imagery analysis, open source investigation and other reporting techniques.
  • Work with desk leaders to shape and execute our broader editorial strategy for visual journalism, including how we should work with partners in photo, video, graphics and news design.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the assistant international editor for visuals.

Basic qualifications:

  • Strong news judgment.
  • Ability to identify and conceive ambitious stories, spot visual opportunities in reporting and develop them into a range of compelling visual forms.
  • Skill pulling multiple visual disciplines together into multimedia projects, with an emphasis on visualization, explanatory visuals, digital design, use of video and other visual forms. 
  • A record of clear communication and strong collaboration with colleagues.
  • The ability to write clearly, work on tight deadlines and edit to sharpen the relationship between visuals and copy.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams to create ambitious multimedia news stories, including interactive visuals, and help them develop as journalists. . 
  • Strong portfolio in one or more of these areas: data visualization, mapping, explanatory writing, news illustration, digital design, interactive development and explanatory multimedia or video.
