job.title: Audience Development Executive- Fixed term Contract
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The role 

FT Live is the global conferences and events division of the Financial Times Group. We deliver more than 200 events a year, including large-scale global summits, bespoke client forums, and digital conferences. Our events convene world-class speakers and bring together senior executives, policymakers, and thought leaders across industries and geographies.

The Audience Development Executive plays a crucial role in driving delegate acquisition and audience engagement for high-impact B2B events. Based in Manila, this role supports the FT Live marketing team by researching, qualifying, and managing delegate leads, contributing directly to the success of our client-sponsored and FT-branded events.

Working under the supervision of the Audience Development Manager, the Executive will be responsible for researching and building prospect lists, conducting outreach, and ensuring data accuracy in line with campaign briefs. 

This is an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented, curious, and proactive individual looking to gain experience in international events and audience marketing. This role is instrumental in identifying new leads for FT Live events and supporting the broader data acquisition strategy. Working from detailed marketing briefs, the Executive will conduct targeted research, build lead lists in a templated format, and collaborate with the Data team to upload and process records.

Key responsibilities

Audience Research & Acquisition

  • Create high-quality lead lists based on event-specific briefs (e.g. job title, industry, location, and company).
  • Use LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Cognism, web research, databases, and other tools to identify prospects.
  • Collaborate with marketing managers and project leads to define and expand on target profiles.
  • Conduct independent company, sector and market research to identify relevant organisations and decision-makers beyond initial campaign wishlists.

Audience Outreach

  • Craft and send personalised LinkedIn InMails and emails to potential delegates.
  • Support delegate invitation campaigns by managing email follow-ups and tracking responses and identifying opportunities for further engagement.

Data Management

  • Perform data audits, clean-ups, and deduplication to maintain high data quality.
  • Support audience data checks to assess the size, relevance and feasibility of potential audiences for prospective events.
  • Collaborate with the Data and Delegate Services teams to ensure leads are uploaded, segmented, and handled in accordance with FT’s compliance protocols, including GDPR and consent regulations.

Campaign Support

  • Track responses and lead engagement through internal systems and campaign dashboards.
  • Contribute to post-campaign analysis, highlighting the impact of research activity and identifying relevant audience insights and learnings.
  • Monitor the status of leads and support the audience development manager in adjusting strategies as needed.
  • Provide ad hoc reporting and analysis as requested.
  • Manage research across multiple campaigns and priorities, adapting to changing deadlines during busy periods.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with event marketers, project managers, sales, and operations to ensure alignment on delegate recruitment goals and expanded event presence.
  • Attend internal briefing meetings and proactively share research findings, audience trends and potential targeting opportunities.

Required skills and experience 

  • Open to fresh graduates with a Bachelor's degree in any four-year course
  • Curiosity and willingness to learn about different industries, companies, markets and business topics.
  • Experience of working with and manipulating large sets of data.
  • Strong research and analytical skills, with the ability to find, assess and organise information from multiple sources.
  • Must be proactive and be able to operate with limited supervision from line manager.
  • A team player, who is a strong, confident communicator and collaborator.
  • Ability to think creatively, ask questions and test ideas.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Resourceful approach to research and willingness to explore different sources and methods when information is difficult to find.

Desirable experience 

  • Prior experience in audience research, lead generation, or delegate acquisition.
  • Knowledge of GDPR (and similar), impact on Marketing and Communications globally.
  • Microsoft Excel Proficiency: Confident using Excel to manage, clean, and analyse lead data (e.g. using filters, pivot tables, and formulas).
  • CRM Experience: Familiarity with Salesforce (or similar CRM systems) for logging, managing, and tracking lead data in alignment with audience development campaigns.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered research tools or data visualisation platforms.
  • Knowledge of Cognism or other B2B contact data platforms for sourcing and verifying leads.
  • Familiarity with collaboration tools like Slack, Monday.com, or other similar tools for task tracking and internal communications.
  • Previous experience working within a global or internationally distributed team.

Working Hours:

  • Flexibility to work UK business hours is required. Occasional out-of-hours support may be needed during key campaign periods.

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process may be monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Please beware of fraudulent job postings and offers claiming to be from the Financial Times. All legitimate opportunities will direct you to apply through the official Financial Times careers site, and the FT will never ask for financial information, payments, or referrals to third parties during the hiring process. If you have any concerns about the legitimacy of a job posting or suspect any scam activity, please contact talent@ft.com.

job.description:
Location: GA-Atlanta

Job Title:  Systems Analyst II

 

Position Overview

The Digital Customer Support (DCS) Systems Analyst II provides Tier 2 technical and operational support for Cox Media Group's business-critical applications and digital platforms. This role focuses on troubleshooting, incident resolution, application administration, and maintaining reliable services for internal customers.

 

The ideal candidate is a customer-focused problem solver with strong technical, analytical, and communication skills. The position includes participation in an after-hours on-call rotation.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide Tier 2 support for enterprise applications, SaaS platforms, and associated integrations.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve application incidents and service requests escalated through the Service Desk.
  • Support CMG's Content Management Systems (CMS) and WideOrbit revenue platform, including troubleshooting, user provisioning, and account management.
  • Participate in on-call support, major incident response, and technical escalations.
  • Support and cross-train on Change Management and Critical Problem Management processes to ensure team-wide coverage, operational continuity, and backup support when needed
  • Collaborate with vendors, application owners, and other IT teams to resolve technical issues.
  • Maintain support documentation, troubleshooting procedures, and knowledge base articles.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, reduce recurring incidents, and enhance customer satisfaction.
  • Support and cross-train on Change Management and Critical Problem Management processes to ensure team-wide coverage, operational continuity, and backup support when needed.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in technical support, application support, or IT operations.
  • Experience troubleshooting enterprise applications and SaaS platforms.
  • Familiarity with IT service management tools such as ServiceNow or Jira.
  • Understanding of Incident, Problem, and Change management processes.
  • Experience with user provisioning, account administration, and application troubleshooting.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple issues and work effectively across technical teams.
  • Experience supporting Windows, macOS, and mobile platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Technical degree or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Experience supporting CMS, WideOrbit, or other digital media applications.
  • Familiarity with ITIL practices and application monitoring tools.
  • Experience with automation, application integrations, or process improvement.

About Cox Media Group 

CMG Media Corporation (d/b/a Cox Media Group) is an industry-leading media company with unparalleled brands, award-winning content, and exceptional team members. CMG provides valuable local and national journalism and entertainment content to the people and communities it serves. The company's businesses encompass 17 high-quality, market-leading television brands in 9 markets; 45 top-performing radio stations delivering multiple genres of content in 9 markets; and numerous streaming and digital platforms. CMG's TV portfolio includes multiple primary affiliates of ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, Telemundo and MyNetworkTV, as well as several valuable news and independent stations. For more information about CMG, visit www.coxmediagroup.com

job.title: Digital Content & Engagement Intern – Forecasting and Communications
job.description:
AccuWeather is seeking a highly creative, curious, and deeply collaborative Digital Content & Engagement Intern – Forecasting and Communications, to work directly with AccuWeather forecasters and the Writing Committee to further elevate the detail, clarity, precision, and distinctiveness of the language used to describe forecasts for our users. This role is designed for a graduate student or an individual with equivalent writing experience who brings fresh thinking about how complex weather information can be expressed in ways that are more detailed, precise, clear, engaging, and scientifically sound.

Embedded closely with Forecast Operations, this position will learn from meteorologists, participate in the forecast-writing process, and help develop new approaches, terminology, and descriptive frameworks that make AccuWeather forecasts more informative and better than what is available from any other source. The emphasis is on improving the consumer forecast experience - not traditional public relations - by helping forecasters communicate what the weather will be, what the impact will be, how it will evolve, what it may look like, and what details matter most to people making decisions. This includes a laser focus on developing stronger displays, greater artistry, and more effective visual communications that amplify the advantages of AccuWeather forecasts and content.

The Digital Content & Engagement Intern – Forecasting and Communications will serve as a bridge between meteorological expertise and exceptional consumer-facing writing, helping AccuWeather deliver forecast descriptions with greater depth, nuance, consistency, and usefulness while preserving the scientific accuracy and authority at the core of the AccuWeather brand.

 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Forecast Language, Detail & Description:

  • Work side-by-side with forecasters to craft and refine accurate, detailed, consumer-focused descriptions of daily weather, changing conditions, major storms, seasonal patterns, and forecast developments.
    • Elevate forecast language beyond basic conditions by identifying the most useful details, nuances, timing, impacts, transitions, and sensory descriptions that help users better understand what to expect. Use bold, catchy and descriptive language.
    • Translate complex meteorological concepts into clearer, more detailed, consumer-friendly language without sacrificing scientific meaning, accuracy, or appropriate expressions of forecast confidence.
    • Develop new descriptive approaches, vocabulary, sentence structures, and frameworks that make AccuWeather forecasts more distinctive, informative, and useful than competing forecast experiences.
    • Help establish consistent terminology for recurring weather patterns while preserving enough flexibility for forecasters to communicate the unique character and details of each forecast.

 

Forecaster & Writing Committee Collaboration:

  • Embed with AccuWeather forecasters to understand how forecasts are created, where language choices can add value, and how writing can better communicate meteorological insight to users.
    • Work closely with the AccuWeather Writing Committee to test, evaluate, and introduce new approaches to forecast writing and description.
    • Bring an outside writing perspective to established forecast workflows, asking thoughtful questions and proposing new ways of thinking, writing, and working.
  • Challenge conventional approaches to forecast description and explore new ways to communicate weather that provide users with greater detail, context, understanding, and value.
    • Gather feedback from meteorologists and other stakeholders, iterate on language, and help turn successful approaches into practical writing guidance and repeatable standards.
    • Support a collaborative environment in which meteorological expertise and strong writing work together to create a richer forecast experience.

 

Consumer Forecast Experience & Innovation:

  • Review forecast descriptions across AccuWeather consumer experiences and identify opportunities to add specificity, context, clarity, and useful detail.
    • Develop and test language that helps users better understand the timing, intensity, duration, variability, uncertainty, and real-world impacts of weather events.
  • Explore new ways to make routine forecasts more useful, engaging, descriptive, and impactful, bringing the same level of creativity and attention to detail to both high-impact weather coverage and everyday conditions such as temperature, wind, precipitation, cloud cover, humidity, visibility, and changing conditions.
    • Help ensure forecast descriptions are clear and effective across digital platforms while retaining the depth and detail that distinguish AccuWeather.
    • Contribute ideas that reinforce AccuWeather’s Superior Accuracy™ through the quality, precision, and usefulness of the forecast language itself.

 

Writing Standards & Continuous Improvement:

  • Help evolve AccuWeather’s authoritative, trustworthy, detailed, and forward-looking forecast voice.
    • Identify new ways to describe weather phenomena that are vivid, memorable, consumer-relevant, and scientifically sound.
    • Contribute to forecast-writing standards, terminology guidelines, examples, and best practices used by forecasters and content teams.
    • Study how forecast language performs in practice and recommend improvements based on clarity, usefulness, consistency, and differentiation.
    • Encourage experimentation and fresh thinking while respecting operational requirements, meteorological accuracy, and established review processes.
    • Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Writing, or a closely related writing-intensive field is required.
    • Current graduate student in communications, writing, journalism, English, creative writing, technical writing, or a related discipline, or equivalent advanced or professional writing experience.
    • Exceptional command of written language, including tone, clarity, precision, descriptive detail, structure, and audience awareness.
    • Demonstrated ability to take complex or technical information and make it clear, specific, useful, and engaging for a broad audience.
    • Strong collaborative skills and genuine interest in working closely with meteorologists, subject-matter experts, and a writing committee.
    • Intellectual curiosity and willingness to learn meteorological concepts and forecast workflows.
    • Ability to receive expert feedback, revise quickly, and improve language through an iterative process.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Interest in or familiarity with meteorology, weather forecasting, climate, environmental science, science communication, or technical writing.
    • Experience developing descriptive language, style guidance, editorial standards, or writing frameworks.
    • Experience collaborating directly with technical or scientific subject-matter experts.
    • Portfolio examples demonstrating precise, vivid, explanatory, or detail-rich writing.

 

Skills & Competencies:

  • Creative thinking grounded in accuracy, precision, and credibility.
    • Exceptional descriptive and explanatory writing.
    • Ability to identify and elevate the details that matter most to users.
    • Strong editing, revision, and language-development skills.
    • Curiosity about weather and willingness to learn from forecasters.
    • Collaborative, workshop-oriented approach to writing.
    • Ability to develop practical writing standards while continuing to experiment with new approaches.
    • Excellent organizational and time management skills.
    • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of an embedded team.

 

About AccuWeather

AccuWeather, recognized and documented as the most accurate and most used source of weather forecasts and warnings in the world, has saved over 12,000 lives, prevented injury to over 100,000 people, and saved companies tens of billions of dollars through better planning and decision-making.

A billion people around the world rely on AccuWeather’s proven Superior Accuracy™ across our consumer digital platforms. AccuWeather.com is the #1 weather destination and one of the top 100 most-visited websites in the world, and our award-winning AccuWeather app delivers detailed real-time forecasts to tens of millions of smartphones.

AccuWeather forecasts also appear on digital signage, in 700 newspapers, are heard on over 400 radio stations, and viewed on 100 television stations. The AccuWeather Network and AccuWeather NOW® reach an audience of over 225 million on cable and streaming platforms including DirecTV, Charter Communications - Spectrum, Verizon, Samsung, Vizio, Philo, Frndly TV, Comcast’s Xfinity X1 and Xfinity Stream, Roku, Xumo, Rockbot, LG, and Amazon Freevee.

AccuWeather For Business serves more than half of the Fortune 500 companies and thousands of other businesses and government agencies globally.

Dr. Joel Myers, Founder and Executive Chairman, established AccuWeather in 1962 and is considered the “father of modern commercial meteorology.” Myers is a visionary entrepreneur and has been called “the most accurate man in weather” by The New York Times. He has been recognized in Entrepreneur Magazine’s Encyclopedia of Entrepreneurs as one of the greatest entrepreneurs in American history.  Myers received the American Meteorological Society’s 2018 Award for Outstanding Contributions to the Advancement of Applied Meteorology and the National Weather Association’s 2017 Lifetime Achievement Award, in addition to numerous other accolades.

 

Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

AccuWeather is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to all applicants and existing employees and we evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, creed, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy and gender identity/expression), sexual orientation, age, ancestry, physical or mental disability, marital status, political affiliation, religion, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran status, or any other basis protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
AccuWeather is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation because of a disability for any part of the employment process, please send an e-mail to human.resources@accuweather.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

A Photo Editor for The New York Times has a creative eye and an innovative approach to formats and mobile-focused presentations. You should bring sharp technical skills and sound journalistic judgment to join a team creating visual journalism—still and video— for breaking news, features and enterprise stories for on- and off-platform publishing.

The primary duties of the job are to conceptualize and assign photography and video for the New York Times’ Business report, and to select and publish images and video for multiple platforms of The New York Times. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs and video, working productively with staff photographers, freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of pictures, as well as editors, designers, and reporters in the newsroom. You will engage our staff and freelance photographers to identify and develop pitches with strong visual potential, producing strong photographic, video and multimedia displays with an eye toward innovative digital story forms and presentations.

You have a strong demonstrable passion for multimedia, journalism and photography of all kinds, and possess a broad knowledge of the current photographic, video, visual and social media landscape, including digitally innovative formats and mobile-first multimedia presentations. You must be a team player and a good communicator, and must initiate and develop ideas for photographs, short video clips and visual stories in different formats.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City, and includes regular attendance in the office up to four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive of, pitch, develop, edit, pace and build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback
  • Collaborate with writers, reporters, editors, visual editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind
  • Coordinate with Business desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field
  • Maintain and meet your desk’s photo budget, process/approve invoices in a timely fashion
  • Attend photo department meetings to report and share your desk’s visual priorities
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • This role reports to a Deputy Editor of Photography

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations
  • Proven deep research skills
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere is a plus
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines in a high-pressure news environment

Please submit a portfolio with examples of work that you have assigned and/or edited along with your CV.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

REQ-020786

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.

job.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
Who We Are

UnitedMasters 

UnitedMasters is building a marketplace that connects artists, brands and fans - empowering artists to earn and grow. UnitedMasters has taken the bold step of building a music distribution service that, radically, puts artists first - disrupting the legacy music business by letting up-and-coming artists distribute their music directly to fans through streaming services while maintaining ownership of their master recording rights and up to 100% of royalties. Through the combination of UnitedMasters' music distribution platform and its deep ties to brands, UnitedMasters enables independent artists and change-makers to grow and earn unlike any other platform.

The UnitedMasters team is made up of musicians, marketers, engineers, and storytellers with backgrounds from YouTube, SoundCloud, Pandora, Facebook, Uber, Dropbox, Complex, VICE, and more. We work hand in hand with the award-winning creative teams that forge those innovative partnerships at Translation (our in-house creative advertising agency).

The Role

You'll partner with platform, data, QA, and product engineers across the organization, owning the intersection of reliability and security: the tooling, monitoring, alerting, emergency response, and systems design the whole org depends on.

A defining part of the role is building how we protect our systems going forward. We're investing in agentic, AI-driven security pipelines that continuously detect, triage, and help remediate vulnerabilities across our codebase and infrastructure — and you'll lead the design and stewardship of that capability.

Above all, though, this is a coaching and consulting role. We're looking for a strong listener, patient collaborator, thoughtful architect, and skilled builder — someone who identifies needs in reliability and security and empowers peer developers to improve them.

What You'll Do

  • Partner with platform, data, QA, and product teams to understand their automation, infrastructure, monitoring, and security needs.
  • Build tooling and processes that solve the problems those conversations surface.
  • Build and maintain an agentic vulnerability detection and mitigation pipeline that will scan, triage, and propose fixes, with human-in-the-loop guardrails.
  • Embed security into the development lifecycle, including threat modeling, supp ly-chain hygiene, secrets management, secure-by-default patterns.
  • Lead security and reliability incident response as first-class operational concerns.
  • Define company-level SLAs, SLOs, and Error Budgets, and help teams set their own.
  • Steer system design toward shared tooling and decisions that ensure reliability, scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Join the on-call rotation as a peer to spot process gaps and coach on response.
  • Act as a senior escalation for infrastructure and security issues, helping resolve them while coaching teams to handle the next.
  • Own our AWS infrastructure and set the long-term strategy for our reliability and security posture, balancing scalability and cost.

Who You Are 

  • Senior-to-staff experience as an SRE, platform, or infrastructure engineer, owning production reliability at scale.
  • Hands-on application and/or infrastructure security experience; enough to lead the security conversation without a separate security team in the room.
  • Practical experience building with LLMs and agentic systems. You've shipped something real and understand their failure modes and where human oversight is non-negotiable.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals. You build tools and systems, not just configure them.
  • A coaching instinct: you measure impact by how much you raise the teams around you.

Our Values

  • We Get on the Plane — Entrepreneurial spirit means fully committing to the journey not just having the idea.
  • We Expect Challenge + Respect — We constantly challenge each other and the work to reach excellence, always with respect.
  • We Are Defined by Our Resilience — We stay resourceful, fail fast, keep getting better, and never quit on our mission or our team.
  • We Pursue Answers Before the Question Has to Be Asked — We understand our customers so well that we anticipate what they need before they ask.
  • We Run Towards Darkness — We have the courage to work through uncertainty rather than settling for an easier, inferior plan.
  • We Know What We Don't Know — We bring confidence in what we do know, and honesty about what we don't.

Compensation

Salary Hiring Range: $195,000 - $240,000

Our salary ranges are designed to be competitive for companies of our size and within our industry and represent just one part of our overall rewards package. We also offer company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision plans, a 401(k) with company match, and, depending on the role and individual circumstances, additional compensation opportunities such as bonuses and stock options.

Individual pay rate decisions are based on a number of factors, including qualifications for the role, experience level, skillset, and balancing internal equity relative to peers at the company. We expect the majority of the candidates who are offered roles at our company to fall healthily throughout the range based on these factors.

The range above is for the expectations as laid out in the job description, however we are often open to a wide variety of profiles, and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this job description as posted. If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated with you as a candidate.

The salary range above is for NY/CA. As a company, we have a location-based strategy, which means the salary range could be lower or higher than this if the role is hired in another location.

About UnitedMasters, Inc.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world's leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. Backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz, and Apple, UnitedMasters, Inc. is reimagining how brands and artists come together to tell their stories, build profitable growth, and push culture forward.

Equal Opportunity & Accommodation

UnitedMasters is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We seek to bring together diverse ideas, experiences, skill sets, perspectives, backgrounds and identities to drive innovative solutions. We commit to promoting a welcoming environment where inclusion and belonging are held as a shared responsibility.

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

Phishing Scam Warning

PHISHING SCAM WARNING: UnitedMasters is among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. The imposters are creating misleading email accounts, conducting remote “interviews,” and making fake job offers in order to collect personal and financial information from unsuspecting individuals. Please be aware that no job offers will be made from UnitedMasters without a formal interview process. Additionally, UnitedMasters will not ask you to purchase equipment or supplies as part of your onboarding process. If you have any questions, please reach out to TA@unitedmasters.com.

Job Description:


Staff Engineer, Snowflake Platform


About the team
The Data Architecture & Platform Engineering team runs the data infrastructure behind Dow Jones products, analytics, and AI across B2B, B2C, and internal use cases. We own the Snowflake footprint which serves as the foundation of all DJ structured data, the surrounding platforms and patterns, and the governance framework. We build for scale, reliability, security, and cost efficiency.


About the role
This is an individual-contributor leadership role focused on Snowflake infrastructure at the Dow Jones enterprise scale. You'll own the platform end to end: account architecture and administration, security and access control, and the DevOps machinery that makes Snowflake safe and easy to use across dozens of teams and every business unit.


You will own the Snowflake platform's AI story: efficient, cost-managed access to Cortex and other AI features, optimized patterns for LLM-assisted workflows, and standards that let engineers across DJ build with AI on top of
governed data.


You'll ship the hard parts yourself, set the standards other teams follow, and mentor the engineers who work in and around Snowflake. You lead through influence: design reviews, working code, written arguments, and mentoring.


You'll partner with security, compliance, finance, product, and engineering leaders to turn DJ's data-platform goals into infrastructure that holds up over time.


You'll split your time between hands-on Snowflake work on the highest-stakes projects; standards and platform-level decisions; and mentoring engineers across levels.


What you'll do
• Own the Snowflake footprint across Dow Jones: accounts, warehouses, roles, databases, and the operating model behind them.
• Design and evolve RBAC, column and row-level policies, masking, tagging, and data classification for every business unit.
• Build and maintain the DevOps pipeline for Snowflake: Terraform, CI/CD for schema and object changes, automated testing, and change management.
• Set and enforce standards for security, network policies, private connectivity, SSO, SCIM, and secrets management.
• Optimize cost and performance: resource monitors, warehouse right-sizing, query analysis, credit budgeting, and FinOps reporting.
• Design for reliability at DJ scale: replication, failover, disaster recovery, incident response, and observability across the platform.
• Explore and implement emerging AI tooling to accelerate our modern data engineering practices.
• Lead architecture and design reviews for major Snowflake initiatives.
• Anticipate scalability, reliability, security, and cost problems before they land.
• Hunt technical debt in the platform to reduce complexity so downstream teams get more done with less.
• Debug the problems no one else can. Lead during incidents and get to root cause fast.
• Mentor engineers across levels, including senior and staff peers, through design guidance, code review, pairing, and documentation.

• Contribute to how the org grows engineers: development practices, career frameworks, communities of practice.
• Communicate through design docs, wiki, and tech talks; tailor the message for engineers, product, security, and executives.

What we're looking for
• 7+ years in data engineering, platform engineering, or infrastructure roles, with time spent at large or enterprise-scale companies.
• Thought-leader of AI and opinionated about how to make it work effectively at scale on a data platform. Dow Jones invests heavily in AI and expects Staff engineers to shape how it lands.
• Deep, hands-on Snowflake experience running a production account at scale: administration, RBAC, security posture, cost, and performance.
• Strong Terraform experience (Snowflake provider or equivalent) and CI/CD for data infrastructure.
• Track record designing and operating data platforms that serve many teams, business units, or downstream systems.
• Security fluency: RBAC design, data masking, access policies, private connectivity, SSO and SCIM, audit posture.
• Fluency with observability, monitoring, incident response, and on-call for data infrastructure.
• Strong Python for platform tooling, automation, or service work.
• Experience working in regulated or audited environments (SOC 2, SOX, GDPR, or equivalent).
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.
• Ability to influence across teams and functions without formal authority, backed by strong writing and speaking.

Nice to have
• dbt, Airflow, or comparable orchestration and transformation experience.
• Snowflake certifications (SnowPro Advanced: Administrator or Data Engineer).
• Serious Snowflake cost optimization or FinOps work.
• Data governance, metadata, or lineage tooling (Collibra, Atlan, Alation, or similar).
• Cloud platform depth (AWS especially) and platform operations at scale.
• Near-real-time or event-driven data processing.
• Prior experience developing engineers through mentoring, design reviews, or communities of practice.

As part of the News Product organization, you will work with designers, other mobile engineers, and web engineers, and more on a team.

21GRAMS, part of Real Chemistry, is a full-service healthcare advertising agency built on the belief that healthcare should feel more human. We combine bold creativity, strategic rigor, and deep scientific understanding to create work that changes behavior, improves outcomes, and makes a meaningful impact on people's lives. Our culture is grounded in collaboration, curiosity, and a shared commitment to doing exceptional work. We believe in being good to each other while pushing ourselves to deliver ideas that move audiences, brands, and healthcare forward.

We’re looking for a Medical Copywriter who can bring together scientific fluency and creative instinct — someone who knows how to turn complex clinical information into clear, compelling, brand-building copy. This is not a traditional medical writer role. We’re looking for someone with healthcare advertising experience who can concept, collaborate, and write across a range of promotional and scientific materials while maintaining accuracy, compliance, and brand voice.

The Medical Copywriter is responsible for developing medically sound, strategically sharp, and emotionally resonant copy across healthcare/pharma campaigns. This person will partner closely with Creative, Strategy, Account, Project Management, Editorial, and medical teams to bring ideas to life across multiple channels and deliverables.

The ideal candidate understands how to translate science into stories, can move fluidly between promotional copy and scientific content, and has experience working in an agency environment where deadlines are fast, standards are high, and collaboration is key.

This is a great opportunity for a writer who loves the challenge of making complex science feel human, relevant, and creatively powerful. You’ll work at the intersection of medical rigor and brand storytelling, helping shape work that is strategically grounded, emotionally intelligent, and deeply impactful.

This role can be remote within the United States or based in any of our U.S. office locations, including New York City, San Francisco, Boston, Chicago, Lambertville or Carmel.

 

What you’ll do:

  • Write for healthcare/pharma advertising campaigns across HCP, patient, caregiver, and DTC audiences 
  • Translate complex clinical data, mechanism of action, and product information into clear, engaging, on-brand messaging 
  • Develop copy for a wide range of deliverables, including websites, digital banners, emails, sales materials, patient education, videos, social, and other omnichannel assets 
  • Partner with an Art Director and broader creative team to develop integrated campaign concepts and executions 
  • Ensure all copy aligns with brand strategy, marketing objectives, tone of voice, and audience needs 
  • Work closely with Medical/Scientific leadership to ensure content is accurate, balanced, and compliant 
  • Participate in strategic planning, internal brainstorms, and client meetings as needed 
  • Present concepts internally and incorporate feedback thoughtfully and efficiently 
  • Review and refine copy throughout the agency process for clarity, grammar, consistency, and accuracy 
  • Collaborate with Editorial to resolve stylistic or grammatical concerns 
  • Build a strong understanding of assigned brands, disease states, competitors, and the evolving market landscape 
  • Proactively identify relevant medical, competitive, or regulatory updates that may impact messaging or tactical development
  • Bring a solutions-oriented mindset to projects and contribute to the overall quality of the work 

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

 

What you should have:

  • 2–4+ years of experience in healthcare/pharma advertising, medical communications, or a closely related agency environment 
  • Experience writing within regulated categories, ideally with exposure to HCP and/or DTC promotional work 
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating conceptual thinking, copywriting craft, and brand voice development 
  • Ability to balance creativity and scientific accuracy 
  • Comfortable partnering with cross-functional teams including Creative, Account, PM, Editorial, and Medical 
  • Strong verbal communication and presentation skills 
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common research tools/platforms 
  • Knowledge of or strong interest in science, medicine, and healthcare marketing 
  • Experience working across multiple products or disease states 
  • Familiarity with MLR/regulatory review processes 
  • Ability to contribute to both promotional initiatives and scientific communications 
  • Curiosity about innovation in healthcare, audience behavior, and emerging creative formats 

 

Pay Range: $90,000 - $110,000

You will lead all aspects of new business development, from opportunity identification through pitch execution. You will ensure every team member involved in the pitch process has a seamless, organized experience, fostering collaboration, efficiency and confidence at every stage.

Additionally, you will help own the new client onboarding process, ensuring that day-to-day brand teams are fully equipped with the insights, timelines, and resources needed to service each brand from day one. This critical handoff function bridges the gap between winning the business and delivering exceptional work, setting the foundation for long-term client partnerships.

This role can be remote within the United States or based in any of our U.S. office locations, including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Lambertville, NJ, San Francisco, or Carmel, IN.

What you’ll do:

New Business Process Development

  • Establish, refine, and enforce new business processes and standards across the agency
  • Create repeatable frameworks for how opportunities are evaluated, pursued, and executed

Growth Team Leadership

  • Lead and develop a high-performing new business team
  • Ensure every team member involved in the pitch process has a seamless, organized, and collaborative experience

Pipeline Management

  • Identify and qualify new business opportunities 
  • Manage the full pipeline from initial opportunity through close 
  • Track and report on win rates, pipeline health, Saleforce integration, and revenue impact 

Pitch Leadership

  • Lead and support pitch efforts across the agency and with Real Chemistry Partners
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams through the pitch process 
  • Foster confidence and collaboration at every stage of the pursuit

Strategic Partnership with Senior Leadership

  • Serve as a trusted strategic partner to agency leadership on all growth matters 
  • Inform and influence go-to-market strategy across therapeutic areas including launch planning

New Client Onboarding

  • Help own the end-to-end onboarding process for all newly won clients 
  • Ensure day-to-day account teams are fully equipped with the insights, context, and resources needed to service each brand from day one 
  • Bridge the gap between winning the business and delivering exceptional work

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • Our Company values, Best Together, Impact Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always, and Accountability with an "I", genuinely resonate with how you work and lead.
  • You demonstrate the Real Chemistry Can mindset by approaching challenges with optimism, accountability, creativity, and a solutions-oriented attitude, always looking for ways to make a meaningful impact for our clients, colleagues, and communities.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and comfortable adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and priorities in a fast-paced, evolving environment. As our business grows and changes, so do we.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful, with strong prioritization skills, intellectual curiosity, and a desire to leverage data to inform decisions and drive outcomes.
  • You are energized by innovation and the transformative potential of AI, actively exploring new technologies, identifying opportunities to work smarter, and championing practical, responsible AI adoption that drives meaningful business impact.

What you should have:

  • Bachelor's Degree from an accredited institution
  • 12+ years of new business, account management, or project management experience in a healthcare advertising setting
  • Minimum 5+ years in a leadership or supervisory capacity managing high-performing, cross-functional teams in high-pressure environments
  • Demonstrated expertise in pharmaceutical advertising, healthcare communications, or life sciences agency environment with hands-on experience managing teams and new business opportunities
  • Strong understanding of pharmaceutical promotion standards, FDA/OPDP guidance, and healthcare communications
  • Demonstrated ability in data analysis, reporting, and translating metrics into actionable business insights
  • Working knowledge of project management methodologies including Waterfall, Agile, and Hybrid approaches, with ability to select appropriate methodology for each pitch opportunity
  • Proven track record of leading, developing, and motivating teams to high performance
  • Executive-level communication skills—ability to present complex information clearly to C-suite audiences, stakeholders, and clients
  • Strong written and verbal communication with ability to adapt messages for diverse audiences
  • Strategic thinking and sound judgment, with demonstrated ability to solve complex problems, make decisions under uncertainty, and balance competing priorities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Deep expertise in pharmaceutical advertising and healthcare communications, particularly with experience in oncology, rare disease, specialty pharmaceuticals, or other complex therapeutic areas
  • Demonstrated results from process improvement initiatives with measurable impact on efficiency gains, cost reduction, or quality improvement
  • Client relationship management experience at a senior level, including presenting to pharmaceutical and biotech executives

CORE COMPETENCIES & ATTRIBUTES

Professional Competencies

  • Strategic Business Leadership: Setting vision and direction; aligning operations with business objectives; thinking beyond immediate execution to organizational capability building
  • Process Excellence: Designing, implementing, and continuously improving standardized processes and workflows that scale across new business
  • Stakeholder Management: Building and maintaining effective relationships with executives, clients, cross-functional partners, and team members; navigating competing interests
  • Organizational Development: Building high-performing teams, developing talent, creating culture, and leading organizational change

Required Leadership Attributes

  • Change-Positive, Growth-Oriented

You actively seek smarter, faster, and more effective ways to operate. You are not threatened by AI, innovation, new tools, or new ways of working—you're energized by them. You challenge legacy thinking thoughtfully, experiment with confidence, and view change as an advantage rather than a disruption. You don't defend the status quo because "it works"; you see every process, system, and methodology as a candidate for improvement. You are quick to spot opportunities to expand how we operate collectively and you bring others along on that journey. You stay current with emerging PM tools and methodologies because you're genuinely curious about better ways forward, not because compliance requires it.

  • Commercially and Market Aware

You operate beyond internal agency mechanics and understand the bigger picture. You know your clients' business contexts, therapeutic landscapes, and commercial realities well enough to make informed decisions, ask smarter questions, and connect execution to real-world impact. You don't need to be a medical expert, but you are an industry-savvy operator who understands pharma economics, launch timelines, competitive dynamics, and patient access challenges. You ask "why does this matter commercially?" and "what does success look like for the client?" regularly. This commercial acumen informs how you scope projects, allocate resources, and prioritize decisions. You help your team see beyond deliverables to outcomes.

  • Confident Driver of Progress

You embrace being a driver, not just a facilitator or administrator. You create momentum, push for clarity and decisions when you see ambiguity, hold teams accountable constructively without micromanaging, and move work forward even when information is imperfect or circumstances are complicated. You don't wait for consensus to take action; you make smart calls and bring people along. You recognize that indecision is a decision, and you're willing to take that on. You drive toward clear wins and celebrate progress, which energizes your teams and builds confidence across the organization.

  • Steward of Team Balance and Performance

You actively shape the health of the system, not just the output. You recognize burnout early—in individuals and in teams—and you recalibrate workload, expectations, or resources proactively before people break. You also recognize underperformance with equal clarity and you raise the bar constructively, providing support and accountability. You design operating rhythms, sprint cycles, and governance structures that support both sustainable, high performance and uncompromising standards. You understand that how people feel about their work is as important as what they produce, and that sustainable excellence requires both.

  • Ownership Mindset and Creative Agency

You do not wait for permission to elevate the work. You bring forward ideas on how to operate better, propose smarter ways of organizing projects, design stronger plans, and take responsibility for improving outcomes beyond your assigned scope. You see gaps and fill them. You spot inefficiencies and fix them. You don't assume "that's someone else's problem"—you own the enterprise. This doesn't mean doing everything yourself; it means taking initiative to identify what needs to change and driving toward solutions. Your ownership extends to your team's success, your clients' outcomes, and the health of the broader organization.

  • Strong Judgment and Prioritization Instincts

You consistently make good calls under pressure and constraint. You distinguish signal from noise in a sea of competing demands. You make smart trade-offs between speed, quality, and risk with sound instinct—not by formula. You prioritize effectively, recognizing what matters most and what can wait. You have good instincts about people, situations, and strategic priorities, and you trust those instincts while remaining open to new information. When you have to move fast, you do. When you need to be deliberate, you are. You know the difference, and you rarely get it wrong.

  • Courage and Comfort with Productive Discomfort

You are willing to push when it's uncomfortable and challenge constructively when you see a better path. You hold tension without smoothing it away prematurely; you recognize that some of the best solutions come from sitting with uncomfortable questions rather than resolving them quickly. You make difficult calls when needed—hard conversations, tough decisions, unpopular stands—with confidence rather than approval-seeking. You bring backup (data, reasoning, alternatives) to every discussion. You operate with the confidence of someone who takes responsibility for their decisions and is willing to defend them, but you're also genuinely open to being wrong and course-correcting when new information warrants it.

21GRAMS, Real Chemistry’s advertising agency, has done a lot in its first 5+ years. Known for our creativity, we've just been ranked as the #2 creative health agency in the world by Cannes Lions. It takes a team to do ambitious things, and our ambition is to help people connect with healthcare – by making advertising less of an interruption and more worth people’s time because it gets them. As an agency with the full capabilities of Real Chemistry at our fingertips, we’ve got endless potential.   

At ROOM42 — 21GRAMS' in-house production company, content studio, and Digital & Technology services arm — we are seeking an AI-Forward Technical Lead who is simultaneously a craftsperson, a creative partner, and an accelerator. This person moves fluidly between writing production-quality code, protecting design intent through every build decision, and orchestrating AI tooling to compress the distance from concept to shipped experience. Whether the starting point is a client brief, a Figma file, or a napkin sketch, this Technical Lead is the person who figures out the fastest, most technically sound path to a working, beautiful, compliant deliverable — and builds it. 

This role spans the full ROOM42 output spectrum: marketing websites, microsites, conference kiosks and panel experiences, interactive apps, and data-driven digital tools for healthcare and pharma clients. The ideal candidate has mastered the traditional web development lifecycle and is actively transforming it — using AI at every meaningful stage. 

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs. 

 

What you’ll do:  

Build and Architect 

  • Own end-to-end technical execution for ROOM42 deliverables — websites, microsites, interactive apps, conference kiosk and panel experiences, and real-world evidence platforms 

  • Write and review production-quality code across the full stack; maintain a target of 50% direct hands-on contribution alongside leadership responsibilities 

  • Architect solutions that balance speed-to-market with long-term maintainability, security, and accessibility compliance 

  • Lead technical solutioning on new engagements — translating UX wireframes and creative briefs into clearly scoped, achievable builds 

DevOps and Delivery Infrastructure: 

  • Own Git workflows, branching strategy, and code review standards across all active ROOM42 builds 

  • Maintain CI/CD pipelines for ROOM42's primary hosting environments (WP Engine, Pantheon, Acquia, Netlify/Vercel for JAMstack); make deployments repeatable and low-risk 

  • Manage staging, UAT, and production environment configurations; provision and document access for all ROOM42 developers 

  • Identify and implement automation opportunities across the DevOps lifecycle — from scaffolding new projects to post-deploy validation 

 

AI-Augmented Design-to-Code Pipeline: 

  • Operate Figma MCP server integration to accelerate design handoff — extracting tokens, components, and layout specs directly into code-ready outputs; eliminating manual interpretation cycles 

  • Leverage AI code generation tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor AI) as daily build accelerators — not novelties — across front-end, back-end, and configuration work 

  • Define and document ROOM42's AI-augmented build workflows for each deliverable type so the approach scales beyond a single practitioner 

  • Stay ahead of emerging agentic tooling (MCP servers, AI browser agents, generative UI frameworks) and evaluate when adoption creates genuine delivery leverage 

 

QA and Test Automation: 

  • Implement AI-assisted QA automation across ROOM42 project types — visual regression testing, accessibility scanning, cross-browser checks, and functional testing pipelines 

  • Establish a QA automation baseline for repeatable deliverable types (CMS sites, kiosk apps, email builds) so that human QA effort concentrates on edge cases and client-specific requirements 

  • Triage technical defects surfaced by QA — classify root cause, assign or resolve remediation, verify fix integrity before re-advancing to UAT  

Standards, Mentorship, and Team Health: 

  • Define and maintain ROOM42's technical standards across deliverable types — coding conventions, repo structure, accessibility requirements, security baselines, deployment protocols 

  •  Conduct code reviews for all ROOM42 developers before deliverables advance to QA; enforce standards consistently and use reviews as teaching moments 

  • Partner with RC's VP of Technology on standards alignment, tooling strategy, and team architecture as the practice scales 

  • Lead technical onboarding for new ROOM42 hires — tool access, standards orientation, and first-week productivity within two weeks of start date 

  • Serve as primary technical escalation point when blockers threaten delivery; resolve environment, integration, and access issues within 24 hours of identification 

 

Technical Delivery: 

  • Partner with Producers and TDMs on SOW scoping — translate creative and functional requirements into accurate technical estimates for hours, stack decisions, and phased rollout 

  • Own the technical delivery lifecycle for key ROOM42 engagement from kickoff through post-launch, work with technical delivery managers to ensure timeline integrity, milestone readiness, and handoff completeness 

  • Maintain a live view of technical progress across all active projects; proactively flag risks to Delivery Managers before they surface in status calls 

  • Drive milestone gates: work closely with QA lead to ensure that what moves from development to QA to UAT to production is actually ready — not optimistically ready 

  • Manage technical dependencies across concurrent projects (shared environments, overlapping APIs, licensing constraints) and surface conflicts before they collide 

  • Own technical documentation throughout each engagement: architecture decisions, environment setup, API integration specs, deployment runbooks — so no knowledge lives only in one person's head 

  • Participate in client-facing conversations where technical credibility matters — scoping sessions, risk discussions, demo walkthroughs — presenting clearly and without jargon 

 

Quality Outcomes: 

  • Define 'done' for every deliverable type — not just 'it works' but that it is performant, accessible, secure, cross-browser validated, and visually faithful to approved design 

  • Own quality accountability end-to-end: if something ships broken, looks wrong, or fails an MLR technical review, this role is accountable for the root cause and the remediation 

  • Work with QA lead to establish and maintain a ROOM42 quality checklist for each deliverable type — covering functional, visual, performance, accessibility, and security checks — so quality is structural, not ad hoc 

  • Review developer output not only for code correctness but for UX implementation fidelity: does the built experience actually look and behave like the approved design? 

  • Lead post-launch quality reviews on major engagements; document defect patterns and translate them into upstream process improvements 

  • Champion performance as a quality dimension: page load, animation smoothness, kiosk responsiveness, and interactive load times are quality metrics, not afterthoughts 

  • Maintain zero tolerance for preventable defects reaching client UAT — own the internal quality bar so clients aren't the ones finding the obvious problems 

 

Design Eye, UX/UI Partnership, and Creative Collaboration: 

  • Speak UX fluently — understand information architecture, user flows, interaction patterns, and content hierarchy well enough to actively contribute to UX decisions, not just receive them 

  • Evaluate wireframes and prototypes through both a user experience lens and a technical feasibility lens simultaneously: identify where a flow creates friction before it's built, and where a design pattern creates technical debt before it ships 

  • Read a Figma file not just for spec values but for design intent — understand what the designer was solving for and protect that intent through every build decision, especially when specs have gaps or edge cases aren't covered 

  • Catch UX implementation drift before QA does: spot when a multi-step interaction is off-sequence, a loading state is missing, an error condition is unhandled, or a mobile breakpoint breaks the intended user journey 

  • Catch visual implementation drift with the same discipline: notice when padding is off, a typeface is rendering incorrectly, a hover state feels wrong, or a component is pixel-perfect in isolation but contextually broken in the live layout 

  • Participating actively in UX and design reviews as a technical partner — able to say 'that interaction pattern will feel laggy on kiosk hardware' or 'here's how we can get the same UX outcome with a lighter implementation' or 'this flow needs an empty state that the design doesn't account for' 

  • Understand foundational UX/UI principles — user task flow design, progressive disclosure, feedback and affordance, responsive and adaptive layout, motion and timing — well enough to make confident decisions when the design file doesn't cover every scenario 

  • Bridge the gap between design and engineering vocabulary; translate UX intent and creative direction into precise technical implementation notes that developers can execute without ambiguity or interpretation risk 

  • Push back constructively when a UX or design spec is technically infeasible at the required timeline or budget — and always bring an alternative that preserves the experience intent, not just a 'no' 

  • Appreciate that in healthcare and pharma, the human story being told is someone's life — and that the quality of the experience we build, how it feels to use, how clearly it communicates, how gracefully it handles errors, is not separate from the mission 

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:  

  • ​Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.  

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.  

  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.  

  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.  

 

What you should have:   

  • 7+ years of hands-on development experience, with at least 3 years in a technical lead, staff engineer, or architect role 

  • Demonstrable full-stack proficiency — not a generalist who dabbles; someone who can build, review, and unblock at every layer 

  • A genuine design eye with UX/UI depth: able to evaluate user flows and interaction patterns for experience quality, read a Figma file for intent, catch UX and visual implementation drift, and make confident decisions at the design-code boundary without designer supervision 

  • Technical delivery experience: has owned milestone tracking, risk communication, and deployment readiness across concurrent projects — not just individual coding output 

  • Demonstrated accountability for quality outcomes: has owned defect triage, post-launch quality reviews, and upstream process improvements when things go wrong 

  • Active, daily practitioner of AI code generation tools (GitHub Copilot, Cursor AI, Claude Code) — able to define team-wide workflows around them 

  • Hands-on experience with Figma MCP server or comparable design-to-code AI tooling; familiar with design token standards and component handoff patterns 

  • QA automation experience: visual regression, accessibility automation, or AI-assisted test generation in a production environment 

  

Pay Range: $119,000 - $140,000

job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

AI Business Partner - Activation

Role Overview

The AI Business Partner translates business priorities into practical AI solutions that improve how work gets done. Sitting at the intersection of business strategy, domain expertise, and applied AI, this role identifies high-value opportunities, builds working prototypes and pilots, and partners cross-functionally to scale successful solutions.

This Partner will be aligned to Activation, a portfolio that spans media, social, content, creator/influencer/Starpower, and omnichannel. The work will vary across these areas and will be conducted in partnership with the designated business and discipline leads. Discipline leaders own business strategy, workflow priorities, functional requirements, stakeholder alignment and adoption within their respective capabilities. The Activation AI Business Partner brings applied AI and technical expertise to assess feasibility, prototype solutions, support operationalization and scale validated capabilities across Activation. The right person is comfortable moving between distinct disciplines with different maturity levels, tooling and ways of working, and can sequence where to focus first.

This role is ideal for someone who can move fluidly from ambiguity to action — working with stakeholders to define problems, rapidly testing ideas using modern generative AI tools, and helping the organization adopt AI in ways that are useful, responsible, and aligned with business needs.

What you'll do:

AI Opportunity Identification & Prioritization

  • Partner with business and discipline leaders to identify high-value opportunities to apply generative AI across workflows, deliverables, and business processes.
  • Translate business priorities, functional requirements and user needs defined with discipline leaders into clearly scoped AI use cases, pilots, and solution concepts.
  • Assess opportunities based on business value, technical feasibility, user needs, adoption potential, scalability and risk.
  • Partner with discipline leaders  to prioritize opportunities within individual capabilities and help sequence initiatives  across the broader Activation portfolio.
  • Maintain visibility across the Activation AI opportunity pipeline to identify shared needs, reusable components, dependencies and opportunities for cross-discipline scale

 

Prototyping & Solution Development

  • Build and iterate on working prototypes, pilots, and lightweight AI-enabled tools in response to business priorities and functional requirements established with business and discipline leads using modern development environments, LLM APIs, agentic workflows, and related technologies.
  • Design prompts, workflows, and tool interactions that guide AI behavior toward accurate, useful, and contextually relevant outcomes.
  • Test solutions quickly with representative users and discipline subject matter experts, incorporate user feedback, and refine prototypes based on real-world usage and evolving requirements.
  • Move ideas from concept to demonstrable value, balancing speed, practicality, technical feasibility, quality and responsible AI requirements.
  • Provide technical consultation during discovery to help discipline leaders distinguish between workflow, process, data, platform and AI-related needs

 

Cross-Functional Delivery & Scaling

  • Own the technical progression of validated concepts from discovery through prototype, pilot, handoff and scaling, in partnership with the appropriate teams (i.e., platform, data, security, governance teams, etc.)
  • Partner closely with AI technical teams, engineering, product, and business stakeholders to transition validated prototypes into scalable, production-ready solutions where appropriate.
  • Define technical requirements, solution dependencies, integration considerations and implementation paths in partnership with technical specialists.
  • Identify when an opportunity should be addressed through an existing enterprise capability, workflow redesign, vendor solution, configurable agent, lightweight prototype, or production-grade build.
  • Work with business and discipline leads to align on priorities, solution design, success metrics, rollout approach and post-launch ownership.

 

Adoption, Enablement & Change Management

  • Partner with discipline leaders to support successful adoption of AI solutions through solution-specific guidance, training, onboarding materials, and usage playbooks.
  • Communicate AI concepts, capabilities, and limitations in clear, accessible language for non-technical audiences.
  • Equip discipline leaders and subject matter experts with reusable materials they can adapt for role-specific training, change management, and workflow adoption.
  • Capture adoption feedback, usage barriers, and technical issues and translate them into product or solution improvements.
  • Help build AI fluency across the organization by enabling teams to use tools responsibly and effectively in their day-to-day work.
  • Foster a culture of experimentation, continuous learning, and practical innovation.

 

Governance, Quality & Responsible AI

  • Help ensure AI solutions are designed and applied in ways that are responsible, compliant, and appropriate for a regulated healthcare communications environment.
  • Incorporate considerations related to privacy, safety, quality, transparency, and human oversight into solution design and rollout.
  • Partner with relevant stakeholders to align AI use with organizational standards, governance expectations, and evolving best practices.
  • Promote thoughtful experimentation while maintaining appropriate safeguards and quality controls.

 

Domain Expertise Application

  • Apply working knowledge strong understanding of healthcare communications, including advertising, activation, communications, and medical domains, to shape relevant and impactful AI solutions.
  • Apply working knowledge of and demonstrate fluency in paid media, social, and influencer marketing — including the platforms, buying and measurement mechanics, and campaign workflows that drive day-to-day execution.
  • Partner with designated discipline leaders and subject matter experts for deep functional expertise, strategic judgement, workflow validation and quality assessment.
  • Understand how agency Activation teams operate, including campaign cycles, reporting cadences, client and platform dependencies, and where handoffs create friction.
  • Ensure solutions reflect real-world workflows, stakeholder needs, and the nuances of regulated client environments.
  • Translate domain knowledge into practical requirements that improve usability, relevance, and business fit.

 

What you should have:

  • Experience in AI innovation, product, or a related area.
  • Demonstrated experience in media, social, influencer, or adtech — agency-side, platform-side, or in an ad tech product/analytics role. This background is a priority for this position; the technical dynamics of media are difficult to learn quickly on the job.
  • Hands-on experience building, testing, and iterating on generative AI workflows, prototypes, copilots, agents, or similar solutions.
  • Proficiency with LLM APIs, prompting strategies, AI-assisted development environments, and modern tools used to prototype AI-enabled workflows.
  • Strong ability to translate ambiguous business needs into practical, testable AI use cases and solution concepts.
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with a proven ability to influence and collaborate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Strong problem-solving, prioritization, and execution skills in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.
  • Ability to evaluate solutions through the lens of usefulness, risk, quality, and business impact.

 

Skills and Competencies

  • Paid Media; Social Media; Influencer Marketing; Campaign Operations; Media Measurement & Analytics
  • Agentic Workflows; AI - Artificial Intelligence; Large Language Models (LLMs); Machine Learning
  • Coding; Programming Languages; Software Engineering
  • Product Demonstration; Technical Troubleshooting
  • Implementation Management; Solution Delivery; Solution Design
  • Client Relationship Management; Problem Analysis; Workflow Analysis

 

This position is crucial in driving the execution of AI strategies at Real Chemistry, ensuring that AI initiatives are not only innovative but also practical, effective, and aligned with real-world needs. The chosen candidate will play a pivotal role in enhancing the organization's capabilities and fostering a culture of AI-driven innovation and continuous improvement.
