job.title: Counsel
job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled. Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day. If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

Overview:

We have an exciting opportunity for an attorney to join the legal department at Skydance based at the Paramount Pictures studios in Los Angeles, with a focus on themed entertainment and live experiences businesses. The position will be an integral member of a team that provides day-to-day business and legal affairs services in support of experiences based on Skydance’s intellectual properties and brands worldwide, including in connection with theme parks, hotels, restaurants, live stage productions, immersive attractions and consumer products. The counsel will drive and close a variety of transactions, support a broad array of business and marketing initiatives and provide day-to-day advice to business and creative teams at all levels.  

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Draft and negotiate intellectual property license agreements, service agreements and other agreements in the global themed entertainment and experiences industry, such as theme parks, hotels, restaurants, live stage productions, concerts, and other immersive attractions and location-based entertainment experiences, as well as consumer products agreements
  • Provide practical, strategic and actionable advice and counsel to business clients regarding review of projects in development, risk allocation and legal implications of proposed business opportunities and actions
  • Communicate property rights analyses and handle rights acquisitions and third-party rights owner and talent relations where needed to execute business initiatives, including interaction with Broadway and film producers, third party rights owners and their representatives
  • Analyze motion picture and television production, financing and distribution agreements, as well as agreements with actors, writers, directors and producers
  • Review and provide guidance on design, creative and marketing materials
  • Interact with and maintain channels of communication with key legal and business affairs personnel, and outside counsel, in technical areas including insurance/risk management, compliance, production, marketing, rights and clearances, compliance, trademarks and enforcement, unions and guilds, bankruptcy, privacy, standards & practices, and litigation

 

Basic Qualifications:

  • License to practice law in the state of CA (and in good standing); or qualified to promptly register as in-house counsel
  • 4+ years of transferable legal experience (ideally with a major media or entertainment company and/or law company)
  • Must have experience managing transactional matters and dealing directly with clients
  • Excellent drafting and negotiating skills, with experience drafting and negotiating entertainment or intellectual property agreements (ideally in the media or entertainment industries)
  • Outstanding communication (written and oral), interpersonal, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail
  • Ability to build strong internal client and colleague relationships at all levels of the business, and successfully advise clients under conditions of uncertainty, high-pressure and/or high-risk and generate strong client satisfaction through quick turnaround, company decision-making and business judgment
  • Proficiency at multi-tasking under time strain, managing and prioritizing a varied, high-volume workload efficiently and accurately, and operating autonomously within corporate parameters
  • Exemplary time management skills
  • Ability to understand numbers in business/financial context
  • Ability to adapt legal work to a changing media and business landscape

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • The ideal candidate will be collaborative, positive, and team oriented. A sense of humor is a plus

 

About Skydance
Skydance is a next-generation global media and entertainment company, comprised of three business segments: Studios, Direct-to-Consumer, and TV Media. Skydance's portfolio unites legendary brands, including Paramount, Warner Bros., HBO and HBO Max, Paramount+, Pluto TV, CBS, CNN, CBS Sports, TNT Sports, Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, MTV, Food Network, BET, HGTV, and Comedy Central.

 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 

Hiring Salary Range: $139,200 - 174,000. 

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing compensation, or a range thereof, for roles where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on a variety of job-related factors, including but not limited to geographic location, external market data, internal equity, skill set, experience, training, education, and/or performance. Base pay is just one component of our total compensation package. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, short- and long-term incentives, and program-specific awards.
This position is bonus eligible.  

What We Offer:

  • Attractive compensation and comprehensive benefits packages. Check out our full list of benefits here.
  • Generous paid time off.
  • Complimentary subscriptions to HBO Max, Paramount+, and other Skydance streaming services and digital news products.
  • Robust employee engagement opportunities, including access to exclusive screenings and events, speaker series, volunteer activities and more.

 

Skydance is an equal opportunity employer (EOE)

 

We embrace the opportunity to build a workforce that reflects a wide array of perspectives, backgrounds and experiences. Being an equal opportunity employer means that we take seriously our responsibility to consider qualified candidates on the basis of merit. In line with the laws of the country or region in which the role is based, this includes consideration without regard to race, color, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship status, religion or belief, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, pregnancy, parenthood, physical or mental disability, genetic information, military or protected veteran status, union status or any other category protected by applicable law.

 

If you are a qualified individual with a disability, you may request a reasonable accommodation during the job application and/or recruitment process. You can request reasonable accommodations by calling 212.846.5500 or by sending an email to paramountaccommodations@paramount.com. Only messages left for this purpose will be returned.

job.title: Multiskilled Journalist
job.description:
About TEGNA

TEGNA Inc. helps people thrive in their local communities by providing the trusted local news and services that matter most. With 64 television stations in 51 U.S. markets, TEGNA reaches more than 100 million people monthly across the web, mobile apps, streaming, and linear television. Together, we are building a sustainable future for local news.

 

WWL WUPL-TV New Orleans, the CBS/MNTV TEGNA affiliate,  is looking for an experienced Multi-Skilled Journalist to help maintain our tradition of superior reporting and newsgathering. We are interested in finding a journalist who can create unique, memorable and well written stories, who can share them on all platforms with a mix of outstanding photography and unforgettable editing. If you're a creative storyteller who understands true multi-platform journalism and who is not bound by the methods of traditional TV news – we want to hear from you! 

Current driver's license and ability to operate news gathering vehicle to and from various locations is required.

Responsibilities: 

  • Perform authoritative, compelling live shots in a developing story or in breaking news situations
  • Develop story ideas
  • Mine the community to find sources who will keep you informed about events and ideas in their areas of expertise
  • Ability to identify, write and produce stories within a specific framework.
  • Research for facts and credibility.
  • Maintain and develop sources who will help bring our reporting to the next level.
  • Shoot, write, produce and edit on air and online content within deadlines.
  • Use creative production techniques such as graphics and new forms of media (viewer pictures, webcam interviews, etc.) to enhance stories.
  • Use social media and digital tools to research, discover and distribute content.
  • Attend editorial meetings and offer story ideas daily.
  • Write in an exciting, captivating and authentic manner.

Requirements: 

  • 1-3 years reporting experience preferred.
  • Must possess solid news judgment, display strong communication skills, creativity, and ethical decision-making skills.
  • Strong writing skills, production skills and tease writing abilities.
  • ENPS, EDIUS and Axis graphics experience is preferred.
  • Must be organized with the ability to work under constant deadlines.
  • Must be able to calmly handle live breaking news situations and changing events.
  • Proven social and digital content creation ability.
  • Knowledge of New Orleans a plus ​

Benefits: 

TEGNA offers comprehensive benefits designed to safeguard the physical, mental and financial health of our employees and their families. TEGNA offers two medical plan options for full and part-time employees through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Texas, as well as access to dental and eye care coverage; fertility, surrogacy and adoption assistance; disability and life insurance.

Our 401(k) program offers full, part-time and temporary employees the opportunity to contribute 1% - 80% of their pay on a pre-tax basis to TEGNA’s 401(k). Contributions made up to the first 4% of pay are eligible for a 100% match from the company and are 100% vested from day one.

Regardless of participation in TEGNA medical plans, ALL employees and their eligible family members receive nine free virtual doctor’s appointments with a physician through Teladoc, and 12 free annual therapy sessions with a licensed clinician through Spring Health.

TEGNA offers a generous Paid Time Off (PTO) benefit as well as nine paid holidays per year.

job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Application Deadline:

We'll close applications for the Manager, Inclusive Programs & Operations posting on Monday, November 9, 2026, at midnight Eastern.

Intro to Position

The Manager, Inclusive Programs & Operations is a hands-on program leader responsible for turning NPR’s diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility (DEIA) priorities into well-designed, successfully executed programs, learning experiences and strategic initiatives.

This role serves as a key operational partner to the Vice President of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, helping move high-level concepts into measurable delivery. Operating as an individual contributor, the Manager will develop project plans, establish timelines and milestones, coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, manage logistics and dependencies, track budgets and deliverables, identify risks, and ensure programs are successfully launched, implemented and evaluated.

The ideal candidate does not simply generate ideas; they build the systems, frameworks and operational discipline needed to turn ideas into sustainable programs. Whether standing up a new initiative from scratch, operationalizing a multi-day convening for Member Station leaders, or designing and facilitating an inclusive leadership workshop, this role balances strong program execution with thoughtful interpersonal judgment.

Responsibilities

  • Program Design& Operational Execution: Own the planning and implementation of DEIA programs and strategic initiatives from concept through completion. Translate strategic priorities into detailed project plans with defined milestones, deliverables, dependencies, resource allocations and measures of success.
  • Strategic Initiative Management: Partner closely with the Vice President of DEI to stand up new programs and initiatives, including cross-functional and externally facing projects. Develop the operational infrastructure necessary to move initiatives from initial concept through launch, implementation and evaluation.
  • Cross-Functional Departmental Coordination: Coordinate work across key departments such as the People Team, Newsroom, Audience Insights, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Procurement, Finance, Member Partnership and other teams. Establish clear roles and responsibilities and maintain communication throughout the lifecycle of an initiative.
  • External Partnership & Program Management: Support programs involving external organizations, universities, speakers, consultants, vendors and NPR Network partners. Coordinate partner communications, schedules, deliverables, agreements, logistics and follow-up necessary for successful execution. Serve as the central point of contact and operational advisor for Employee Resource Group (ERG) leaders, guiding them through charter development, strategic goal-setting, and budget reconciliation.
  • DEI Learning & Facilitation: Design, develop and facilitate DEI-specific learning experiences for employees, supervisors, executives and Network partners. Topics may include inclusive leadership, equitable feedback, navigating difference, psychological safety, accessibility, bias, organizational culture and other emerging workplace needs.
  • Convenings & Program Logistics: Operationalize large-scale programs, convenings and learning experiences by coordinating participant communications, agendas, speakers, facilities, technology, vendors, transportation, materials, registration and other logistical components.
  • Resource & Curriculum Development: Create practical resources, facilitator guides, trainings, toolkits, templates, and frameworks that translate DEIA principles into practices staff and leaders can apply.
  • Measurement & Continuous Improvement: Develop quantitative and qualitative measures of success for programs. Gather participant feedback, analyze outcomes, document lessons learned and recommend improvements for future iterations.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications

  • DEIA Program Experience: At least 5+ years of demonstrated experience designing or implementing diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility, organizational culture or employee-engagement initiatives.
  • Program and Project Management Experience: At least 5 years of experience developing, managing and executing complex programs, projects or initiatives involving multiple stakeholders, timelines and deliverables.
  • Building Programs From the Ground Up: Demonstrated ability to take a new idea or strategic objective and build the operational structure required to launch it, including workplans, timelines, stakeholder roles, communications, logistics and evaluation.
  • Training Development and Facilitation: Demonstrated experience designing learning content and facilitating workshops, trainings or discussions for employees, managers or organizational leaders.
  • Cross-Functional Stakeholder Leadership: Experience coordinating projects across multiple departments or functions, driving progress when participants do not directly report to the project lead, and managing relationships with senior leaders, employees, external partners, vendors, and community stakeholders.
  • Complex Event or Convening Management: Experience planning and executing large-scale convenings, programs, events or multi-session initiatives involving internal and/or external stakeholders.
  • Operational Problem-Solving: Strong record of identifying potential barriers, dependencies and risks and developing practical solutions before they disrupt project delivery.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Operational Translation: Exceptional ability to deconstruct complex, strategic priorities into clear, sequenced operational steps and detailed project management plans. 
  • Inclusive Coaching: Strong skill in providing constructive coaching and guiding managers on how to cultivate psychological safety within their teams.
  • Empathy & Candor: Excellent interpersonal skills with a proven capacity to build strong, trusted relationships across diverse groups while ensuring accountability.
  • Data Literacy: Comfort collecting, synthesizing, and interpreting qualitative feedback (surveys, focus groups) and quantitative metrics to continually iterate and improve programs.
  • Organizational Navigation: Strong capability to manage administrative processes, budget tracking, and governance guidelines within structured systems.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Organizational Development, Social Sciences, Communications, or a related field, OR equivalent work experience.

Work Location & Requirements

  • NPR Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. Some aspects of this role require duties better performed at an NPR facility. The employee will be required to be in the office at the Washington, D.C. location weekly. 

Job Type

  • This is a full-time, exempt position.

Compensation

Salary Range: The U.S.-based anticipated salary range for this opportunity is $142,500 - $158,500 plus benefits. The range displayed reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to provide for new hires for the position across all US locations.

NPR Benefits: NPR provides comprehensive benefits for employees and dependents. Regular, full-time employees scheduled to work 30 hours or more per week are eligible to enroll in NPR’s benefits options. Benefits include access to health and wellness, paid time off, and financial well-being. Plan options include medical, dental, vision, life/ accidental death and dismemberment, long-term disability, short-term disability, and voluntary retirement savings to all eligible NPR employees.

While our newsroom leadership focuses on the stories we tell, you will lead how, when, where, and to whom public media journalism is delivered and experienced across our nationwide network.

The ideal candidate sits at the intersection of executive media leadership, digital strategy, and network operations—scaling quality, editorial integrity, and audience reach by building a collaborative publishing framework that aligns, empowers, and coordinates NPR, Member stations, and affiliate partners. You will oversee enterprise content roadmaps and channel distribution strategies to maximize audience acquisition, reader/listener retention, and civic impact across owned properties, third-party platforms, and member newsrooms.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

Multi-Platform Distribution & Ecosystem Growth

  • Drive Enterprise Content Planning: Build and manage the enterprise-wide content roadmap, aligning daily news flow, major investigative series, podcasts, newsletters, and special projects across all publishing platforms to optimize newsroom capacity and audience engagement.
  • Execute Channel & Syndication Strategy: Oversee multi-platform distribution across owned digital properties (apps, web, newsletters) and third-party networks (search, social platforms, news aggregators, streaming platforms) while adapting to media consumption trends and algorithm shifts.
  • Lead Ecosystem Relationships: Build, maintain, and expand long-term executive relationships with publishers, digital-native media outlets, radio/TV syndicators, and non-profit journalism networks.
  • Optimize Audience Growth & Impact: Direct cross-functional initiatives with SEO, social media, and newsletter teams to boost discovery, retention, and measurable civic and journalistic impact.

Member Network Strategy

  • Architect Station Network Publishing: Design, govern, and scale the operational framework for network syndication, content sharing, joint reporting initiatives, and affiliate publishing across Member stations and affiliate newsrooms.
  • Cultivate Member Relationships: Serve as the central executive partner to station managers, news directors, and affiliate leaders, establishing partner advisory cadences and service standards that deliver maximum strategic value to Member stations.
  • Establish Impact & Performance Metrics: Partner with data and analytics teams to define network operational KPIs, content adoption metrics, and ROI frameworks, translating audience data into actionable strategic recommendations for editorial leadership.

Enterprise Infrastructure & Strategic Leadership

  • Modernize Publishing Workflows: Architect technology-enabled distribution workflows, enterprise CMS stacks, asset management repositories (DAM/MAM), and ethical AI tools designed for distributed network environments.
  • Manage Budget & Executive Alignment: Oversee the content operations and distribution budget, manage strategic resource allocation, and collaborate with Legal, Product, Tech, and Revenue leadership to preserve brand safety and organizational alignment.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

Minimum Qualifications 

  • 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in media strategy, content operations, audience development, or network distribution—ideally within a major newsroom, public broadcasting network, or federated media alliance.
  • Demonstrated expertise managing complex editorial calendars, media partner relationships, and multi-channel digital distribution mechanics (SEO, news aggregators, newsletters, social platforms, and streaming syndication).
  • Proven experience designing, scaling, and managing complex affiliate syndication systems, content-sharing networks, or federated member-station alliances.
  • Executive-level familiarity with enterprise publishing architecture, distributed CMS stacks, media asset management systems (MAM/DAM), and workflow automation.
  • Exceptional executive presence with a track record of building consensus, inspiring collaboration, and aligning independent station partners and cross-functional leaders around shared strategic goals.
  • Strong operational budget management experience with familiarity with network economics, membership models, or syndication structures.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Deep operational understanding of public radio, member-station governance, and federated media fundraising/licensing models.
  • Direct experience evaluating and implementing ethical AI, automated distribution tools, or next-generation media delivery frameworks within distributed media environments.

Required Skills/Competencies

  • Strategic Publishing Vision: Ability to bridge high-level editorial vision with operational execution, aligning enterprise storytelling with multi-platform delivery mechanics.
  • Federated Stakeholder Diplomacy: Exceptional interpersonal and negotiation skills to build trust, navigate federated governance structures, and align independent partners.
  • Data-Informed Editorial Judgment: Strong competency in translating quantitative audience analytics and qualitative metrics into strategic publishing decisions.
  • Executive Change Leadership: Proven capacity to guide teams through digital transformation, process modernization, and evolving media landscapes.
  • Mission-Driven Commitment: Passion for public-interest journalism, editorial integrity, and the vital role of news in a healthy democracy.

Education Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, Business Administration, or a related field, OR equivalent practical work experience demonstrating equivalent executive capability.

Work Location & Requirements

NPR and SAG-AFTRA Hybrid Permitted: This is a hybrid permitted role. The employee will be required to be in the Washington, D.C. office at least 3 days a week. The employee must also reside in Washington, D.C. / Maryland / Virginia.

Job Type

This is a full-time, exempt position.

Salary Range: The anticipated U.S.-based salary range for this opportunity is $290,000 - $ 350,000 plus benefits. The displayed range reflects the minimum and maximum salaries NPR expects to offer new hires for the position across all US locations.

Position Overview

The Manager of Content Operations will be responsible for managing the day-to-day delivery, readiness, and availability of PBS general audience video content across PBS owned-and-operated and third-party streaming platforms, including PBS.org, PBS apps, and YouTube. This role will oversee the workflows that move content from producer delivery through quality review, publishing, and ongoing library management, supporting both free and paid streaming experiences. Working alongside the other video operations roles, this role will translate programming schedules, content windowing policies, and platform strategies into reliable operational plans. The Manager will coordinate with PBS Programming, Technology, Digital & Marketing, and content management teams as well as PBS Distribution, and national producers to ensure content and supporting assets are complete, accurate, and available when audiences expect them.

Key responsibilities

will include, but are not limited to: Manage digital video delivery from intake through distribution, establishing schedules, confirming requirements, and coordinating dependencies across internal teams and external partners. Translate approved content windowing and platform plans into publishing requirements, including release dates, expirations, geographic restrictions, and access settings. Resolve discrepancies with the appropriate policy and rights owners. Oversee multiple versions of video assets and supporting materials, including captions, audio tracks, artwork, metadata, and platform-specific edits, ensuring the correct assets reach each destination. Manage operational readiness for premieres, library releases, and new distribution initiatives. Identify delivery risks early, communicate impacts, and coordinate contingency plans. Establish and maintain quality assurance procedures for video, audio, captions, and metadata. Coordinate corrections and verify that published content meets PBS standards and platform requirements. Maintain accurate asset records, delivery tracking, and streaming availability information across content and digital asset management systems. Lead troubleshooting of failed deliveries, publishing errors, and content availability issues. Coordinate resolution across teams, escalate risks, and address recurring causes. Develop and document processes that improve turnaround times, reduce manual work, and clarify

responsibilities

across Video Operations, Programming, Content Packaging, and platform teams. responsibilities

as assigned. undefined Requirements for success: Bachelor’s degree in communications, media production, technology, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Seven or more years of

experience

in digital video operations, media asset management, streaming distribution, or a related field, including responsibility for complex workflows and cross-functional projects.

Experience

with content management and digital asset management systems, including asset ingest, metadata, publishing, and library maintenance. Working knowledge of video formats, encoding and transcoding, captioning, audio specifications, and file delivery methods. Understanding of streaming platforms across web, mobile, and connected television, including YouTube publishing tools and operational requirements.

Experience

applying content rights, windowing restrictions, and platform specifications to distribution workflows. job.title: Senior Staff Editor, Off Platform Graphics
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The Graphics department at The New York Times seeks to hire an experienced and versatile senior visual editor to manage and execute the presentation of our graphics journalism in formats beyond nytimes.com, including social media, email newsletters and the print newspaper. This is a high-impact role designed for a senior journalist who wants to pioneer best practices and drive our off-platform visual storytelling.

You will guide the adaptation of complex graphics for audiences on social media, including Instagram, Facebook, X and other emerging surfaces. You will be responsible for coordinating strategy with the Social Visuals team and for assigning, editing and in some cases crafting graphics to meet that strategy, and help to do the same for Times newsletters, including The Morning and On Politics. And you will work with the Print Hub to coordinate production and edit graphics for the Times print edition.

You possess impeccable news judgment and have extensive experience creating and editing a wide range of types of information graphics. You operate with autonomy to proactively identify new opportunities to extend the reach of our journalism.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute unified visual styles that can effectively translate complex data, maps and diagrams into digestible, high-impact visual assets to fit a variety of formats.
  • Produce and edit news graphics under tight deadlines during breaking news environments.
  • Guide and edit the work of other visual journalists who translate interactives, spatial models and breaking news graphics into these formats.
  • Expertly and independently carry out all aspects of visual production, serving as the primary leader of all off-platform displays.
  • Work with the Social Visuals and Audience teams to direct the packaging of graphics journalism off-platform.
  • Maintain strong relationships and coordinate across other multidisciplinary desks (Graphics, Design, Video and the Print Hub) to track projects and establish publishing workflows.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a deputy graphics editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of professional experience producing and editing visual journalism or multimedia graphics at a major news organization.
  • Deep familiarity with visual storytelling devices, including a strong portfolio demonstrating hands-on execution of maps, charts, diagrams, 3-D modeling or motion graphics.
  • Expert proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (specifically Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects) and Figma.
  • Experience with creating, editing or art directing graphics for a print publication.
  • Strong writing and editing skills and experience synthesizing complex information and work on strict deadlines.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with reading and editing code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).
  • Familiarity with tracking off-platform traffic trends and optimizing display assets (headlines, thumbnails, custom visual cards) to maximize audience engagement.
  • Experience managing or guiding visual journalists.

The New York Times is looking for a Technical Product Manager II to shape product direction for Data Platform's Compute and Storage team. The team builds shared compute engines, lakehouse storage, and connective infrastructure so engineers can publish and own data products without managing the underlying platform.

You will partner with engineering, machine learning, analytics, and others across the company to deliver reliable, scalable, easy-to-use capabilities. You will make data infrastructure more accessible and efficient through reusable products for diverse workloads.

job.title: Product Manager
job.description:
The big picture: Axios is a media company dedicated to delivering trustworthy news and information with efficiency, clarity, and Smart Brevity. As a Product Manager, Revenue, you will independently lead features and projects of moderate complexity that grow Axios’ advertising business and create value for advertising partners.

Why it matters: You will turn advertiser needs and commercial opportunities into buyable products. Working with revenue, engineering, design, and editorial partners, you will take initiatives from discovery through delivery, using data and user research to guide priorities and measure results.

Responsibilities

In this role, you will make an impact at Axios with the following responsibilities:

  • Independently manage advertising product features and priorities from discovery through delivery.
  • Partner with revenue, engineering, design, and editorial teams to identify advertiser needs and translate commercial opportunities into clear product requirements.
  • Use data to guide priorities, measure performance, and improve advertising products across Axios’ properties and client base.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the internal tools, technology, and workflows that support the revenue organization.
  • Translate between commercial priorities and technical requirements, communicating clearly with different audiences.
  • Deliver high-quality features with minimal oversight and keep cross-functional partners aligned.
  • Use AI tools to improve the speed and quality of routine work, sharing effective prompts and workflows with peers.

Skills

Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit, a passion for Axios’ mission, and have the following skills:

  • Keen interest in commercial products that drive revenue growth for Axios
  • 5+ years of experience in product management or equivalent roles in technology, media, or SaaS. Experience in advertising or commercially focused product development is preferred.
  • Proven ability to independently manage features, projects, and quarterly priorities.
  • Experience launching commercially focused products and translating customer needs into solutions that drive revenue.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience using data to evaluate product performance and inform commercial decisions.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain business needs to technical teams and technical decisions to business stakeholders.
  • Experience conducting user research and translating findings into product requirements.
  • Fluency with AI tools to accelerate work and share effective use cases with peers.

What success looks like

  • High-quality delivery with minimal oversight and strong cross-functional alignment.
  • Clear communication that builds trust with stakeholders and peers.
  • Strong revenue partnerships that turn commercial needs into useful product solutions.
  • Continuous improvement of how you work, including using AI and embracing new ways of developing products

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $100,000 - $125,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. This range does not include other compensation benefits. Axios' compensation philosophy takes into account the cost of labor differentials across the country. Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

Axios is committed to embracing artificial intelligence as a core part of how we work. All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. We invest in ongoing learning to ensure every employee is equipped to responsibly and effectively integrate AI into their daily workflows.

job.title: Product Knowledge and Enablement Manager - AXS
job.description:
AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.  

The Role

The Product Knowledge & Enablement Manager creates clear, client-facing education for complex AXS products and workflows. This role strengthens the Knowledge Base as the primary self-service learning resource while supporting advanced client education, product adoption, GTM initiatives, and release communications. The role partners with Product, Product Operations, Ticketing Operations, Client Services, Account Management, Training, Documentation, and business unit stakeholders to convert complex product knowledge into searchable, actionable, and AI-ready content.

 

 

What you will do

  • Develop complex process documentation and workflow-based learning resources for assigned AXS products, services, and client use cases. Create playbooks, checklists, job aids, process guides, decision support materials, and other resources that help users complete work accurately and independently.
  • Improve the quality, structure, and usability of Knowledge Base content. Apply content standards, templates, taxonomy, metadata, tagging, lifecycle practices, and content consolidation strategies. Identify documentation gaps, duplicate guidance, outdated content, and failed-search topics.
  • Design and deliver advanced, client-facing product education and adoption activities. Facilitate product deep dives, feature education, office hours, workshops, and other learning experiences that support continued education and effective product use beyond initial onboarding.
  • Support product launches, releases, GTM initiatives, and product communications by translating product changes into audience-specific education plans and resources. Coordinate related KB content, Academy materials, webinars, job aids, and client-facing communications.
  • Use participation, search, content, support, and adoption data to evaluate the effectiveness of learning resources and recommend improvements. Maintain strong stakeholder relationships and communicate risks, priorities, and progress.

 

What we'd like to see

 

  • BA/BS Degree (4-year) Client education, product enablement, instructional design, training, communications, customer success, or a related field.
  • 5+ year's experience in product education, client enablement, technical writing, knowledge management, instructional design, product adoption, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting complex B2B software, SaaS, ticketing, venue operations, event operations, or another workflow-intensive technology environment.
  • Experience creating client-facing documentation, playbooks, job aids, workflow guides, learning content, or product adoption resources.
  • Experience supporting product releases, GTM initiatives, feature adoption, advanced training, webinars, or client workshops.
  • Experience with knowledge management, content lifecycle management, taxonomy, metadata, search optimization, or learning management platforms.
  • Experience using generative AI tools for content development, analysis, classification, or workflow improvement with appropriate human review.
  • Strong understanding of complex software workflows, business processes, user personas, and product adoption challenges.
  • Excellent technical writing, editing, presentation, facilitation, and plain-language communication skills.
  • Ability to create practical, audience-specific content, including articles, playbooks, checklists, job aids, tutorials, and learning resources.
  • Knowledge of information architecture, taxonomy, metadata, search optimization, content governance, and content lifecycle management.
  • Ability to structure accurate, current, searchable, reusable content for users and future AI-enabled search or chatbot experiences.

job.title: 21GRAMS- Group Copy Supervisor
job.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Group Copy Supervisor to join our growing team!  

The Group Copy Supervisor is a brand steward and category champion, responsible for having a deep understanding of the brand, its benefits, and competitive differentiation. Working with art partners and reporting to a Creative Director, the Group Copy Supervisor will own all day-to-day writing responsibilities for assigned healthcare/pharma-related HCP accounts. The ideal candidate will have the skills and experience to think strategically, supply creative ideas and concepts, and execute across a range of mediums.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

What you’ll do: 

  • Responsible for writing headlines and body copy for various types of digital tactics, including websites, interactive visual aids, videos, banners, landing pages, and emails, for branded and unbranded HCP clients
  • Convey scientific information into compelling and memorable messages for HCP campaigns
  • Champion creative thinking for campaigns and initiatives that advance creative strategy and brand personality
  • Prepare materials for client copy approval submissions, ensuring pieces are referenced and annotated according to AMA style, without supervision
  • Collaborate with Art Directors, Designers, and Developers from job initiation to digital deployment, and partner with Account and Strategy teams at all points
  • Ability to independently lead multiple projects, sometimes for different brands/industries
  • Clearly and expertly present work to clients and internal team members

This position is a perfect fit for you if: 

·  ​Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you. 

·  You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving. 

·  You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data. 

·  You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines. 

What you should have:  

  • 7+ years healthcare/pharmaceutical writing, preferably in an agency setting
  • College degree in a related field preferred
  • Experience writing for the healthcare/pharmaceutical industry
  • Portfolio or PDF of relevant work samples required

job.description:
iHeartMedia

                                                                             

Current employees and contingent workers click here to apply and search by the Job Posting Title.

                                                                             

The World's Largest Broadcast Software Provider.

 

RCS Worldwide is home to four industry-defining brands: RCS, Media Monitors, Mediabase, and Florical Systems — serving the broadcast, music, and media intelligence markets across 120 countries. Every day, thousands of radio and television stations around the world rely on RCS technology to stay on air, sound great, and compete in a rapidly changing landscape.

 

Here is what makes us different:

 

We are the company behind the scenes of media that billions of people consume every day. When a song plays on your favorite radio station, when a song charts in the music industry, when a TV network stays on air without a second of downtime — there is a good chance RCS technology played a role. Our portfolio touches every corner of the media ecosystem, from playout and music scheduling to international advertising intelligence and airplay analytics.

 

We are a global team passionate about the industry we serve and moving with the speed and ambition to lead it forward.

 

If this opportunity excites you, but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we encourage you to apply. At RCS Worldwide, we know that great talent comes from many different backgrounds and experiences. We're committed to building an inclusive, collaborative workplace where people can grow, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.

                                                                              

What We Need:

Florical Systems is hiring an Intermediate Software Tester to join the team responsible for developing and validating software used at the core of the world's largest and most recognized broadcast television operations.

As a Software Tester, you will evaluate the functionality, reliability, and performance of our software across a broad range of technologies. You will identify and investigate issues, clearly communicate your findings, and work closely with developers and other team members to help ensure our products meet the standards required for mission-critical broadcast environments.

This position provides an opportunity to expand your software testing and technical skills while gaining experience with the systems and technologies that support modern television operations.

This is a full-time, non-exempt position.

                                                                             

What You'll Do:

  • Develop and execute manual and automated test plans, test cases, and test scenarios for broadcast television software.
  • Perform functional, regression, integration, system, and exploratory testing.
  • Identify, reproduce, document, and track software defects through resolution using Atlassian Jira.
  • Verify software fixes and perform appropriate regression testing to identify unintended effects.
  • Analyze software and system behavior using application logs, diagnostic tools, SQL queries, databases, APIs, and other available data.
  • Write SQL queries and analyze SQL Server and MongoDB databases as part of software testing and troubleshooting.
  • Review and modify JSON, XML, and other configuration or data files used by the systems under test.
  • Deploy and configure software in containerized test environments and troubleshoot associated container platforms.
  • Install, configure, and troubleshoot broadcast industry equipment used in software test environments.
  • Install and configure COTS hardware used in test systems, including servers, network switches, and related equipment.
  • Configure and troubleshoot LAN connectivity and other networking required within non-production test environments.
  • Create documentation, as needed, including test results, defect details, procedures, and installation or configuration notes.
  • Collaborate with software developers, product owners, support personnel, and other team members to understand requirements, investigate issues, and validate expected behavior.
  • Participate in Agile development activities, including backlog refinement, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Contribute to the continued improvement of test processes, test coverage, automation, and product quality.

                                                                             

What You'll Need:

Skills and Experience

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, a related technical field, or equivalent relevant work experience.
  • Ability to develop and execute test cases and test scenarios from requirements, specifications, and expected system behavior.
  • Experience identifying, reproducing, documenting, and communicating software defects.
  • Working knowledge of LAN/WAN networking concepts, including TCP/IP and common network troubleshooting techniques.
  • Experience installing, configuring, and troubleshooting Windows operating systems.
  • Working knowledge of SQL or NoSQL databases.
  • Strong technical troubleshooting and analytical skills, including the ability to investigate application logs, configuration files, databases, and system behavior.
  • Ability to communicate technical information clearly and professionally in written and verbal form, including defect reports, test results, and technical documentation.

Preferred

  • Professional experience performing software testing, including functional, regression, integration, or system testing.
  • Experience working within a software development lifecycle and an Agile development environment.
  • Experience developing or maintaining automated software tests.
  • Experience with cloud platforms or cloud-based application environments.
  • Experience with or knowledge of a modern programming or scripting language, such as C#, Python, PowerShell, JavaScript, or similar.
  • Experience testing distributed, networked, real-time, or hardware-integrated software systems.

                                                                             

What You'll Bring:

                                                                             

Location:

Gainesville, FL: 4500 NW 27th Ave, Building B-1, 32606

job.title: Promotion Assistant
job.description:
Company Overview

Cumulus Media is an audio-first media company delivering premium content to a quarter billion people every month — wherever and whenever they want it. Cumulus Media engages listeners with high-quality local programming through 377 owned-and-operated radio stations across 84 markets; delivers nationally-syndicated sports, news, talk, and entertainment programming from iconic brands including the NFL, the NCAA, the Masters, US Soccer, and AP News, across more than 7,800 affiliated stations through Westwood One, a leading national audio network; and inspires listeners through the Cumulus Podcast Network, an established and influential platform for original podcasts that are smart, entertaining, and thought-provoking. Cumulus Media provides advertisers with personal connections, local impact and national reach through broadcast and on-demand digital, mobile, social, and voice-activated platforms, as well as integrated digital marketing services, powerful influencers, full-service audio solutions, industry-leading research and insights, and live event experiences. For more information visit www.cumulusmedia.com.


Position Overview

CUMULUS MEDIA | Syracuse is in search of a hard-working Part-Time Promotions Assistant. If you are looking to get a foot in the door to the radio industry, have an outgoing personality and have a passion for radio, this is a great opportunity for you! This job will consist of general office duties as well as going out into the community to interact with listeners and promote our stations.

 

The Promotions Assistant travels around the area and represents the Cumulus stations at specified events, acting as Brand Ambassadors. This includes set-up and breakdown of pop-up tents and tables, hanging banners, interacting with listeners and executing on-site activations. To join the team, you must be able to lift 50 pounds and be on your feet for extended periods of time.


In the office, the Promotions Assistant handles prize fulfillment, event preparation, contest building, attending weekly promotions meetings, posting on radio station social media platforms, brainstorming new ideas, and other promotion-oriented tasks. The position also includes running errands and helping with vehicle maintenance.


Would you describe yourself as an extrovert? Are you social media savvy? We’re looking for charismatic applicants, with smiling faces and outgoing personalities. If you love talking to people and listening to great radio, this could be the perfect job for you. If you desire a job where no day is the same as the last, this could be for you! This position is a great foot in the door to an exciting career in media!


Key Responsibilities & Qualifications

Key Responsibilities:

  • Assist in planning, organizing & execution of promotional events and digital campaigns
  • Execute proper technical and physical set-up and breakdown of remote broadcasts and station events; ability to troubleshoot and resolve issues on the fly
  • Represent stations at events in an upbeat, outgoing and friendly manner
  • Data Entry of Promotional events and contesting
  • Create e-blasts, social media posts & website posts; review promotional information and graphics
  • Inventory and maintenance of prize closet, calendars, events for current and upcoming promotions
  • Assisting the Promotions and Marketing Department with projects as needed in the office
  • Assist with vehicle inspections, fuel and coordinating maintenance
  • Ability to drive station vehicles with attached trailer
  • Maintain and storage of station equipment


Qualifications:

  • No experience necessary, however Customer Service experience helpful
  • Must have a valid driver’s license and clean driving record
  • Reliable; have a flexible schedule and be available to work at least 20 hours per week, including days, nights, weekends and holidays
  • May require lifting or moving up to 50 pounds
  • Must be able to stand for extended periods of time
  • Outgoing, energetic, detail-oriented and responsible
  • Proficient using computers and Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint
  • Multi-tasking abilities
  • Event experience a plus
  • Works well with a variety of personalities
  • Passion and desire to perform at a high level in a competitive environment
  • Positive attitude, even in stressful situations, is a must
  • Desire and bravado to share innovative ideas with team
  • Ability to ask for clarification, when needed
  • Strong Social Media skills

Pay Range

USD $16.00 - USD $16.00 /Hr.
What We Offer

  • Competitive Pay
  • Focused, responsible and collaborative work environment with the ability to ask, “what if” and try innovative solutions
  • 401K with company match


For immediate consideration, please visit: https://jobs.cumulusmedia.com/careers

 

For more information about Cumulus Media, visit our website at: https://www.cumulusmedia.com/


EEO Statement

CUMULUS MEDIA is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE).

Junior Broadcast Technician

Melfort, Saskatchewan

After an incredible 51 years of service, our longtime Technical Manager in Melfort has recently retired. Pattison Media is now looking for a Junior Broadcast Technician to join our Technical Services team and help support our two radio stations in Melfort.

This is a great opportunity for someone early in their technical career who enjoys troubleshooting, working with technology and learning how things work. You don't need to arrive knowing everything about broadcast engineering. You'll be supported by Pattison Media's Technical Services team and will work closely with our Technical Services Manager in Prince Albert, who will provide ongoing technical support and mentorship.

If you have a background in electronics, IT, networking, telecommunications or broadcast technology and are interested in building a career in radio broadcast engineering, we'd like to hear from you.

What you’ll do:

  • Help maintain, troubleshoot and repair studio and broadcast equipment.
  • Assist with the operation and maintenance of radio transmission systems.
  • Support computers, servers, network equipment and other technology used by our Melfort stations.
  • Support broadcast systems including WideOrbit automation and other studio, newsroom and audio systems.
  • Assist with the installation and commissioning of new technical equipment and systems.
  • Maintain technical documentation, records and drawings.
  • Help troubleshoot technical issues affecting our on-air and business operations.
  • Work with the Pattison Media Technical Services team on technical projects and upgrades.
  • Provide day-to-day technical assistance to staff at our Melfort stations.

What we’re looking for:

  • A genuine interest in broadcasting, electronics and technology.
  • Education or experience in electronics, electrical technology, IT, networking, telecommunications, broadcast technology or a related technical field.
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Basic knowledge of computers and networking.
  • Good organizational skills and an ability to follow tasks through to completion.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a larger technical team.
  • Good communication skills and a willingness to learn.
  • A valid driver’s License.

Broadcast experience is an asset, not a requirement.

Previous experience working in radio or with broadcast equipment would certainly be an asset, but we're also interested in candidates with strong technical aptitude who are willing to learn.

You'll have the support of an experienced Technical Services team and the opportunity to develop hands-on experience with studio technology, radio automation, IT and networking, RF transmission systems and other broadcast infrastructure.

If you're technically curious, enjoy solving problems and are interested in building a career in broadcast technology, we'd like to hear from you.

job.title: Promotions Director – Portland Media Group
job.description:
Looking for your next career move?

We’re Portland Media Group, and we’re hiring a Promotions Director to lead the promotions department for our eight radio brands.

This is a leadership role for someone who’s creative, highly organized and ready to turn ideas into events people remember. You’ll run every on-air and on-site promotion across our brands, from contests and remotes to concerts, community events and sponsor activations, taking each one from first idea to final recap.

You’ll work closely with our sales team to build promotions that deliver real results for clients and open doors with the business owners and decision makers they want to meet. If you enjoy big projects, tight deadlines and being part of a team that helps businesses succeed, you’ll thrive here.

You’ll work alongside our Director of Sales, Sales and Promotions Assistant and our Directors of Content from each radio brand to keep us front and center in the community. Our live events draw thousands of fans each year to raise money for local nonprofits and charities.

We’re what we call a Click, Visit, Call and Search media company. Our mission is simple: help our clients Get Wanted, Get Found and Get Chosen!

What we’re looking for:

3+ years in promotions, event marketing or a similar role; radio experience preferred but not necessary.

Strong planning and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple events and deadlines.

Proficiency with WordPress, website management, Photoshop and Illustrator or comparable tools.

Experience running targeted social media campaigns.

Excellent communication and customer fulfillment skills.

Familiarity with vCreative, vPromotions and Aptivada/Audience is a plus.

A love of live and recorded music.

Availability for evenings and weekends as events may require, a valid driver’s license and the ability to lift 50 lbs.

What you’ll do:

  • Plan and run radio brand promotions, contests, remotes and live events from start to finish.
  • Build sponsor packages with sales team and deliver what was promised on air, on site and online.
  • Host client events such as business breakfasts, VIP nights and concert hospitality that bring our sales team face to face with decision makers.
  • Keep brand websites current in WordPress and create graphics in Photoshop and Illustrator.
  • Run targeted social media campaigns for our brands and sponsors.
  • Write contest rules and ensure FCC, sweepstakes and brand policy compliance.
  • Manage prizes and fulfillment, the street team and the promotions vehicle.
  • Deliver sponsor recaps with photos, attendance and results.
  • Manage promotions budgets and vendor relationships.

What you’ll get:

  • $49,000–$54,000 annual salary, based on experience.
  • Health benefits, PTO, 401K and ongoing training.
  • A creative role at the center of our brands’ concerts, contests and community events.
  • A supportive team that wants to see you succeed.
  • Career growth opportunities within Portland Media Group.

Every day is different, every event is unique, and this is a place that invests in its people. We’re committed to your growth, and if that sounds like your kind of opportunity, let’s talk.

Send your resume and a quick note to Barry Gabloff, General Manager at talent@portlandmediagrp.com. We can’t wait to meet you!

WFSB is seeking a Social & Streaming Producer who will help WFSB break news, own the social conversation, and create content people actually want to watch. From turning breaking news into scroll-stopping vertical videos to producing YouTube livestreams and streaming shows, this role is built for someone who can move fast, think creatively, and deliver across platforms.

You’ll be part digital content producer, part social video creator, and part streaming show producer. If you’re passionate about YouTube, love breaking news, and want to push local journalism beyond the traditional newscast, we want to hear from you.

Duties/Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Think social first. Spot the moments, interviews and stories people need to see now, not hours later.
• Make YouTube a destination. Produce livestreams, create compelling thumbnails and headlines, and find new ways to grow views, watch time and revenue.
• Make shows happen. Book guests, develop topics, build rundowns, and produce live and recorded streaming shows from start to finish.
• Create what’s next. Pitch original social franchises, streaming series and documentary-style projects that go beyond the daily newscast.
• Own the details. Cut video for the web, create graphics and carousels, track performance, and keep content moving across platforms.
• Be a newsroom player. Work with reporters, anchors, producers and managers to turn good journalism into great digital storytelling.

Qualifications/Requirements:

• Strong vertical video editing and news judgment.
• Adobe Premiere skills and the ability to edit quickly under deadline.
• A working knowledge of TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and digital publishing.
• The ability to juggle breaking news, video production and show logistics without losing sight of the story.
• Creativity, initiative and a genuine obsession with what makes people click, watch and share.
• A passion for reinventing how local news reaches its audience.

The bottom line: We’re not looking for someone who just posts the news. We want someone who helps make the news impossible to miss — on social, on YouTube, on WFSB+ and everywhere our audience is watching.

job.title: Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer (External Agency Employee)
job.description:
NFL Films is seeking an experienced Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer to play a critical role in bringing our stories to life through sound. This position is responsible for crafting immersive, broadcast-quality audio experiences across a wide range of NFL Films productions, including documentaries, feature programming, branded content, commercial projects, and digital media.

Working at the intersection of storytelling and technology, the Associate, Post-Production Audio Mixer will lead all aspects of audio post-production, including dialogue editing, sound design, restoration, re-recording mixing, and final delivery. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong creative instincts, understanding how sound enhances emotion, reinforces narrative, and elevates the viewer experience.

Success in this role requires exceptional attention to detail, the ability to thrive in a collaborative and deadline-driven environment, and a passion for producing world-class content that reflects the quality and legacy of NFL Films.

This role compensates at $53 to $63 per hour for this long term, benefited contract engagement.  

Essential Functions

  • Perform dialogue editing, sound effects editing, restoration, and cleanup for a variety of NFL Films productions.
  • Create original sound designs that support and enhance storytelling objectives.
  • Execute re-recording mixes for documentary, long-form, short-form, commercial, and digital content.
  • Deliver final mixes and mix stems in accordance with production, broadcast, and distribution specifications.
  • Mix and deliver content in stereo, surround sound, and Dolby Atmos formats.
  • Utilize DaVinci Resolve Fairlight and other industry-standard tools to manage audio post-production workflows.
  • Apply advanced audio restoration and repair techniques utilizing tools such as iZotope RX.
  • Collaborate closely with producers, editors, composers, and other creative stakeholders to ensure audio elements align with the creative vision.
  • Troubleshoot technical and workflow challenges while maintaining project schedules and quality standards.
  • Manage multiple projects simultaneously while meeting demanding production deadlines.

Required Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Communications, Audio Engineering, Recording Arts, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Minimum of 10+ years of professional experience as a Sound Designer and/or Re-Recording Mixer in a post-production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience across documentary, sports, commercial, and long-form content production.
  • Advanced knowledge of mix stem creation and delivery workflows.
  • Extensive experience mixing in stereo, surround, and Dolby Atmos environments.
  • Strong understanding of digital audio workstations, audio signal flow, and contemporary post-production techniques.
  • Proficiency with audio restoration, repair, and cleanup tools, including iZotope RX.
  • Proven ability to maintain high-quality output while working under tight deadlines and shifting priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in sports, entertainment, or broadcast media environments.
  • Advanced proficiency with DaVinci Resolve Fairlight.
  • Familiarity with evolving audio standards and emerging post-production technologies.

Other Key Attributes

  • Strong creative instincts and a passion for storytelling through sound.
  • Collaborative team player with the ability to build effective working relationships across production teams.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Solution-oriented mindset with the ability to adapt quickly to changing priorities.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to remain composed and productive in fast-paced production environments.

Terms / Expected Hours of Work

  • In-office position.
  • Standard schedule averages 40 hours per week.
  • Must be available to work early mornings, evenings, weekends, extended hours, and other non-standard schedules as required by production demands and delivery deadlines.
  • This job posting is for a position with one of the NFL’s third-party agency partners that provides services to the NFL. The individual selected for this role will be an employee of that third-party agency and not the NFL. All compensation, benefits, and other terms and conditions of employment are handled by the agency. The assignment to provide services to the NFL will be limited in duration but may be extended for an additional period by agreement between the NFL and the agency.

This job posting contains a pay range, which represents the range of salaries or hourly rates that the NFL believes, in good faith, at the time of this posting that it might be willing to pay for the posted job. The NFL expects to hire for this position near the middle of the range. Salary $53—$63 USD

At the NFL, in-person work at our offices is a top priority because it allows us to collaborate more effectively, build stronger connections, and maintain the culture that drives our success. Develop and implement marketing and promotions campaigns, along with the Championship Director, and/or PGA contracted marketing agencies, to enhance Championship sales and overall multi-channel marketing strategies.

Development and activation of approved local corporate partnerships to grow both quality and quantity of ticketing database, and ultimately sales from it.

In conjunction with the Corporate Hospitality Sales staff Identify companies in the local and regional market who are possible new clients. 


Assist the Corporate Hospitality Sales/Services staff with all steps in the sales and services process by coordinating production of sales collateral, sending mass mailings to potential and current customers, sending/receiving letters of intent, contracts, collecting payments, sending gifts and invitations, etc. 


Serve as the primary administrative on-site contact for all Club Member ticket purchasers and assigned corporate clients. 


Respond to consumer inquiries and requests for assistance. Answer day-to-day operational and administrative questions. 


Make sales appointments with corporate prospects, including setting up sales calls and mailing correspondence and sales materials. Respond to public inquiries and requests for information and offer course tours. 


Coordinate and support all on-site corporate hospitality special events (i.e. Corporate Hospitality Launch, Corporate Cup, and Ticket Distribution). 


Work closely with various staff at PGA Frisco (Ticket Center, Integrated Marketing, PGA Interactive, Promotions, Media, etc.) in order to ensure compliance with PGA guidelines.


Work in conjunction with the Corporate Hospitality Sales/Service Staff to prepare for Championship week, work with outside vendors and staff to determine materials/equipment needed; necessary signage; order office supplies; organize and schedule venue inspections with clients; delivery of Championship Journals, brochures and information to each venue around the course; coordinate hospitality staff and volunteers. 


Provide Championship Director with regular updates on pending and completed Club Member ticket sales. 


Work with the Championship Director to complete weekly and monthly tasks on a timely basis. 


Assist the Corporate Hospitality Sales Staff in supporting the Championship Sales Committee, by attending meetings, assisting in the preparation of agendas, notifying committee members of meeting dates/times, reserving space and refreshments for meetings, following up with committee members on clients they have contacted, etc. 


Help establish, maintain, and foster Club and Community relations, specifically while the Championship Director is off-site.


Assist with preparing, monitoring and administering an annual budget, while following all financial policies established by The PGA of America (i.e., purchase requisition, purchase orders, check requests, bid proposals, etc.). 


Assist in the recruitment and management of Corporate Hospitality Assistants / Interns.

job.title: Lead Machine Learning Operations Engineer
job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled.

 

Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day.

 

If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

Lead Machine Learning Operations Engineer
Personalization & Recommendation Systems


Overview
We’re hiring a Lead Machine Learning Operations Engineer to own the operational excellence, observability, reliability, and governance layer around our personalization and recommendation ML systems. 

Our recommendation models retrain and deploy frequently. You will define how we detect model behavior changes, diagnose issues quickly, and prevent bad deployments from reaching customers.


This is a lead-level IC role: you’ll set technical direction and drive adoption across ML Engineering, DevOps, Platform Engineering, Data Engineering, and Product.


Sitting within ML Platform and Infrastructure, you’ll partner closely with ML engineers who own model development. You’re not expected to build infrastructure from scratch, but you’ll define what good looks like, evaluate tooling, and own the day-to-day operational layer.


What You’ll Do

Own ML production reliability strategy

  • Define and lead the operational strategy for production ML systems, including monitoring, traceability, deployment safety, incident response, and post-deployment validation.

  • Set the standards ML teams use to assess model health, performance, and trustworthiness in production.

Own model traceability and governance

  • Ensure every production model has clear lineage (data, features, code, artifacts, validation, deployment history) and drive adoption of model registry and metadata tooling across ML teams.

Build end-to-end ML observability

  • Design and implement monitoring across the full ML signal path: data arrival, feature freshness, distribution stability, candidate generation, ranking behavior, model metrics, serving latency, and SLA performance.

Define production health metrics

  • Partner with ML, data, product, and business stakeholders to define post-deployment metrics covering model quality, system reliability, business guardrails, and degradation indicators.

Detect drift and degradation proactively

  • Detect data drift, feature drift, model behavior changes, and silent failures before they impact customers via thresholding, alerting, anomaly detection, and release-over-release monitoring.

Lead diagnostic tooling and root-cause analysis

  • Build dashboards, logs, and diagnostic workflows that progress quickly from “recommendations look off” to root cause, with context captured across candidates, features, scores, ranking decisions, and downstream outcomes.

Own ML deployment safety

  • Define and operate automated gates that prevent bad models or bad data from being promoted to production. Partner with MLEs to establish validation checks, rollback criteria, canary strategies, shadow testing, and release health reviews.

Lead ML incident response

  • Own incident response practices for ML systems, including rollback playbooks, hotfix strategies, severity definitions, tradeoff frameworks, communications, and post-mortems. Drive closure of systemic gaps after incidents rather than only resolving the immediate issue.

Partner across ML Platform, Data, and ML

  • Partner with DevOps/Platform on infrastructure and observability needs; with Data Engineering on data quality, drift, and freshness; and with ML Engineering to embed operational requirements into development and deployment workflows.

Set standards and mentor others

  • Act as the technical lead for ML operations: establish reusable patterns, playbooks, and standards, and mentor engineers on reliability, observability, and operational rigor.


Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in machine learning engineering, ML platform, applied ML, MLOps, data platform, reliability engineering, or a related technical role.

  • Demonstrated experience operating production ML systems, including monitoring, deployment, incident response, model validation, data quality, or reliability ownership.

  • Experience leading technical initiatives across multiple engineering teams, especially where success required influencing architecture, tooling, standards, or adoption.

  • Hands-on experience with model registries, feature stores, ML metadata systems, production monitoring, model deployment pipelines, or ML observability platforms.
