job.description:
Storytelling is, and will always be, the heart of what we do at Skydance.
Our vision is to build a thriving entertainment ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced. We create for every age and audience, anchored by the strength of our content and experiences and the depth of our connection with fans. We are creator-first, audience-focused, tech-forward, globally scaled. Here, you’ll work with talented teams that move fast, think boldly and collaborate with purpose to deliver results. We aim high, champion the best ideas and win together, earning the trust of our employees, creators, partners and audiences every day. If you’re energized by the opportunity to help build the next-generation global media and entertainment company powered by creativity and technology, we’d be thrilled to welcome you aboard. LET’S GO!

 

Overview:

If you thrive at the intersection of dealmaking, financial analysis, and creative judgment, this role is for you. We’re hiring a Director, Acquisitions to help shape Paramount Picture’s film slate. This role sits at the center of the studio’s acquisitions strategy, structuring and negotiating deals while partnering closely with finance and legal to evaluate opportunities across the global marketplace. You’ll build deep familiarity with the studio’s output and licensing deals, and use that knowledge to identify commercial opportunities that align with our broader strategy.   You will be the studio’s presence at major festivals and markets, including Sundance, Cannes, TIFF, and AFM, leading internal prep, briefing the EVP, and representing Paramount directly in conversations with filmmakers, producers, and sales agents. Beyond the deal, you’ll stay involved through post-production, offering creative feedback on cuts, and you’ll drive cross-departmental coordination through mastering, marketing, distribution, and publicity to ensure a successful launch.   This role requires someone who can move fluidly between financial rigor and creative instinct, with the relationships and market fluency to spot opportunities.  

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: 

  • Structure, negotiate, and execute acquisitions deals, utilizing financial analysis and strategic insight in partnership with finance and legal teams
  • Lead financial evaluation of acquisition opportunities, partnering with finance to build and analyze P&L models to inform valuation and overall deal strategy
  • Maintain deep familiarity with the studio’s global output and licensing deals and leveraging them effectively in the evaluation of acquisition opportunities worldwide
  • Lead sourcing, tracking, and evaluation of packages across the global marketplace, identifying commercial opportunities aligned with the overall acquisition strategy
  • Maintain and cultivate strong relationships across agencies, financiers, filmmakers, producers, and international sales companies to gain access to high-level acquisition opportunities
  • Lead internal preparation for major film festivals and markets (e.g., Sundance, Cannes, TIFF, AFM), including identifying priority titles, coordinating team coverage, and preparing the EVP with relevant materials and market intelligence to align internal stakeholders around acquisition targets
  • Represent the studio in market-facing conversations at festivals and markets, attending screenings and meetings with filmmakers, producers, and sales agents to evaluate opportunities and communicate the studio’s acquisition priorities
  • Provide strategic guidance and creative feedback to filmmakers and producers on acquired projects, including reviewing cuts during post-production and collaborating with creative stakeholders to help shape the final film
  • Maintain deep familiarity with the domestic and international sales landscape, sourcing market intelligence on upcoming projects and monitoring buyer sentiment
  • Oversee the lifecycle of acquired titles from acquisition through release, driving cross-departmental coordination across mastering, marketing, distribution, publicity, and legal to ensure timely delivery, optimal windowing strategy, and successful launch
 

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in film, Business, Media, or a related field
  • 8+ years of experience in film acquisitions, distribution, or sales, preferably with a major studio or agency

 

Additional Qualifications:

  • Strong analytical and financial modeling literacy, with the ability to interpret P&L projections and apply financial insights to acquisition decision-making
  • Established industry relationships across the creative and sales communities
  • Strong understanding of the global film marketplace and distribution landscape
  • Proven ability to evaluate material, talent packages, and market dynamics through both a creative and commercial lens
  • Exemplary written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to interface effectively with senior leadership as well as external partners

job.title: Senior Vice President, NPR Content Strategy & Business Development
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

We are seeking a strategic, deal-driven SVP of Content Strategy & Business Development to lead the strategic expansion of our editorial reach and enterprise distribution. Reporting directly to the Chief Content Officer, this executive will serve as the primary architect and operator of our external partnership strategy. You will bridge the gap between our content production and revenue growth—identifying, negotiating, and executing strategic alliances with digital platforms, streaming networks, audio networks, and mission-aligned distribution partners.

In addition to structuring external partnerships, you will collaborate closely with enterprise stakeholders across the organization to standardize operational frameworks, direct the division’s OKR planning, and align resource allocation directly with Content’s overarching strategic objectives.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.    

Responsibilities

Strategic Business Development & Monetization

  • Drive Partnership Revenue: Pitch, negotiate, and close high-value content distribution, co-production, and IP licensing deals for network content across platforms.
  • Expand Distribution Channels: Identify and secure deal structures with major digital news aggregators, streaming platforms, newsletter networks, and public media systems to scale audience reach and maximize revenue.
  • Innovate Business Models: Work alongside the CCO to design business models (e.g., enterprise member subscriptions, content licensing, revenue-share frameworks) that bring financial sustainability to NPR and the Network.

Partner Management & Strategic Alliances

  • Co-Production & Joint Ventures: Structure operational agreements for collaborative, multi-newsroom reporting initiatives to ensure partner alignment while protecting editorial standards.
  • Cross-Sector Alignment: Collaborate with executive leadership to identify grant-funded or corporate-sponsored distribution initiatives that support the organization's broader mission.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Execution

  • CCO & Newsroom Partnership: Partner with the Chief Content Officer and network editorial leads to ensure business development strategies protect editorial standards and elevate network priorities.
  • Deal Structuring & IP Oversight: Manage the contract lifecycle, intellectual property rights, licensing terms, and revenue-sharing mechanisms in collaboration with legal counsel.
  • Metrics & Strategy Iteration: Track partnership performance, audience expansion, and net revenue to regularly present actionable pipeline insights to the CCO and executive team.

job.title: Vice President, Talent Strategy
job.description:
OVERVIEW

A thriving, mission-driven multimedia organization, NPR produces award-winning news, information, and music programming in partnership with hundreds of independent public radio stations across the nation. The NPR audience values information, creativity, curiosity, and social responsibility – and our employees do too. We are innovators and leaders in diverse fields, from journalism and digital media to IT and development. Every day, our employees and member stations touch the lives of millions worldwide. 

Across our organization, we’re building a workplace where collaboration is essential, diverse voices are heard, and inclusion is the key to our success. We are committed to doing the right thing in our journalism and in every role at NPR. This means that integrity, adherence to our ethical standards, and compliance with legal obligations are fundamental responsibilities for every employee at NPR.

Intro to Position

Reporting directly to the Chief Content Officer (CCO), the Vice President of Talent Strategy serves as the principal architect, relationship builder, and strategic scout for creative, journalistic, and host talent across NPR. In this role, you will work side-by-side with the CCO and editorial leadership to align talent acquisition, career stewardship, and creator partnerships directly with NPR’s long-term multimedia vision.

You will nurture trusted relationships with our established roster of award-winning journalists, hosts, and commentators while proactively identifying, evaluating, and attracting emerging voices from independent media, podcasts, newsletters, and digital platforms. Serving as an executive bridge across Content, People, Legal, and Member station network, you will champion a collaborative environment where exceptional storytellers can thrive and expand public media's reach across platforms.

This is an NPR editorial role covered under the terms of the NPR Ethics Handbook. All editorial staff are bound by this guidance. Editorial staff is defined as staff members who play a role in shaping the journalistic or creative direction of NPR's content, including events.

Responsibilities

  • Executive Talent Relationship Management: Serve as the primary executive liaison and trusted advisor to high-profile journalists, hosts, and creative contributors, cultivating sustainable career pathways and retention strategies in close collaboration with the CCO.
  • Talent Scouting & Pipeline Development: Design and lead a comprehensive discovery strategy across traditional broadcast, podcasting, newsletter platforms, social ecosystems, and independent journalism to build an ongoing, diverse pipeline of on-air and digital talent.
  • Cross-Functional Mediation & Advocacy: Act as the central connective tissue between creative talent, talent representatives (agents, managers, attorneys), and internal executive teams (People Team, Legal, Marketing, and Operations) to align individual goals with organizational priorities.
  • Complex Contract Structuring & Negotiations: In close coordination with the CCO, Legal, and People teams, oversee talent agreement frameworks, leading contract renewals, compensation structures, and rights agreements with precision and diplomatic finesse.
  • Editorial Standards & Mission Alignment: Ensure all talent recruitment, onboarding, and partner strategies rigorously reflect NPR’s core mission, journalistic ethics, and commitment to public service.
  • Audience Forecasting & Metric Analysis: Partner with Content Insights and divisional leadership to evaluate audience consumption trends and identify future talent requirements across evolving media such as video, episodic audio, and experiential storytelling.
  • DEI Talent Initiatives: Systematically embed diversity, equity, and inclusion principles into every phase of talent identification, pipeline cultivation, and retention.

The above duties and responsibilities are not an exhaustive list of required responsibilities, duties and skills. Other duties may be assigned, and this job description can be modified at any time.

  • Proven track record of structuring and negotiating complex, multi-party talent contracts, intellectual property rights, and compensation agreements in compliance with organizational policies.
  • Demonstrated success building and sustaining diverse, multi-perspective talent rosters that engage cross-generational and culturally diverse audiences.

job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team

The Brand and Experiences group plays an integral role in positioning the company for advancement and growth. We are responsible for the outward expression and inward embodiment of our Brand.  We develop the core capabilities, tools, and assets required to extend the Brand and empower GTM functions across the business by activating the Brand through campaigns, events, sponsorships, and tradeshows.  We do this by partnering with other areas of marketing, product, and sales groups to create high-impact opportunities to grow subscribers, sponsors, and accelerate the growth agenda.


The organization consists of a number of key, senior-level COE roles in areas such as Brand and Experiential Marketing, as well as senior capability leads. Together, this team will collaborate to build a unified, scalable, and consistent approach to marketing the brand to create awareness and drive preference.


About the Role

In this role, you will help strengthen how Brand operates and partners with the broader business by supporting the design, implementation and continuous improvement of Brand's operating model, processes and ways of working.


This role will partner closely with Ops leadership to understand business needs, assess Brand's capabilities, identify operational gaps, and translate those insights into practical processes, RACI, engagement models and enablement.


You Will:

Business Enablement

  • Partner on discovery with business units to understand their needs, workflows, pain points and opportunities to improve how they engage Brand.
  • Help define and communicate how and when teams should engage Brand, including the types of support and capabilities Brand provides.
  • Develop and maintain RACI, decision rights, engagement models and ways of working with key business partners.
  • Develop roadshows, playbooks, onboarding and other enablement that make it easier for teams across the business to understand and work with Brand.

Brand Capabilities & Insights

  • Help build and maintain a clear view of Brand's capabilities, services and outputs.
  • Gather and analyze information through surveys, workflow and asset analysis, stakeholder feedback and other sources to understand how Brand's capabilities are being used.
  • Identify capability gaps, recurring needs and opportunities to evolve how Brand supports the business.
  • Translate insights into recommendations for processes, ways of working and future capabilities.

Creative Operations & Process Improvement

  • Map current-state workflows and help design improved future-state processes.
  • Identify friction, unclear handoffs, unnecessary approvals and gaps across the creative lifecycle.
  • Develop and implement improved workflows, governance, RACI, escalation paths, SLAs and operating cadences.
  • Ensure operational processes support the realities of strategy and creative development while improving clarity, consistency and speed.

Tools & Technology Enablement

  • Help identify tools and technology that could improve Brand's workflows, creative processes and operational effectiveness.
  • Evaluate existing enterprise capabilities and emerging solutions, including opportunities to leverage AI and automation.
  • Partner with internal teams such as Technology, Procurement, Legal and Compliance, as well as external vendors, to understand requirements and support implementation of new capabilities.
  • Coordinate pilots, onboarding, training and adoption of new tools and features across Brand.
  • Partner with vendors such as Asana and existing enterprise technology partners to understand available capabilities and identify opportunities to improve how Brand works.
  • Track adoption and feedback to determine whether new tools are delivering the intended operational value.

Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Support the ongoing evolution of Brand's operating model as business needs and capabilities change.
  • Monitor how new processes and ways of working are performing and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Pilot new approaches, gather feedback and support implementation and adoption.
  • Maintain the playbooks, standards and operating frameworks that enable consistent ways of working across Brand.
  • Help measure whether operating-model changes are improving clarity, collaboration, speed and effectiveness.

You Have:

  • 10+ years of experience in creative operations, production operations, workforce planning, or a related function, including experience operating at a senior manager level or equivalent scope.
  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional initiatives, partnering with senior stakeholders to assess business needs, align priorities, and drive organizational change.
  • Proven ability to design, implement, and optimize operating models, workflows, and processes, translating complex business challenges into scalable solutions that improve efficiency and effectiveness.

job.title: Congressional Reporter (5-month contract)
job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.

Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is seeking a sourced, creative and high-energy reporter to cover the U.S. Senate on a temporary basis.


This is a full-time, approximately five-month assignment filling in for a member of our Congress team who will be on parental leave. The temporary contract position is expected to begin Nov. 30.


We are looking for an aggressive and versatile journalist who can hit the ground running on one of Washington’s most competitive beats. The successful candidate will know how to cultivate sources, break news, explain complex policy fights and demystify the sometimes arcane workings of the Senate — from reconciliation and the filibuster to holds, confirmations and floor procedure — for a broad audience.


The ideal candidate has a proven ability to deliver agenda-setting reporting and a clear sense of how to tell stories about Congress that resonate well beyond Washington. This reporter will illuminate the personalities, power struggles and policy battles shaping the Senate, bringing authority and insight to consequential developments while finding opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting. We are looking for someone who can deploy seriousness, wit and narrative flair as the story demands.


This position is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You

  • You are driven to break news and compete aggressively on one of Washington’s most consequential beats.
  • You thrive on cultivating sources and uncovering what is happening behind the scenes.
  • You enjoy making complicated legislative and procedural fights clear and compelling for a general audience.
  • You are fascinated by the personalities, alliances and power dynamics that shape the Senate.
  • You are collaborative and eager to contribute immediately to a high-performing team.

How You’ll Support the Mission

  • Work collaboratively with The Post’s Congress team to make what happens in the Senate — and how it affects people across the country and around the world — interesting and accessible to a broad audience.
  • Break news on senators, Senate leadership, key committees and the political and policy dynamics driving the chamber.
  • Quickly develop and maintain sources among senators, aides, committee staff, administration officials, activists, lobbyists and others seeking to influence the Senate.
  • Cover major policy and procedural fights, including legislation, nominations and confirmations, explaining both the political stakes and real-world consequences.
  • Track the relationship between the Senate and other centers of political power, including the House, White House and federal judiciary.
  • Identify opportunities for enterprise and accountability reporting, including potential conflicts of interest, misconduct and abuses of power.
  • Produce fast, authoritative journalism as news develops while pursuing original reporting that distinguishes The Post’s coverage.
  • Adhere to the highest ethical standards, ensuring fairness, rigor and meaningful opportunities for subjects of our reporting to respond.
  • Think creatively about the best formats for our journalism, collaborating with data reporters, graphics journalists, photographers, designers and video journalists to maximize impact.

The Skills and Experience You Bring

  • At least five years of experience covering Congress, another legislature or a similarly competitive political or government beat, with a track record of breaking impactful stories.
  • Experience covering the Senate is strongly preferred.
  • Existing Senate sourcing and familiarity with Senate rules, institutions and procedure that would enable you to contribute quickly are significant advantages.
  • Demonstrated ability to report and write breaking news with speed, clarity and precision.
  • Strong source-building skills and an instinct for original and consequential reporting.
  • An ability to explain complicated policy and procedural matters without resorting to insider language.
  • Excellent news judgment and the ability to balance the demands of daily coverage with enterprise and accountability reporting.
  • An eagerness to collaborate with colleagues across a competitive, fast-moving newsroom.
  • A commitment to accuracy, fairness and the highest standards of journalism.

Interested candidates should upload a cover letter, résumé and three examples of their work (as PDFs) to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Nov. 1 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Deputy Congress Editor Sean Collins, Congress Editor John Wagner, Deputy Politics & Government Editor Jen Liberto and Politics & Government Editor Nick Baumann.


This is a full-time contract position expected to begin Nov. 30 and last approximately five months while a member of the Congress team is on leave. It pays between $8,000 - $10,000 per month, depending on experience level and qualifications.

  Your story awaits. Apply today!

Learn more about The Post at careers.washingtonpost.com.

About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

This role is fundamental to the core of the Audience Development and Media Buying team within the Digital Marketing department of Columbia Records. The manager will own the planning and execution of paid digital ad campaigns in collaboration with the project manager and artist teams, with a concentration on D2C growth and efficiency. Just as crucial, the manager will immerse themselves in the fanbase of their roster of artists, helping to ideate and execute campaigns to build fan communities, including a focus on qualitative audience knowledge, first party data capture, and subsequent usage of that data in marketing. Creativity, attention to detail, and data acumen are essential to this role. The ideal candidate will have a passion for music, fan culture, and analytics.

What you'll do:

  • Out of Home Planning. Weave out of home placements into the marketing mix, complimenting IRL and digital activations through a creative and geo-targeted lens.

  • Fan Building Data Initiatives. Ideate and integrate fan data acquisition initiatives into digital marketing plans with an eye towards long term fan journeys.

  • Content Ideation. Help brainstorm content ideas for bespoke advertising objectives, incorporating real-time trends into creative campaigns.

  • Reporting and Storytelling. Synthesize campaign insights for senior management and artist teams; derive narrative from numbers; own reporting templates and innovate tracking documentation.

  • Resource building. Learn existing tools to streamline digital media processes and explore new platforms to further innovate workflow.

  • Billing reconciliation. Coordinate billing reconciliation and invoice fulfillment for digital advertising partners.

job.description:
The Orchard have an exciting opening for a Solutions Manager to join us in the Johannesburg offices.

The Solutions Manager is responsible for the end-to-end operational onboarding of clients , content management, and synthesizing all back-office inquiries to resolve administrative and operational issues efficiently and accurately. 

You will serve as the primary client-facing representative for backend teams - including Legal, Finance, and Operations - this role ensures seamless account setups, catalog ingestions, and digital rights workflows.

You will work closely with the Relationship Management team and Operational Support. As Solutions Manager you will navigate complex technical platforms to advocate for client needs, maintain catalog integrity, and manage the full client lifecycle through offboarding.

The Orchard team meet in the office Monday- Thursday.  Most teams usually work remotely on Fridays.

Client Onboarding & Lifecycle Management

  • Collaborate closely with the Relationship Team and Contract Admin during contract cutovers to guarantee smooth operational transitions.
  • Manage the complete client offboarding process when agreements expire or conclude, ensuring clean catalog handovers and system updates.

Administrative & Back-Office Representation

job.title: Manager, Social Media
job.description:
We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

How we LEAD:


CD Baby is looking for a Social Media Manager to lead our organic social presence as one of the most useful and relevant voices for self-releasing artists.


Our audience spans from artists releasing for the first time to experienced musicians building independent careers. What connects them is their intent: they care about their craft, want to grow, and take their careers seriously. You’ll help them navigate the business of music, make informed decisions, and find tools and opportunities to move their careers forward.


This is a hands-on role spanning strategy, content creation, community engagement, and performance. You’ll turn business priorities and audience needs into a clear social plan, and own its execution.


We’re looking for someone who understands both social and artists: what they care about, what they struggle with, and what earns their attention.


How you'll CREATE:


Own Social Strategy & Growth:

  • Lead organic social strategy across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Reddit, and emerging platforms.
  • Build a prioritized roadmap grounded in audience needs, with clear channel strategies and KPIs tied to artist acquisition and brand authority.
  • Stay close to artist conversations—from release strategy and fan growth to royalties, promotion, touring, and industry shifts.
  • Evaluate trends and cultural moments for artist relevance and business opportunity.
  • Build a distinctive mix of timely content, recurring series, artist stories, education, and entertainment.

Create Great Content:

  • Own the calendar from idea through publication, coordinating production, stakeholder input, approvals, and deadlines.
  • Concept, write, shoot, edit, and publish platform-native content, especially short-form video.
  • Turn artist challenges and complex topics – from royalties to music marketing – into clear, credible, useful content that reflects CD Baby’s expertise.
  • Develop strong hooks and formats that give artists a reason to follow our socials.

Build Artist Community:

  • Lead daily engagement across comments, DMs, mentions, and relevant conversations.
  • Use community insights to shape content and identify opportunities to support and spotlight artists.
  • Build a distinct CD Baby voice that is knowledgeable, approachable, direct, and human.
  • Exercise editorial judgment about when to educate, celebrate, take a point of view, or join the conversation.

Use Social to Drive Growth:

  • Define channel-specific KPIs for audience growth, engagement, traﬃc, artist acquisition,and conversion.
  • Own reporting and analysis, translating insights into recommendations for content, channel strategy, and campaigns.
  • Test formats, messaging, talent, and CTAs; apply learnings and scale what works.
  • Partner with marketing to connect social goals to broader business priorities.
  • Track competitors, platform shifts, creator trends, and music culture to inform strategy.


Bring your VIBE:

  • You bring 5+ years of relevant experience, ideally in music, entertainment, creator platforms, or a community-driven business.
  • You’ve independently owned organic social strategy and execution, with measurable results.
  • You understand creating content for musicians versus marketing to musicians.
  • You know social platforms and internet culture, with strong creative and editorial judgment.
  • You’re hands-on with short-form video, from concept through shooting and editing.
  • You write clearly, with a strong voice, making complex subjects engaging and useful.
  • You’re proficient in social analytics and Google Sheets or Excel and can translate data into strategic recommendations.
  • You’re highly organized and keep multiple priorities moving.
  • You’re collaborative, but don’t wait for a brief to bring ideas and turn them into action.
  • You’re based in the NYC area and plugged into music, emerging artists, and culture.

Why CD Baby:

Independent artists have more ways than ever to release music—and more responsibility for what happens after release day. CD Baby is building for artists who take that opportunity seriously.


For nearly three decades, CD Baby has helped independent artists bring their music to the world. Now, as part of Virgin Music Group and Universal Music Group, we’re building on that history for the next generation.


This role will help define how that next chapter sounds, feels, and shows up every day.

We are UMG, the Universal Music Group. We are the world’s leading music company. In everything we do, we are committed to artistry, innovation and entrepreneurship. We own and operate a broad array of businesses engaged in recorded music, music publishing, merchandising, and audiovisual content in more than 60 countries. We identify and develop recording artists and songwriters, and we produce, distribute and promote the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful music to delight and entertain fans around the world.
 

Job Summary 


We are currently seeking an Identity & Access Management Engineer with specialization in Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) to join UMG’s global Tech Security & Identity organization. Reporting to the VP, Tech Security & Identity, this is a hands-on engineering role responsible for designing, implementing, and operating enterprise IGA capabilities across a complex, global environment. 

This engineer will play a critical role in governing digital identities, access entitlements, and lifecycle processes for employees, contractors, and non-employee populations. The role emphasizes strong engineering execution, automation, and operational discipline, partnering closely with security, HR, infrastructure, and application teams to ensure access is provisioned appropriately, reviewed regularly, and removed in a timely manner. The ideal candidate brings deep experience with modern IGA platforms, strong understanding of access governance controls, and the ability to operate at scale in a regulated enterprise. 


Job Functions 


Design, engineer, deploy, and operate Identity Governance & Administration (IGA) solutions across the enterprise. 

Implement and manage identity lifecycle processes including joiner, mover, and leaver (JML) workflows for employees and non-employee identities. 

Engineer and maintain access request, approval, and provisioning workflows integrated with HR systems, directories, and enterprise applications. 

Design and operate access governance controls including role models, entitlement catalogs, access certifications, and periodic access reviews. 

Partner with application owners and platform teams to onboard applications into IGA and remediate access governance gaps. 

Develop and maintain automation and integrations for IGA workflows using scripting, APIs, and infrastructure-as-code approaches (e.g., PowerShell, Python). 

Support segregation of duties (SoD) controls, access policy enforcement, and audit readiness activities. 

Troubleshoot and resolve complex identity lifecycle, provisioning, and access-related issues across integrated systems. 

Collaborate with Security, HR, Compliance, and Infrastructure teams to ensure identity governance controls align with security policies and regulatory requirements. 

Maintain technical documentation, configuration standards, and operational runbooks to support scalable and repeatable IGA operations. 

Continuously identify opportunities to improve access governance maturity, reduce manual effort, and enhance user experience through automation and platform enhancements. 


Job Requirements 


Essential Qualifications 


5+ years of hands-on experience in Identity & Access Management or Security Engineering roles, with a strong focus on Identity Governance & Administration. 

Demonstrated experience implementing and operating enterprise IGA platforms (e.g., Saviynt, SailPoint, or equivalent). 

Strong understanding of identity lifecycle management, access provisioning, role-based access control (RBAC), and entitlement governance. 

Hands-on experience designing and supporting access certification campaigns and remediation processes. 

Experience integrating IGA solutions with HR systems, Active Directory / Entra ID, and enterprise applications. 

Proficiency in scripting and automation using tools such as PowerShell or Python. 

Experience working in hybrid and cloud environments (Azure and/or AWS) with IAM integrations. 

Ability to independently own complex technical deliverables while collaborating effectively within a global organization. 

Strong troubleshooting, documentation, and communication skills. 


Desirable Qualifications 


Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. 

Experience with advanced IGA capabilities such as role mining, access analytics, or policy-based provisioning. 

Familiarity with compliance and audit frameworks such as SOX, ISO 27001, NIST, or similar. 

Professional certifications such as Saviynt Certified Professional, SailPoint Certified IdentityIQ Engineer, Security+, or CISSP. 

Experience operating IAM or identity governance platforms within a large, global, or highly regulated enterprise environment.

job.title: Manager, Financial Reporting
job.description:
At Warner Music Group, we’re a global collective of music makers and music lovers, tech innovators and inspired entrepreneurs, game-changing creatives and passionate team members. Here, we turn dreams into stardom and audiences into fans. We are guided by three core values that underpin everything we do across all our diverse businesses: 

  • Curiosity: We do our best work when we’re immersing ourselves in culture and breaking through barriers. Curiosity is the driving force behind creativity and ingenuity. It fuels innovation, and innovation is the key to our future. 

  • Collaboration: Making music and bringing it to the world is all about the power of originality amplified by teamwork. A great idea, like a great song, travels globally. We ignite passions and build connections across our diverse community of artists, songwriters, partners, and fans.

  • Commitment: We pursue excellence for our team and our talent. Everything in music starts with a leap into the unknown, and we’re committed to keeping the faith, acting with integrity, and delivering on our promises.

WMG is home to a wide range of artists, musicians, and songwriters that fuel our success. That is why we are committed to creating a work environment that actively values, appreciates, and respects everyone.  We encourage applications from people with a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences.

Consider a career at WMG and get the best of both worlds – an innovative global music company that retains the creative spirit of a nimble independent.
 

A little bit about our team:

The Corporate Finance Department at Warner Music Group is responsible for overseeing all of the financial operations of the Company in partnership with the finance groups at the labels and individual companies within Warner Music Group. The department provides financial reporting, accounting, planning, budgeting, and financial compliance for the Company. The department is filled with fun, outgoing and overall successful individuals who work hard all while enjoying the perks of working in the Music Industry.


Your role:

Warner Music Group is excited to offer this opportunity in the Corporate Finance Department. This position is responsible for analyzing certain income statement accounts and other key reporting metrics for budget, actuals and forecast submissions on a consolidated basis for Warner Music Group. This position reports to the VP of Financial Reporting. 


Here you’ll get to:

  • Prepare financial statement analytics and reviews for non-operating income statement activity (i.e. “below-the-line” accounts) for budget, actuals and forecasts
  • Coordinate with segments and affiliates on the accurate recording and submission of below-the-line activity for all required income statement submissions including depreciation, amortization, interest expense, interest income, equity income, noncontrolling interest, foreign exchange gains and losses, and other non-operating activity.
  • Prepare of debt covenant calculations, including a trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA calculation, for budget, forecasts, and quarterly and annual report periods
  • Prepare CFO Analytics Package which is used by the Company’s Global CFO to assist in their preparation of the quarterly earnings process
  • Assist in preparation of management reporting deliverables for key metrics and below-the-line analysis
  • Collaborate with external reporting and technical accounting to ensure below-the-line activity is properly reported in accordance with US GAAP and disclosed in the WMG quarterly and annual financial statements (e.g. Form 10-K, Form 10-Q)
  • Assist with the preparation review of certain monthly recurring journal entries in our consolidation system (HFM)
  • Oversee the Sr. Financial Analyst – Consolidations and Financial Reporting who is responsible for performing the monthly intercompany reconciliation, monitoring the status of the monthly close, and preparing various financial reporting deliverables.
  • Liaise directly with Financial Planning and Analysis to prepare quarterly income statement analysis, management discussion and analysis, and other ad-hoc reporting and analysis in connection with our quarterly earnings process.
  • Collaborate with External Reporting and Investor Relations to assist in the development in the quarterly and annual press releases earning scripts documents, and other financial communications.

About you:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance
  • Minimum of 5+ years of professional experience in accounting
  • Big Four public accounting or large multinational experience preferred
  • CPA or CPA candidate a plus
  • Intermediate level knowledge of GAAP/SEC accounting and reporting
  • Proficient with MS office (Excel, PowerPoint and Word)
  • Knowledge of SAP, S/4HANA, Hyperion Financial Management is a plus



We’d love it if you also had:

  • Strong work-ethic and a self-starter with effective organizational skills with attention to detail who proactively seeks out new solutions
  • Demonstrate problem solving, decision making, and continuous process improvement skills
  • Ability to multi-task and prioritize projects. Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines
  • Demonstrates partnering, influencing, and communication skills up and down the organizational structure to convey key elements in a concise and positive manner
  • Ability to communicate clearly and identify issues, without being prompted to do so
  • Ability to work proactively, independently, and as a strategic partner in a team environment
  • Ability to find and implement efficiencies within tasks successfully
  • Demonstrates critical thinking and dedication to deepening understanding of work being done
  • Passion for music and desire to build a career in Finance

job.title: Editor, Cannonball
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.

  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.

job.description:

Over the past two years, “The Interview” has made itself a trustworthy New York Times brand and a destination, where artists (Mick Jagger, Nicolas Cage, Charlize Theron), politicians (Zohran Mamdani, Chuck Schumer), athletes (Karl-Anthony Towns), influential figures in the media (Megyn Kelly, Andrew Schulz, Tucker Carlson), at the center of a story (Scott Pelley, Gisele Pelicot) and beyond sit down for thoughtful, wide-ranging, challenging, fun, news-making video conversations about their lives and ideas.

We are seeking an experienced editor to, in collaboration with the executive producer, guide the editorial selection, writing and structure of the show. You will need to be a total omnivore — as excited about and adept at figuring out the best approach for an interview with John Fetterman as Lena Dunham — and a positive, motivating leader on the team. You need to believe in the power of good conversation to reveal subjects and illuminate ideas and also understand how to structure those conversations to be as compelling as possible — which will at times be free-wheeling and loose and at other times tighter and more targeted. You must have a keen understanding of the moment — in the news, in the culture — and know how to translate that understanding for a show that works on a few different tracks at once, with some bookings coming together far in advance and others really responding to a news moment. You must be skilled in writing for video and have a proven track record of working with hosts, embracing their approach to interviews and figuring out how to bring out their best work. The right candidate is a curious, creative thinker, a rigorous journalist who is filled with ideas, excited to build and evolve the show, and thrives in a collaborative, deadline-driven environment. You will report to the Executive Producer.

Responsibilities:

  • Edit episodes, with attention to pacing, framing, clarity, tone, structure and visual continuity and storytelling
  • Give final sign-off on episodes and social clips
  • Collaborate with the executive producer and hosts on setting editorial agenda and guest selection
  • Help guide the prep process with a team of talented producers to ensure episodes have clarity of thought, logical sequencing of ideas and are structured for maximum impact, while also leaving room for the best part: the surprises that come in actual conversation
  • Know how to guide a host during an interview, when things don't go as planned and the carefully prepared script needs to be thrown out the window
  • Set production schedules and drive production for a small team that is always making several episodes at once (often booking one interview, prepping two, recording two, editing one, and mixing one all in the same week)
  • Communicate notes and feedback to hosts and producers clearly, directly, quickly and compassionately
  • Work closely with producers to help them do their best work on deadline while they juggle their many responsibilities
  • Anticipate challenges in episodes and proactively solve them
  • On occasion, be able to respond to breaking news moments with a sense of urgency, while staying true to the longform, in-depth, conversational identity of the show.
  • Exercise calm under pressure and motivate the team
  • Be a true partner for the executive producer
  • May have input into staffing decisions and will be required to assess performance and provide feedback to staff
  • Welcome feedback, incorporating editorial notes quickly, working cooperatively and coming up with creative solutions when disagreements arise
  • Employ editorial judgment that's reflective of Times mission of independent journalism
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • At least 7 years experience in audio or video production, including several as an editor
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing
  • Experience working with and coaching hosts
  • Experience overseeing soup-to-nuts audio or video production
  • Experience navigating a newsroom environment and solid news judgment

  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, motivating and innovative environment.
  • Collaborative spirit is a must.

You will serve as a hub for the newsroom’s public records requests, helping provide resources and guidance to journalists across The Times about how to maximize our ability to obtain information in the public’s interest. You will serve as a consultant to teams on effective tactics, working with reporters and editors at the inception of stories and projects to help integrate FOIA requests early in the process. You will also be responsible for developing story ideas and original coverage through the FOIA process, identifying opportunities to obtain public records that will generate news. You are excited to experiment with new technology and formats and collaborate with our data, visual and product teams to tell stories that resonate with our audience.

You will help track and expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals, and will work closely with the Legal department to identify efforts that merit litigation support.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office each week. The person will also work closely with our bureau in Washington and make periodic visits there. 

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and refine FOIA requests in partnership with internal stakeholders for submission

  • Serve as a consultant for teams as they design public records requests to bolster their reporting, with a priority on integrating such requests early into the process of developing stories.

  • Propose and drive story ideas based on FOIA requests and coordinate coverage across multiple desks 

  • Consult with desks to understand when and how to augment ongoing themes with FOIA requests

  • Advise journalists across the newsroom about the most effective approaches to obtain information through public records laws.

  • Develop and maintain training materials and deliver training about what information can be obtained through the federal Freedom of Information Act and similar state and local statutes.

  • Coordinate, track and help expedite public records requests by maintaining a centralized database of FOIA requests and appeals.

  • Partner with the Legal department in identifying efforts to seek public information that merit litigation support.

  • Represent the Newsroom in partnership with Legal on FOIA matters

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the enterprise OR news research team.

  • 5+ years’ experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization.

  • Demonstrated success navigating and resolving legal issues related to public records laws. 

  • A record of collaborating and partnering with colleagues to find innovative storytelling approaches through the use of public records and other legal strategies. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in shaping the public records strategy of a news organization.

  • Conversant in local and state public records laws and practices in addition to the federal statute.

  • Deep familiarity with media law or a law degree

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  1. What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  2. Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  3. Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  4. What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  5. What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  6. Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times Politics desk is seeking a Night Editor to drive our evening operation, editing news, features and live stories across our platforms. This essential role requires an essential quality: excellent news judgment.

You will manage the Politics news report during the evening, coordinating with leadership and the subject matter and live editors, serving as the primary liaison. You will edit a wide range of copy including major enterprise pieces and breaking news. You will launch reporters on breaking stories and start live blogs with speed and good judgement when the news rises. You will monitor and anticipate news developments, make assignments, and handle first reads — comprehensive edits for structure, framing and balance – and second reads – close-in edits for grammar, spelling and New York Times style.

You are curious and passionate about meeting our audience needs. You are excited to collaborate with departments across the newsroom, experimenting with different storytelling formats to find the best ways to connect our journalism with audiences around the world. This is a collaborative desk; you must be able to navigate input from colleagues across the newsroom and develop superb relationships with the news desk, live, audience, video, photo and print teams, among other collaborators. 

You are currently expected to work weekdays, from afternoon through evening, and must be capable of stepping in at all stages of the editing process, from a story’s conception through its publication. 

This is an in-office position, based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. 

Responsibilities:

  • You will supervise and work with reporters on shaping stories and lifting copy and may be expected to manage one or more reporters.
  • You will make news judgments, including launching reporters on stories, under intense pressure and consult widely with colleagues around the newsroom.
  • You will oversee coverage of breaking news stories, including live blogs.
  • You will work closely with the live editors during the evening.
  • You will generate story ideas that demonstrate solid news judgment and knowledge of a subject area.
  • You will coordinate and maintain strong relationships and communication with colleagues on visuals, audience, news desk and more.
  • You will stay current on and willing to work with new story forms, visual formats and digital innovations in the newsroom.
  • You will monitor sources for breaking news, coordinating with other editors on deployment decisions and launching reporters as needed.
  • You will edit a vast range of material from the reader’s perspective for accuracy, grammar, comprehension and readability.
  • You will provide first and second edits for a variety of stories and topics across the desk
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Politics Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years editing experience at a journalism or media company
  • Experience working independently in high-pressure, deadline-driven newsrooms -- including coverage and workflow, as an editor
  • Writing/editing skills that demonstrate mastery of journalistic style and standards, including ethical and superb news judgment
  • Experience working independently and setting priorities when breaking news demands attention 
  • Proficiency in all aspects of digital production

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A willingness to be flexible as the newsroom’s needs evolve
  • Experience covering American politics
  • Experience supervising reporters

The New York Times is looking for someone to join our Newsroom Operations team. We are looking for someone who can handle the demands of a fast-paced news environment and can work under sometimes ambiguous circumstances. 

The Operations Manager will work with Shows and Visuals, but also assist other departments at the center of visual journalism at The Times. The work of these journalists — along with visual efforts across the newsroom — is a pillar of our reporting that has a large and engaged audience. You will help support these journalists with a variety of daily responsibilities and short- and long-term projects and coordinate with this group's other operations managers. You will be responsible for ensuring that day-to-day on-site operational tasks are completed in a timely manner to support the needs of department managers and staff.

The Operations Manager's work is critical in supporting the journalism produced at The New York Times and all tasks, whether daily, weekly or one-off are greatly valued. You will report to a senior manager of Newsroom Operations.

  • Able to work with all levels of management and staff in a highly professional manner; ability to manage the various needs of a team of 100+ employees and leaders

job.title: Reporter Fellow, Local Investigations - Mississippi, Louisiana, & Arkansas
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters who have a local investigative story idea rooted in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.  

This is a NY Guild role based in Louisiana, Mississippi, or Arkansas.

Responsibilities:

  • Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.
  • Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet
  • You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue
  • Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here. 

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered. 

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

  • What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?
  • Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?
  • Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?
  • What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.
  • What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?
  • Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations. 

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices. And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails. 

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

  • Starts with high stakes
    How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?
  • Has a clear line of accountability
    Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.
  • Reveals something
    Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?
  • Has a clear sense of place
    The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis. 

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

job.title: Research Director, Audience Insights, Content Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.
  • Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.
  • Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.
  • Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.
  • Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.
  • Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.
  • Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products
  • Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.
  • Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.
  • Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.
  • Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.
  • Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.
  • Experience managing external research partners/vendors.
  • Experience with visualization tools and creating compelling presentations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • B.A./B.S. degree.
