  • Develop, test, and validate agentic AI and intelligent automation across the direct tax lifecycle, including document understanding, data mapping and reconciliation, anomaly detection, and AI-assisted review. 
  • Give engineers and data scientists direct, practitioner-grounded feedback on AI feature accuracy, performance, and real-world fit, using independent judgment built on tax experience. 
  • Lead the development of advanced use cases for tax professionals using ONESOURCE and the broader Thomson Reuters AI portfolio, and build thought leadership in how AI applies to corporate tax practice. 
  • Partner with product managers to bring domain expertise to roadmap prioritization, requirement definition, and feature validation, so what gets built reflects how corporate tax work is actually done. 
  • Create guidance, use case documentation, and adoption resources that help tax professionals get value from new capabilities quickly. 

Customer & Stakeholder Engagement 

  • Engage directly with enterprise customers—including corporate tax directors, controllers, tax managers, and Big Four advisors—as a credible peer who understands their workflows, pressures, and standards. 
  • Represent ONESOURCE in customer advisory boards, enterprise client engagements, and industry events, offering expert perspective on product direction and corporate tax best practices. 
  • Translate what you hear from practitioners into clear, actionable input for the product team, serving as the ongoing bridge between real-world tax practice and product development. 
  • Partner with Customer Success, Sales, and Support to drive adoption, resolve complex tax questions, and strengthen customer satisfaction and retention. 
  • Collaborate with UX/design, engineering, compliance, and go-to-market teams as the authoritative internal voice of the corporate tax professional throughout the product lifecycle. 
  • Coordinate with other Thomson Reuters divisions and teams on initiatives where direct tax expertise and cross-product alignment are needed.

Required Qualifications:


Education 

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field is required. 
  • CPA designation is required, or actively in progress. 

Tax & Accounting Domain Expertise 

  • Minimum 5–7 years of professional experience in corporate tax or public accounting environment, with hands-on responsibility for corporate income tax provision, compliance, or planning. 
  • Deep, working knowledge of corporate direct tax processes is required, with demonstrated depth in at least one core area: income tax provision, compliance, or planning. 
  • Demonstrated ability to apply tax best practices to assess software functionality, identify gaps, and articulate what a high-quality direct tax solution should do. 
  • Prior use of enterprise corporate tax software—such as ONESOURCE, Checkpoint, Corptax, Longview, etc.—is strongly preferred; direct ONESOURCE experience is a significant plus. 

AI & Technology Fluency 

  • Proven experience working with or evaluating AI tools in a professional context, with the ability to assess accuracy, reliability, and fitness for use in high-stakes tax workflows. 
  • Comfortable collaborating with engineering and data science teams to test AI-powered features and provide practitioner-grounded feedback. 
  • Awareness of responsible AI principles including auditability, explainability, and appropriate use of AI in regulated accounting and tax environments. 

Communication & Collaboration 

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex tax concepts into clear product guidance, customer-facing materials, and cross-functional requirements. 
  • Experience drafting guidance documents, use case materials, or training content for professional audiences. 
  • Proven ability to work effectively across internal teams — product, engineering, sales, and customer success — in a fast-paced, collaborative environment. 

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Prior experience in a product specialist, solutions consultant, or subject matter expert role within a tax or financial technology company. 
  • Experience at a Big Four or large regional accounting firm, or within the tax function of a large multinational corporation. 
  • Hands-on experience testing, validating, or providing feedback on AI-powered features in enterprise software. 
  • Familiarity with ERP platforms relevant to tax data (SAP, Oracle, Workday, NetSuite). 
  • Experience presenting to or engaging with executive stakeholders in an advisory, SME, or thought leadership capacity.

Thomson Reuters is a global leader in providing trusted information and technology to professionals in law, tax, accounting, compliance, and news. Corporate tax is at an inflection point. Data volumes, regulatory complexity, and pressure on lean tax teams are rising, while AI, automation, and modern cloud architecture create the chance to fundamentally reimagine how direct tax gets done. ONESOURCE sits at the core of the corporate tax lifecycle for thousands of companies worldwide, and we are accelerating investment to lead that change. We are looking for a Strategic Account Executive to expand our presence across Argentina, Chile, Uruguay, Costa Rica, and Guatemala by developing new business opportunities and growing strategic customer relationships within the assigned geography.

  • Coordinate meetings and build relationships with key decision-makers and senior stakeholders.
  • Lead consultative sales conversations to understand client needs and position the appropriate SaaS solutions.
  • Prepare and deliver compelling commercial proposals tailored to customer requirements.
  • Manage the full sales cycle from prospecting through negotiation and close.
  • Support retention, upselling, and renewal opportunities within existing accounts where applicable.
  • Present monthly pipeline updates, sales results, and business progress to leadership.
  • Prioritize activities and opportunities based on business direction and market potential.
  • Lead important business initiatives and contribute to the execution of commercial strategies within the region.
  • Provide market insights and specialized recommendations to management to support decision-making and growth plans.
  • Manage budget considerations related to projects or programs within the scope of the role.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to support complex customer needs and ensure effective account development.

  • 10+ years of experience in consultative sales of SaaS technology solutions within the corporate and/or enterprise segment.

Titre : Agents au soutien fiscal - postes contractuels / Télétravail

Thomson Reuters est à la recherche d'agents de soutien fiscal motivé. À propos du poste 
Dans cette opportunité en tant qu'Agent de Soutien fiscal, vous allez : 

·         Assurer le soutien à la clientèle en matière de fiscalité par téléphone et courriel, pour notre gamme de logiciels d’impôts pour Professionnels et Consommateurs

·         Participer au contrôle de qualité de nos logiciels. 

·         Rédiger des réponses type dans le cadre de foires aux questions (FAQ). 

·         Identifier des problèmes récurrents rencontrés par les clients, et en aviser son supérieur 

À propos de vous 

Vous êtes fait pour le rôle d'Agent de Soutien fiscal si votre expérience professionnelle inclut : 

·         Solides connaissances en fiscalité.

·         Diplôme universitaire en fiscalité, comptabilité, finance, gestion.

job.description:
Thomson Reuters is seeking a high-caliber Senior Legal Counsel & Privacy Operations Lead to join the General Counsel’s Office. Reporting directly to the Chief Privacy Officer (CPO), this role serves as both the technical operations leader and a trusted Chief of Staff to the CPO. You will blend deep legal and regulatory expertise with hands-on technical privacy operations, while providing strategic governance, operational cadence, and administrative oversight across Thomson Reuters’ global privacy program.


About the Role

In this opportunity as a Privacy Operations Lead / Senior Counsel, you will lead:


Chief of Staff & Strategic Program Oversight

  • Act as the CPO’s right-hand strategic partner and advisor, driving the execution of high-priority strategic initiatives across the global privacy office.
  • Provide overarching administrative governance, including tracking program budgets, vendor management, resource allocation, and team operating rhythms.
  • Prepare executive-level briefings, Board of Directors presentations, and cross-functional reporting on privacy program maturity, risks, and compliance posture.
  • Lead cross-functional alignment between the CPO’s office, General Counsel, Information Security (CISO), Product, and business unit leaders.

Privacy Program Management

  • Drive end-to-end program governance, operational roadmap planning, and scalable execution for Thomson Reuters’ global privacy program.
  • Oversee the day-to-day operations of Thomson Reuters’ global privacy program
  • Implement privacy policies, procedures, and operational frameworks
  • Conduct or facilitate the conduct of risk assessments, including privacy impact assessments (PIAs), data protection impact assessments (DPIAs), and transfer impact assessments (TIAs)
  • Coordinate responses to data subject access requests (DSARs) and ensure timely resolution
  • Track and report on privacy program metrics and KPIs

Privacy Compliance & Risk Management

  • Track and report changes in new/existing privacy regulations and monitor compliance with key regulations including GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, among others
  • Build out and maintain data inventory, and data mapping automation initiatives Identify privacy risks and work with stakeholders to implement mitigation strategies
  • Support privacy incident response and breach notification processes
  • Conduct privacy audits and assessments of internal processes and third-party vendors

Cyber Incident Management

  • Support the day-to-day operational execution of the cyber incident response program, including intake, triage, and escalation of security incidents with privacy implications
  • Support cross-functional co-ordination with Information Security, IT, Legal, and Business teams during active incidents to ensure timely containment, remediation, and communication
  • Support legal assessment of incidents to determine breach notification obligations under applicable privacy and data protection regulations, and drive timely notification to affected individuals and regulators
  • Maintain and continuously improve incident response playbooks, runbooks, and operational procedures for cyber incidents

Privacy-by-Design and Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Legal, Information Security, IT, Product, and Business teams to integrate and operationalize privacy-by-design principles and guidance into the product development cycle.
  • Serve as a privacy subject matter expert and advisor to business units
  • Facilitate privacy training and awareness programs for employees
  • Work with vendors and partners to ensure contractual privacy obligations are met
  • Identify current sub-processor's and updating contractual documentation to reflect current state

Documentation & Reporting

  • Maintain records of processing activities (ROPA) and privacy documentation
  • Prepare and maintain privacy metrics, dashboards and reports for leadership and relevant stakeholders
  • Document privacy procedures and create operational playbooks
  • Support regulatory inquiries and audits

Team Leadership & Management

  • Provide strategic direction, mentorship, and operational management to privacy operations specialists, privacy engineers and cross-functional privacy champions.
  • Set clear performance expectations, conduct regular one-on-ones, and provide ongoing coaching to support individual growth and career development.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Legal, IT, Security, and Business teams to align privacy operations priorities, resolve escalations, and ensure the team has the resources and guidance needed to execute effectively.
  • Drive team efficiency by establishing standardized workflows, refining processes, and implementing best practices that scale with the organization’s evolving privacy landscape.

About You

You’re a fit for the role of Privacy Operations Lead / Senior Counsel if your background includes:


Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in law, Information Systems, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related legal or technical field Juris Doctor (J.D.) or Master’s degree in legal studies
  • 8-10+ years of combined experience in privacy law, technical privacy operations, and program management, preferably in a SaaS environment
  • 4-6+ years leading technical/legal teams, driving program strategy, and serving in an executive advisory or Chief of Staff capacity
  • Relevant privacy and/or cybersecurity certification, such as IAPP’s Certified Information Privacy Professional credential (CIPM, CIPPT), Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP).
  • Experience with privacy risk assessments from a technical perspective.
  • Subject matter expertise in privacy tech stacks (OneTrust, PETs, automated data mapping) paired with the ability to translate technical architecture into actionable legal guidance.
  • Strong knowledge of global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA, etc.)
  • Ability to interpret legal and regulatory requirements into system-level controls.
  • Experience in advising product and technology teams on privacy obligations relating to the processing of sensitive data, including implementing privacy by design requirements.
  • Knowledge of data classification, retention, and lifecycle management.
  • Experience managing privacy operations in a large, complex organization.
  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects and priorities simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication skills with ability to explain complex privacy concepts to non-technical audiences.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities Experience with privacy management tools and technologies.

Preferred:

  • Experience with automation tools (e.g., PowerBI, PowerAutomate) and AI/ML frameworks for compliance.
  • Experience with data governance tools, SIEM systems, and privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs).
  • Proficiency in scripting and automation for compliance tasks/privacy automation tools and technologies.
  • Knowledge of information security frameworks and practices.
  • Project management certification or experience.
  • Experience operating within a dual legal/technical capability at an enterprise software or data provider.
  • Proven track record supporting a General Counsel or Chief Privacy Officer with strategic planning, budget management, and executive communications.

Skills & Competencies

  • Strategic thinking with operational execution capabilities
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across global teams

job.title: IT Procurement Manager
job.description:
Job Description:

The IT Procurement Manager is responsible for leading strategic sourcing and procurement initiatives across a broad range of technology spend categories. This role partners closely with business stakeholders, Category Leads, Finance, Legal, and Information Security teams to develop sourcing strategies, negotiate complex supplier agreements, optimize spend, and deliver sustainable business value. The position plays a key role in driving procurement excellence, operational efficiency, supplier performance, and compliance across global procurement operations.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead end-to-end sourcing activities, including requirements gathering, supplier evaluation, negotiation, and contract execution.
  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies utilizing competitive RFx processes, eRFx tools, and e-Auctions.
  • Analyze spend data, contracts, budgets, and market trends to identify cost-saving and value-creation opportunities.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders and Category Leads to understand procurement requirements and develop sourcing pipelines.
  • Create and implement category strategies aligned with business objectives and organizational priorities.
  • Negotiate complex supplier agreements and manage contract execution across multiple geographies.
  • Drive supplier performance management and procurement compliance initiatives.
  • Support procurement systems and operational strategies to improve efficiency and business outcomes.
  • Partner with Finance, Legal, and Information Security teams on contract drafting, risk mitigation, and negotiations.
  • Resolve complex procurement issues and provide strategic guidance to stakeholders.
  • Develop sourcing collateral, including business cases, contract summaries, and RFx documentation.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Fluent English communication skills, both written and verbal.
  • 5+ years of experience in Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Procurement Operations, or Program Management.
  • Strong experience managing end-to-end sourcing engagements and supplier negotiations.
  • Expertise in IT Procurement and technology-related spend categories.
  • Experience negotiating and managing contracts valued at $1M+ across multiple geographies.
  • Strong understanding of sourcing methodologies, procurement processes, and contract management.
  • Ability to analyze spend patterns, contracts, supplier performance, and market trends to drive sourcing strategies.
  • Excellent stakeholder management, relationship-building, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Experience with Source-to-Pay platforms such as Ariba and/or Fieldglass.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of procurement regulations, compliance requirements, and industry best practices.

job.title: Senior Software Engineer, AI Platform
job.description:
The AI Platform team builds, develops, and operates the Enterprise AI Platform at Thomson Reuters — a comprehensive ecosystem of services, tools, and infrastructure that empowers both technical and non-technical users to develop, evaluate, deploy, and monitor AI solutions at scale.


We are looking for a Senior Site Reliability Engineer to take ownership of the reliability, scalability, and long-term operational architecture of the AI Platform. In this role, you will partner closely with platform and ML engineers to design and evolve infrastructure that is resilient by default, observable at every layer, and built to sustain the pace of a fast-moving GenAI platform. Beyond day-to-day operational excellence, you will be expected to make deliberate, forward-looking infrastructure decisions — establishing patterns, standards, and guardrails that scale with the platform and reduce systemic risk over time. This is a senior individual contributor role with real technical ownership and meaningful influence over how the AI Platform is built and operated at Thomson Reuters.

About the role:

In this opportunity as a Senior Software Engineer, AI Platform, you will: 

  • Own and drive the long-term infrastructure strategy for the AI Platform team — designing systems and standards that are built to scale, remain reliable under growth, and reduce operational burden over time.
  • Own and improve the operational posture of cloud-native services including containerized workloads, serverless functions, and managed ML infrastructure.
  • Instrument services with observability tooling (Datadog, CloudWatch, or equivalent) covering metrics, logs, and distributed tracing.
  • Establish and enforce SLAs and error budgets; drive incident response, post-mortems, and systemic reliability improvements.
  • Collaborate with platform engineering to harden infrastructure against security findings (Wiz, Snyk) and maintain compliance with organizational standards.
  • Design, build, and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI Platform services, SDKs, and infrastructure, ensuring fast and reliable delivery across environments.
  • Automate toil — infrastructure provisioning, security remediation workflows, environment management, and deployment operations.
  • Mentor junior team members and raise the engineering bar across DevOps practices on the team.

About you:

You’re a fit for the role of Senior Software Engineer, AI Platform if you:

  • Strong communication skills and the ability to work across engineering, security, and product teams and distill unclear requirements into clear engineering goals.
  • 5+ years of experience in cloud and infrastructure engineering roles.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and shell scripting, with hands-on experience building and deploying automation tools that eliminate toil and streamline DevOps workflows. Infrastructure-as-code experience with CloudFormation, Terraform, ARM or SAM is expected.
  • Deep hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure is expected.

job.title: Sales Representative - Sales ERP (Bejerman)
job.description:
Job Description  


Sumarse al área de ventas para comercializar soluciones de software orientadas al segmento empresas en Argentina, principalmente Bejerman ERP combinando generación de nuevos negocios con desarrollo de cartera activa.


La posición requiere un perfil comercial con experiencia en venta consultiva de productos intangibles, capaz de gestionar oportunidades de punta a punta, identificar necesidades del cliente, acompañar procesos de decisión con múltiples interlocutores y sostener un seguimiento comercial estructurado en ciclos de venta de mediana duración.


Key Responsibilities

  • Formar parte del área de ventas suscriptivas del segmento empresas.
  • Comercializar soluciones de software de gestión administrativa y productiva para pymes en Argentina.
  • Realizar venta consultiva de productos intangibles, tanto de manera telefónica como presencial.
  • Prospectar nuevos clientes para ampliar la cartera asignada. (Excluyente)
  • Gestionar y desarrollar una cartera de clientes activa, promoviendo nuevas funcionalidades, ampliaciones de uso y oportunidades de upselling/cross-selling.
  • Detectar necesidades, dolores y requerimientos del cliente para construir propuestas comerciales acordes.
  • Acompañar oportunidades comerciales end to end, desde la prospección hasta el cierre.
  • Brindar capacitaciones, presentaciones y demostraciones comerciales de producto, con fuerte capacidad de oratoria y manejo de relaciones interpersonales.
  • Trabajar colaborativamente con otras áreas en temas de producto, compliance, alianzas y actualizaciones funcionales.
  • Utilizar herramientas de IA para mejorar productividad comercial, preparación de mensajes, seguimiento y comunicación con clientes.

Required Qualifications

  • Profesional graduado o estudiante avanzado de carrera universitaria, preferentemente en:Administración de Empresas,Contador Público,Comercialización,o carreras afines.
  • Mínimo 2 años de experiencia en posiciones comerciales/ventas.
  • Experiencia en venta consultiva y en manejo del ciclo comercial end to end.
  • Experiencia en comercialización de productos intangibles.
  • Experiencia en prospección activa y generación de nuevos clientes.
  • Capacidad para desarrollar y mantener cartera de clientes.
  • Buenas habilidades de comunicación oral y escrita.
  • Capacidad para brindar presentaciones, capacitaciones o demos comerciales.
  • Manejo de algún software CRM; idealmente experiencia con Salesforce.
  • Capacidad de autogestión, proactividad y orientación a resultados.
  • Facilidad para trabajar en equipo.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experiencia en prospección y generación de nuevos clientes.
  • Experiencia en uso de herramientas de IA aplicadas a procesos comerciales.
  • Experiencia previa en venta de software, tecnología, suscripciones o soluciones B2B.
  • Experiencia gestionando clientes con distintos interlocutores, como:jefes de área,responsables administrativos,finanzas,contadores internos o externos,perfiles de sistemas/IT,gerencias.




#LI-AC1

 

 


¿Qué te ofrecemos?

  • Modelo de Trabajo Híbrido: Hemos adoptado un entorno de trabajo híbrido y flexible para nuestros roles en oficina, ofreciendo una experiencia fluida que está conectada digital y físicamente.
  • Flexibilidad y Equilibrio entre Trabajo y Vida Personal: "Flex My Way" Consiste en un conjunto de políticas de apoyo en el entorno laboral, diseñadas para facilitar la gestión de las responsabilidades personales y profesionales, ya sea atendiendo a la familia, participando en actividades comunitarias o dedicando tiempo al descanso y la renovación personal. Estas políticas se basan en nuestro enfoque flexible de trabajo, que permite a los empleados trabajar desde cualquier lugar hasta 8 semanas al año, promoviendo así un equilibrio ideal entre sus compromisos laborales y personales.
  • Desarrollo y Crecimiento Profesional: Fomentamos una cultura de aprendizaje continuo y desarrollo de habilidades, preparando a nuestro talento para enfrentar los desafíos del futuro y ofrecer soluciones reales. Nuestro programa "Grow My Way" y el enfoque en habilidades garantizan que tengas las herramientas y conocimientos para crecer, liderar y prosperar en un futuro habilitado por la inteligencia artificial.
  • Beneficios Competitivos del Sector: Ofrecemos planes de beneficios integrales que incluyen seguros de gastos médicos, dos días de descanso por salud mental a nivel de la empresa, programas de incentivos para empleados y recursos para el bienestar mental, físico y financiero.
  • Cultura: Reconocida globalmente con una reputación premiada por inclusión y pertenencia, flexibilidad, equilibrio entre trabajo y vida personal, y más. Vivimos nuestros valores: Obsesión por nuestros Clientes, Competir para Ganar, Desafiar nuestro Pensamiento, Actuar Rápido / Aprender Rápido, y Más Fuertes Juntos.
  • Impacto Social: Genera un impacto en tu comunidad con nuestro Instituto de Impacto Social. Ofrecemos a los empleados dos días de voluntariado pagados anualmente y oportunidades para involucrarse en proyectos de consultoría pro bono e iniciativas de Medio Ambiente, Sociales y de Gobernanza (ESG).
  • Haciendo un Impacto Real en el Mundo: Somos una de las pocas compañías a nivel global que asiste a sus clientes en la búsqueda de justicia, verdad y transparencia. Trabajando en conjunto con los profesionales e instituciones a los que servimos, contribuimos a sostener el estado de derecho, fomentar el comercio, detectar a los infractores, informar sobre los hechos y ofrecer información confiable e imparcial a personas en todo el mundo.

 

 

Quiénes somos

Thomson Reuters marca el camino hacia el futuro al reunir contenido confiable y la tecnología que las personas y organizaciones necesitan para tomar decisiones correctas. Servimos a profesionales en los sectores legal, fiscal, contable, de cumplimiento, gubernamental y de medios. Nuestros productos combinan software altamente especializado e información para capacitar a los profesionales con los datos, inteligencia y soluciones necesarias para tomar decisiones informadas y ayudar a las instituciones en su búsqueda de justicia, verdad y transparencia. Reuters, parte de Thomson Reuters, es un proveedor líder mundial de periodismo y noticias confiables.

Contamos con el talento de 26,000 colaboradores en más de 70 países, donde todos tienen la oportunidad de contribuir y crecer profesionalmente en entornos de trabajo flexibles. En un momento en el que la objetividad, precisión, equidad y transparencia están bajo ataque, nos comprometemos a buscarlos. ¿Suena emocionante? Forma parte de nuestro equipo y contribuye a moldear las industrias que impulsan el progreso de la sociedad.

Como empresa global, confiamos en los antecedentes únicos, perspectivas y experiencias de todos los empleados para cumplir con nuestros objetivos comerciales. Para asegurarnos de poder hacerlo, buscamos colaboradores talentosos y calificados en todas nuestras operaciones alrededor del mundo, sin importar raza, color, sexo/género, incluyendo embarazo, identidad y expresión de género, origen nacional, religión, orientación sexual, discapacidad, edad, estado civil, estado de ciudadanía, condición de veterano u otra clasificación protegida bajo la ley aplicable. Thomson Reuters se enorgullece de ser un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades laborales, proporcionando un ambiente de trabajo libre de drogas.

Asimismo, ofrecemos adaptaciones razonables para personas calificadas con discapacidades y para aquellas con creencias religiosas sinceras, conforme a la legislación vigente. Puedes encontrar más información sobre cómo solicitar una adaptación aquí.

job.title: Manager, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
job.description:
Site Reliability Engineering Manager

Job Description

As a Site Reliability Engineering Manager, you will lead a team of SREs responsible for the availability, reliability, and performance of our products. You will combine technical depth, hands-on use of AI, and people leadership. You will own the team's contribution to availability targets, lead incident and problem management, and build the telemetry and processes that keep our services measurably healthy. You will be the escalation point for our most urgent customer issues. You will also be the bridge between engineering, operations, and senior leadership. If you have experience in service management, cloud providers, software development, and technology infrastructure, join our team and develop your career.

Key Responsibilities

  • Drive best practices for reliability, scalability, and performance across our systems and services. Make sure the team delivers sustainable improvements, not just reactive support.
  • Identify risks to service reliability early and develop strategies to mitigate them, ensuring business continuity and resilience.
  • Identify where AI and ML tools can improve reliability, reduce cost, and lower risk.
  • Promote DevOps principles and integrate SRE practices into the software development lifecycle.
  • Champion automation, AI, and tooling to streamline operational workflows, increase efficiency, and reduce manual toil.
  • Drive the development of monitoring, alerting, and automation solutions that proactively identify and remediate issues.
  • Lead the team through incident and problem management processes. Use AI-assisted tooling to speed up triage and root cause analysis.
  • Communicate major incidents, root causes, and corrective actions to senior leadership.
  • Turn incident learnings into durable improvement actions that prevent repeat events.
  • Lead and mentor a team of SREs, providing technical guidance, coaching, and support that foster collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
  • Hire, develop, organize, and equip talent, and make hiring decisions.
  • Build a service culture and motivate staff through clear expectations and constructive feedback.
  • Foster a culture of continuous improvement through experimentation, learning, knowledge sharing, and professional development. Encourage the team to adopt AI tools responsibly.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience. A Computer Science or related technical degree is preferred.
  • 5+ years of experience in a leadership role managing a team of DevOps engineers, Site Reliability Engineers, or related technical professionals.
  • 5+ years of relevant experience in software development and/or technology platform, infrastructure, or operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to set direction and inspire team members to engage and deliver on a vision.
  • Experience developing team members through performance evaluations and constructive feedback.
  • Experience managing availability targets and leading incident and problem management processes.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, with a proactive approach to resolving complex technical issues.
  • Experience with cloud platforms and their APIs (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Hands-on experience with programming and scripting languages (e.g., Python, Java, or C#).
  • Proven ability to learn new technologies quickly, including AI tools, our products, and our architecture.
  • Excellent critical thinking, communication, presentation, documentation, troubleshooting, and collaborative problem-solving skills.
  • Demonstrated ownership of accountabilities.
  • Comfort in a fast-paced environment and motivation from complex technical and business challenges.

Are you a curious and innovative thinker with experience doing machine learning research? Thomson Reuters Labs is seeking a machine learning scientist intern with experience in natural language processing, information retrieval, and AI agent design and evaluation.

We experiment, build, and deliver. We support the organization and our customers through applied research and development of new products and technologies. job.title: Executive producer, Full Story
job.description:
Guardian Australia is part of Guardian News & Media (GNM), publisher of theguardian.com. As a leading global media organisation, we are renowned for our pioneering independent journalism and our award-winning digital products.
 

We are seeking an Executive producer for Guardian Australia’s flagship daily podcast, Full Story. You will have a pivotal role in brainstorming ideas to commissioning them, through to production and editorial sign off. 

 

This role is being offered on a full-time, permanent basis, with early starts or late finishes.


In this role you will…
 

  • Manage and executive produce our daily news podcast - Full Story - including commissioning daily episodes, managing staff and production schedules 
  • Ensure that Full Story covers topics our audience is interested in and that showcase Guardian Australia’s award-winning journalism in a timely manner
  • Manage and mentor staff as directed
  • Oversee episode editing sessions, including directing and signing off sound design, audio and video edits
  • Ensure episodes meet the highest editorial standards and legal compliance
  • Work closely with producers on interviews and scripting, and with sound designers to elevate stories
  • Work with hosts to continually develop the show’s sound and structure
  • Ensure that senior editorial staff are updated on progress and work with department heads to guide our marketing and social media teams to make sure the shows are promoted to the widest audience possible
  • Create audio and video episode pages with engaging headlines
  • Create site-specific thumbnails and headlines for YouTube and social clips  
  • Stay up to date with the latest developments in audio and video podcasting


You’ll bring….
 

  • At least 6-7 years’ experience in news storytelling in a digital news environment 
  • Substantial experience of producing news accurately and quickly under tight deadlines
  • Advanced level of editorial judgement, preferably developed in a national newsroom 
  • Significant experience of managing journalists and/or producers, key contributors and on-air talent
  • Proven track record in making high quality audio programming
  • Experience in producing interviews, collaborating on scripting and overseeing schedules 
  • Understanding of video podcasting processes and promotion
  • Commitment to showcasing diverse perspectives
  • Good knowledge of media law
  • Ability to consistently meet tight deadlines 
  • Ability to recognise and develop growth opportunities 
  • Excellent understanding of the tone, purpose and editorial aims and values of the Guardian
  • Understanding of (and interest in) the latest developments in audio 
  • Understanding of podcast distribution platforms and analytics 
  • The Guardian’s values: honesty, integrity, courage, fairness, and a sense of duty to the audience and the community 
  • Collaborative manager with excellent communication skills
  • Comfortable producing work on a tight deadline
  • Organised and able to manage multiple projects at a time
  • Good problem-solving skills
  • Ability to work with high profile journalists and external contributors
  • Flexible and able to adapt to changing priorities
  • Ability to build relationships at all levels
  • Passion for narrative audio, podcast production and digital journalism
  • Proven journalistic instincts
  • Creative team player
  • Open to feedback and correction


About working at Guardian Australia… 
 

  • Hybrid working 
  • Employee assistance program (EAP) to support employee wellbeing
  • Paid volunteer leave
  • Dedicated diversity and inclusion employee groups, action plans (including our Reconciliation Action Plan) and cultural competency training
  • Guardian digital subscription


For more information please view the full job description here.


This role is being offered on a full-time, permanent basis, working over a seven-day roster with early starts or late finishes.
 

To apply for this position, please apply online and upload your résumé (maximum three pages) plus covering letter. In your covering letter please outline your motivation for applying for the role and why you think you are suitable.
 

Closing date for applications: Thursday, 19 November 2026

 

If you have application questions or if you require an adjustment to be made during the recruitment process, please email australia.hr@theguardian.com

We believe that these communities must be centred in the work we do, bringing a new perspective and a diversity of thought. We also encourage flexible working and aim to create a work environment where all employees feel respected.

  • A bachelor’s degree in marketing preferred
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of experiential marketing
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), Teams, and Canva
  • Proficiency in Spanish a plus

Travel

job.title: LA Kings - Sr Director Human Resources
job.description:
The LA Kings are where hockey, culture, and community come together. As one of the most iconic franchises in the NHL, the Kings deliver high‑energy games, unforgettable moments, and a game‑night experience that goes far beyond the ice.

Owned by AEG, the LA Kings are powered by teams who bring passion, precision, and pride to everything they do, from game‑day operations and fan experiences to the work that happens behind the scenes. Every role plays a part in creating nights fans remember and a culture that represents Los Angeles.   If you want to be part of a team where the work matters on and off the ice, there’s a place for you here. You’re part of what makes it happen.

Job Summary

The Sr Director Human Resources provides strategic and operational leadership for the human resources function supporting the AEG Sports properties, including the LA Kings and Ontario Reign. The role serves as a senior advisor to business leaders on organizational design, workforce planning, leadership coaching, employee relations, talent strategy, and change initiatives. The Sr Director leads the HR team and provides direction across process improvement, staff development, talent acquisition, learning and development, compliance, and employee relations. This role works across each organization and department to promote consistent, practical, and business-aligned application of human resources programs, policies, and practices while addressing the distinct needs of each property. 

Essential Functions

  • Translate business priorities into an integrated Human Resources strategy for each supported property. Advise senior leaders on workforce, organization, and people implications of business decisions. Participate in key leadership and department discussions, bringing a broad HR perspective and recommending practical solutions that support near-term operating needs and longer-term objectives.
  • Maintain current knowledge of industry trends and employment legislation and oversee the organization's compliance. Assess the impact of regulatory and policy changes, communicate requirements to leaders, and recommend updates to policies, procedures, controls, and practices to reduce risk and support consistent application.
  • Lead the Human Resources department, establish priorities, clarify accountability, coach and develop team members, and monitor goals and service delivery to ensure work is completed accurately, consistently, and in a timely manner.
  • Connect broader business strategy to HR priorities and ensure programs remain relevant to the needs of the supported organizations. Identify patterns and opportunities across properties and recommend approaches, policies, and processes that improve organizational effectiveness, productivity, and HR service delivery.
  • Provide proactive counsel on complex and sensitive people matters, serving as a trusted advisor, coach, and thought partner to senior leaders. Frame issues, assess risk and organizational impact, develop well-supported recommendations, and guide leaders toward timely and sustainable resolutions. Oversee significant employee relations matters and partner with Legal as appropriate.
  • Provide strategic direction for employee experience, recognition, training, and development initiatives. Partner with leadership and the administration team to assess organizational and employee needs, identify capability gaps, prioritize learning solutions, and evaluate whether programs support business and talent objectives.
  • Provide oversight for core HR operations supporting new hires, employee changes, payroll coordination, and benefits administration. Establish appropriate review and escalation practices, ensure regulatory and policy compliance, partner with Legal as needed, and provide leaders and employees with clear interpretation of HR policies.
  • Lead the performance review and merit increase processes for supported properties, ensure appropriate planning and governance, monitor completion and quality of performance discussions, and address exceptions with leadership and corporate partners.
  • Serve as the senior HR liaison between AEG corporate partners and the supported properties. Shape local implementation of enterprise programs and initiatives, communicate business requirements and feedback, and promote alignment while accounting for legitimate operating differences.
  • Provide governance and oversight for the integrity, security, and confidentiality of employee data and records, including documentation standards, access controls, record retention, and lawful disposition of personnel files.
  • Oversee talent acquisition strategy and execution across supported departments. Ensure recruitment, selection, and hiring decisions follow approved practices, address critical and hard-to-fill needs, strengthen candidate quality and experience, and support retention of key talent.
  • Develop and manage the Human Resources budget and workforce plan. Allocate resources against business priorities, monitor spending and capacity, and recommend adjustments that support effective and sustainable HR delivery.

Required Qualifications

  • BA/BS Degree (4-year) in Business Management, Business Administration, or Human Resources Management. Advanced degree preferred. 
  • 7+ years of Human Resources leadership experience, including direct people leadership, experience advising senior executives, and responsibility for leading a broad HR function or major client group.
  • Broad experience across Human Resources disciplines, including compensation, talent acquisition, employee relations, performance management, and talent management, with the ability to integrate these areas into practical business solutions.
  • Experience leading and developing HR teams that support multiple locations, properties, or business units.
  • Experience with Human Resource Information Systems (i.e. UltiPro; Workday; Oracle; PeopleSoft); and Applicant Tracking Systems (i.e. Greenhouse; Taleo)
  • Experience with compensation planning, job leveling, workforce planning, and organizational design and development.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and improving HR initiatives that support measurable business and organizational outcomes.
  • Experience working within entertainment or sports industry is preferred.
  • SPHR or SHRM-SCP is highly preferred.
Skills and Abilities
  • Demonstrated ability to anticipate, assess, and resolve complex and sensitive Human Resources matters using sound judgment, discretion, and an appropriate balance of business and employee considerations.
  • Executive-level verbal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex or sensitive matters clearly and follow through on commitments.
  • Strong knowledge of California, Federal and local employment laws including, but not limited to, ADA, FLSA, EEOC, Title VII, Pay Transparency, etc.
  • Ability to professionally handle sensitive and confidential information
  • Ability to establish credibility and influence decisions with senior leaders while communicating effectively across all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to navigate conflict, competing priorities, and ambiguity and to recommend balanced, sustainable solutions.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize data, identify implications, and present clear recommendations.
  • Strong proficiency with Microsoft Office Products (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and ability to learn applicable business systems.
  • HR Systems knowledge (i.e., UltiPro, applicant tracking system)
  • Ability to read, listen and communicate effectively.
  • Able to balance strategic priorities with operational requirements and respond with an appropriate sense of urgency.

Payscale: $148,956 - $200,000

Bonus: This position is eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Benefits: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: medical, dental and vision insurance, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, company paid basic life insurance, voluntary life insurance, parental leave, 401k Plan (with a current employer match of 3%), flexible spending and health savings account options, and wellness offerings.

job.description:
For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer. 

Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations. 

If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer!

Position Summary:

The Senior Director of Production serves as AEG's on-site representative providing strategic leadership for the operational and execution of large-scale touring productions. Serving as the senior production representative on assigned tours, this role oversees daily show operations, revenue optimization, and cross-functional coordination to maximize tour performance. The Senior Director partners with artists, promoters, venue personnel, ticketing, and production teams to drive operational excellence while ensuring accurate execution throughout the tour lifecycle.

Essential Functions:

  • Lead the day-to-day operational and financial execution of assigned touring productions, serving as the senior production representative with responsibility for production delivery, show settlements, and operational decision-making.
  • Drive revenue optimization by evaluating venue configurations, production layouts, and ticket inventory opportunities to maximize sellable seating while maintaining production, safety, and guest experience standards.
  • Oversee daily financial settlements, expense management, and accounting activities, ensuring timely reconciliation and compliance with internal financial controls and contractual requirements.
  • Coordinate cross-functional tour operations by partnering with ticketing, venue management, production, catering, temporary staffing, and other internal and external stakeholders to ensure seamless show execution.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and operational leadership by developing best practices, mentoring production staff, and supporting organizational initiatives related to tour operations, financial processes, and production standards.

Required Qualifications:

  • Extensive experience managing large-scale touring productions, including live event operations and financial settlements.
  • Strong knowledge of production accounting, revenue management, and ticketing operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent operational decisions in high-pressure, live event environments.
  • Experience with tour settlement systems, ticketing platforms, and production management software.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills with the ability to influence cross-functional teams.
  • Experience managing multiple complex projects simultaneously while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including advanced Excel skills, and experience using budgeting, project management, and financial systems.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with clients, venues, and co-workers
  • Excellent written, verbal and listening communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills
  • Self-motivated and takes initiative
  • May require heavy travel for long period of time of the road

Payscale:  $142,477.05 - $218,083.94 

Bonus: This position is eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements.

Benefits: Full-time: We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: medical, dental and vision insurance, paid holidays, vacation and sick time, company paid basic life insurance, voluntary life insurance, parental leave, 401k Plan (with a current employer match of 3%), flexible spending and health savings account options, and wellness offerings.

AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants.  We are an equal opportunity employer and will not discriminate against any individual, employee, or application for employment on the basis of race, color, marital status, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, or any other legally protected status recognized by federal, state or local law.

AXS connects fans with the artists and teams they love. Each year we sell millions of tickets to thousands of incredible events – from concerts and festivals to sports and theater – at some of the most iconic venues in the world. Since our founding in 2011, we’ve consistently pushed the industry forward and improved experiences for fans, making it easier than ever to discover events, find the perfect seats, and enjoy unforgettable live entertainment, and we continue to lead the evolution of our industry today.

We’re passionate about improving the fan experience and providing game-changing solutions for our clients, and we’re always looking for smart, motivated people to help make it happen. Bring your enthusiasm, your big ideas, and your desire to team up with some of the best and brightest in technology and entertainment.  

The Role

The Ticketing Operations Analyst – Product Operations coordinates cross-departmental product initiatives, ensuring effective stakeholder engagement in User Acceptance Testing and managing issue tracking with product teams under the supervision of the Manager, Ticketing Operations.  The role also supports data cleansing efforts and fraud monitoring, collaborates on triage and escalation of product issues, and participates in after-hours on-call rotations as needed.

  • Recruits, coordinates, and holds accountable the business stakeholders required to complete User Acceptance Testing (UAT) on new AXS products and features, working closely with the Product Owner and Project Managers.

  • Assists with completing client and promoter requests for OTL sweeps, generating reports on problematic orders for clients, and coordinating the bulk cancellation of orders in violation of ticket limits. 
  • Participates in an on-call rotation with other department staff to assist with daily bulk refunds for rescheduled events and triaging emergency requests after hours and on weekends. 
  • Provides general and project-specific assistance as needed to the other Ticketing Operations staff under the supervision of the Manager, Ticketing Operations.

  • BA/BS Degree in Computer Science, Business Administration, or Marketing major preferred.

job.title: Insomniac - Art Curator
job.description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE YOU?

Do you enjoy dance music? Do you excel at creating memorable art experiences? Then you’re in luck! We are looking for a highly motivated self-starter who embodies both a passion for dance culture and a love of the live event space. Is this you? Read on…

 

WHO ARE WE?

Insomniac produces some of the most innovative, immersive music festivals and events in the world. Enhanced by state-of-the-art lighting, pyrotechnics and sound design, large-scale art installations, theatrical performers and next generation special effects, our events captivate the senses and inspire a unique level of fan interaction. The quality of the Headliner experience is our top priority.

 

Insomniac produces 10,000 concerts, club nights and festivals for seven million attendees annually across the globe. Since its inception, Insomniac's events have taken place in 13 countries across five continents. The company's premiere annual event, Electric Daisy Carnival Las Vegas, is the world’s largest dance music festival and attracts more than 525,000 fans over three days. The company was founded by Pasquale Rotella and has been based in Los Angeles since it was formed in 1993.

 

THE ROLE

Insomniac Events is looking for an Art Curator who can help find and commission artist sculptures, creative environments, and collaborate with the experience team to enhance each festival or concert while always in line with the individual brands.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES


  • Collaborate with the Director of Curation to develop a creative direction for each show that reflects Insomniac’s brand identity and the specific art direction of the event
  • Curate and propose artwork, installations, and experiences in alignment with the approved art direction
  • Initiate conversations with selected artists to explore feasibility, align vision, and develop initial concepts before handing over executional data to Art Ops Managers
  • Work within and manage allocated budgets, finding opportunities to maximize impact without compromising Insomniac’s art policy integrity
  • Ensure art curation timelines are maintained and that deadlines are communicated and met

Art Installation & Production Workflow


  • Develop and maintain detailed art decks that showcase proposed artists and installations for each event, and save all art decks in the art ops Google Drive
  • Present decks to internal producers and promoters for review, feedback, and approval
  • Coordinate with the production and finance teams to ensure the installation build aligns with production feasibility and financial constraints
  • Assist in translating conceptual art into real-time builds—this includes sourcing materials, identifying lighting needs, and brainstorming creative fabrication solutions
  • Collaborate with Art Ops Managers to ensure all artwork is engineered correctly, fabricated, and installed according to safety protocols and site limitations
  • Support artists with insomniac safety and building expectations by helping initiate technical, engineering, and safety discussions to ensure a smooth transition into the Insomniac building and engineering process

 

Art Ops Collaboration


  • Work closely with Art Ops Managers and the Art Ops Leads to conceptualize, and work closely with Art Ops Managers and the Art Ops Leads to and execute installations and custom art areas built by the Insomniac Art Ops team
  • Participate in budget development and scope planning for Art Ops-led builds
  • Assist in developing build schedules and help manage on-site installation timelines and workforce coordination
  • Be a reliable and energetic presence on-site during festival builds, ensuring that all curated and in-house installations are completed to Insomniac’s quality and safety standards
  • Troubleshoot challenges alongside the Art Ops team and provide feedback that balances creative ideas with logistical solutions

 Communication & Reporting

  • Maintain regular check-ins with the Director of Curation to ensure project alignment and report progress
  • Document conversations with artists and maintain clear records of scope, deliverables, and budget agreements

  • Act as a point of communication between creative and production teams during the early stages of project development
  • Notify appropriate team members of any risks, delays, or budget issues in a timely and manner

job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

 

Our commitment to inclusion and fairness
We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

 

The role

This is an opportunity for a UK-based financial journalist to cover a period of parental leave at the FT’s award-winning Lex opinion column.

At Lex we write views on companies and markets. No hot takes — only concise, deeply informed, analytical notes on big business, public and private markets and what makes finance tick.

We are looking for a numerate, naturally curious writer who wants to provoke debate with well-reported insights. The Lex column is central to the FT’s premium subscription strategy, and reaches an influential, engaged global audience.

Sector expertise is welcome, but we'll also want to see that you are an all-rounder. We’ll help you hone your ability to write punchy, directional and entertaining opinion.

 

What you will bring to the role

Analytical rigor: A strong grasp of corporate reporting, accounting, and the mechanics of M&A and earnings.

Conviction: The ability to generate clear, directional, and deeply reported views, backed up with numbers.

Intellectual agility: A fearless approach to untangling complex, unfamiliar topics.

Source management: A knack for conducting difficult, probing and diplomatic conversations with high-level sources.

Ambition: A drive to make a tangible impact, both in the market and within the FT newsroom.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Thursday 19th November 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. FT Newsroom staff are expected to work onsite a minimum of three days per week, subject to role requirements and regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for Editorial roles.

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

job.title: Product Manager
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

About the role

The FT app is an important part of how subscribers engage with FT journalism, and we believe there is a significant opportunity to go further. We're looking for an experienced Product Manager with a strong background in native and/or cross-platform mobile apps to play a central role in this transformation.

You'll join at a pivotal moment, working alongside our Principal Product Manager, engineering and design colleagues to turn our app strategy into reality, delivering improvements to the app experience and building the capabilities that will support its continued evolution.

This is an opportunity to shape a product used by a highly engaged global audience, while helping establish a stronger mobile product discipline within the FT.

What you'll be doing

Help shape the future of the FT app

  • Work with the Principal Product Manager to translate our long-term app strategy into clear product requirements, priorities and a deliverable roadmap.
  • Bring specialist mobile product knowledge and experience to decisions about the future app experience, challenging assumptions and finding opportunities to make better use of native device capabilities.
  • Develop a deep understanding of our customers, their behaviours and the moments in which they turn to the FT, using research, analytics and experimentation to see opportunities.
  • Champion a mobile-first approach to product development, ensuring we're designing around the needs of app customers and complementing their web experience.
  • Work across product teams to ensure the app delivers a coherent, premium experience that delivers meaningful value for the business, while making effective use of shared FT capabilities.

Deliver a distinctive, premium mobile experience

  • Own and prioritise defined areas of the app roadmap, balancing customer value, strategic impact, technical dependencies and commercial outcomes.
  • Work day-to-day with engineering, design, data and editorial colleagues to take initiatives from discovery through development, release and iteration.
  • Help deliver experiences that make the FT more essential to customers' daily routines, including better navigation, discovery, personalisation, notifications, offline experiences and continuity across devices.
  • Explore opportunities to make FT journalism more engaging and useful through native mobile interactions and seamless experiences across text, audio, video, data and other formats.
  • Collaborate with teams responsible for identity, subscriptions and customer lifecycle to make the app a more effective platform for acquisition, engagement, retention and subscriber growth.
  • Establish clear success measures, use experimentation and customer feedback to inform decisions, and continuously optimise the experience.
  • Ensure that performance, accessibility, reliability and usability are treated as fundamental parts of the product experience.

Build mobile product expertise within the FT

  • Act as a source of specialist mobile product knowledge for colleagues across product, design and engineering.
  • Share best practices in app product management, including platform conventions, app store requirements, release management, mobile analytics and experimentation.
  • Help establish effective ways of working for developing and maintaining high-quality iOS and Android experiences.
  • Stay informed about developments in mobile technology, customer expectations and emerging product capabilities, identifying opportunities relevant to the FT.

About you

Essential experience and skills

  • Proven mobile app product management experience: You have owned and delivered meaningful improvements to consumer-facing iOS and/or Android apps, ideally within products with significant scale, frequent usage or complex customer journeys.
  • Understanding of mobile technologies: You have practical experience working with native and/or cross-platform development teams and understand the differences, opportunities and trade-offs between architectures. You don't need to be an engineer, but you can engage in technical discussions and understand the product implications of architectural decisions.
  • Knowledge of the mobile ecosystem: You're familiar with Apple and Google's platform conventions, app store policies, submission and release processes, in-app purchases, push notifications, device capabilities and the considerations involved in delivering consistently high-quality app experiences.
  • Strong product management fundamentals: You're experienced in customer discovery, defining problems and opportunities, prioritisation, roadmap management, experimentation and measuring product outcomes.
  • Proven delivery experience: You've worked closely with cross-functional engineering and design teams to deliver products iteratively, navigate technical complexity and balance short-term improvements with longer-term investment.
  • Customer and commercial focus: You use qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand customer needs, make decisions and evaluate success. You understand how product experience contributes to engagement, retention and commercial performance.
  • Collaborative and influential: You're comfortable working across organisational boundaries, bringing different disciplines together and influencing decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: You can operate effectively while technology choices, team structures and delivery approaches are evolving, helping turn strategic ambition into practical action.

Desirable experience

  • Experience working on subscription-based digital products, particularly in publishing, media, content or other habit-forming consumer services.
  • Experience developing products that combine native and web-based capabilities.
  • Experience with personalisation, content discovery, notifications, offline functionality or other features that drive regular app engagement.
  • Experience working with external development partners while retaining internal product ownership.
  • Experience helping organisations establish or mature their mobile product development practices.

 

 

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available on the FT Careers website.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility
